options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

tools.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea – assessment, CPAP and driving
niceRefs: NICE NG202 Obstructive sleep apnoea/hypopnoea syndrome and obesity hypoventilation syndrome 2021
NICE CKS Obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome

options.label: Assessment and referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas/choking, unrefreshing sleep, excessive daytime sleepiness (Epworth ≥11), morning headache, nocturia, resistant hypertension, AF, type 2 diabetes, obesity (BMI ≥35), large neck (>17 in/43 cm men), retrognathia, Down's syndrome, acromegaly, hypothyroidism, pregnancy. STOP-Bang ≥3 = at risk (≥5 high). Children: snoring + behaviour/growth/enuresis → ENT (adenotonsillectomy).
2. Check: BP, BMI/neck circumference, Epworth Sleepiness Scale, TFT, HbA1c, FBC (polycythaemia), oxygen saturation (daytime <94% or bicarbonate >27 suggests obesity hypoventilation — urgent referral), ECG; examine airway (Mallampati).
3. NG202: refer sleep service (respiratory/ENT) for home sleep study (respiratory polygraphy/oximetry) — URGENT (within 4 weeks) if: vocational driver (HGV/PCV/taxi), safety-critical job (pilot, machinery), Epworth ≥16/excessive sleepiness with risk, unstable cardiovascular disease, pregnancy, pre-operative, obesity hypoventilation (daytime hypercapnia/hypoxia), or falls asleep driving. Pre-referral: advise not to drive if sleepy.

options.label: Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. All: weight loss (≥10% improves AHI; consider tier 3 weight management/GLP-1 — tirzepatide licensed for OSA in obesity 2025; bariatric surgery), stop smoking, reduce alcohol (especially evening), avoid sedatives/opioids/benzodiazepines, side-sleeping (positional therapy/tennis-ball), treat nasal obstruction (intranasal steroid), sleep hygiene/regular hours.
2. Mild OSA (AHI 5–14) with symptoms: lifestyle ± mandibular advancement splint (custom, via dentist/sleep service) or CPAP if symptomatic/wants; moderate–severe (AHI ≥15): CPAP first line (fixed or auto-titrating with humidification; telemonitoring; mask fitting support — adherence ≥4 h/night on ≥70% nights; manage nasal symptoms, claustrophobia, pressure intolerance); MAS if CPAP declined/not tolerated; hypoglossal nerve stimulation (NICE IPG598) or upper airway surgery selected cases via ENT. Obesity hypoventilation: CPAP or NIV + weight management; avoid oxygen alone.
3. Follow-up: sleep service annual review (download compliance, Epworth); GP — BP control (OSA causes resistant hypertension; CPAP lowers BP modestly), CVD risk, driving reassessment, pre-operative notification (anaesthetic risk), review sedatives; CPAP in all patients with AF ablation/cardiac surgery planning.

options.label: Driving and occupational rules
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVLA: patients with suspected/confirmed OSA with EXCESSIVE SLEEPINESS must not drive and must notify DVLA (Group 1 cars; Group 2 lorries/buses — stricter). Moderate/severe OSAS: must notify; may resume when symptoms controlled on treatment (CPAP compliance confirmed by specialist, usually within 4 weeks), Group 2 needs annual specialist review. Mild OSA without sleepiness: no need to notify. Advise in writing and document; GP has GMC duty to inform DVLA if patient continues to drive against advice.
2. Occupational: safety-critical roles — inform occupational health; HGV/PCV licence reviewed with treatment evidence; shift work worsens.
3. Patient advice: no driving when sleepy, avoid long drives/night driving until treated, Sleep Apnoea Trust (SATA); family — CPAP adherence support.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

options.label: Pleural effusion — assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breathlessness, dull chest ache, stony-dull percussion, reduced breath sounds/vocal resonance; CXR shows blunted costophrenic angle (>200 mL) — PA + lateral; USS more sensitive. Unilateral effusion in adult = needs diagnosis (BTS 2023: urgent respiratory/pleural clinic referral — 2WW if cancer suspected: smoker, weight loss, age >40, asbestos exposure).
2. Bilateral effusions with heart failure/cirrhosis/nephrotic syndrome/hypoalbuminaemia → treat cause (diuretics; BNP, LFT, albumin, U&E, urine ACR, TFT); aspirate only if atypical (fever, chest pain, unilateral, not resolving with treatment).
3. Pleural aspiration (secondary care, USS-guided): Light's criteria — exudate if pleural:serum protein >0.5, LDH >0.6, or pleural LDH >2/3 upper limit; send protein, LDH, pH, glucose, cytology, microbiology (incl. AFB), differential cell count. Exudate causes: malignancy (lung, breast, mesothelioma, lymphoma), parapneumonic/empyema (pH <7.2 → chest drain), TB, PE, pancreatitis, RA/SLE, drugs (methotrexate, amiodarone), post-cardiac injury, chylothorax.

options.label: Pleural effusion — management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Parapneumonic/empyema: admit — antibiotics (co-amoxiclav or per culture, 2–6 weeks), chest drain if pH <7.2/pus/loculated; intrapleural tPA/DNase; surgery (VATS) if failure.
2. Malignant effusion (specialist): therapeutic aspiration for symptoms; definitive — indwelling pleural catheter (IPC, home drainage, hospice-compatible) or talc pleurodesis (slurry via drain or thoracoscopic); treat primary (chemotherapy/targeted); mesothelioma — pleural MDT, compensation (Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit, Diffuse Mesothelioma Payment Scheme — notify, Mesothelioma UK).
3. GP role: breathlessness management (fan, positioning, opioids in palliative setting), recognise re-accumulation (repeat CXR/USS if symptoms return), IPC care via community nurses, anticipatory care planning; ensure safety-netting for drain site infection. TB effusion: standard 6-month anti-TB therapy (TB team).

options.label: Pneumothorax
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sudden pleuritic chest pain + breathlessness; reduced breath sounds, hyper-resonance; tall thin young men (primary spontaneous), COPD/asthma/ILD/CF (secondary), trauma, iatrogenic; TENSION (hypotension, tracheal deviation, distended neck veins, severe distress) → 999, needle decompression (2nd intercostal space mid-clavicular, or 4th/5th anterior axillary) by trained clinician, high-flow oxygen.
2. Any suspected pneumothorax → same-day ED for CXR. BTS 2023 (adult, non-tension): minimal symptoms → conservative (ambulatory) regardless of size; symptomatic — high-risk features (secondary, >50 with smoking history, hypoxia, haemopneumothorax, bilateral) → chest drain; otherwise ambulatory device (Rocket pleural vent) or needle aspiration or conservative by patient preference; review 2–4 days, CXR follow-up until resolved.
3. After: no flying until 7 days after CXR confirms resolution (CAA/BTS), NO scuba diving ever (unless bilateral pleurectomy), stop smoking (recurrence risk), avoid heavy exertion 2–4 weeks; recurrence 30–50% → thoracic surgery (VATS pleurodesis/bullectomy) after second ipsilateral episode, first contralateral, or high-risk occupation (pilot, diver).

options.label: Low Risk (Score 0-1)
options.guidance:

1. Treatment: Amoxicillin 500mg tds for 5 days. 
2. Allergic: Doxycycline 200mg day 1 then 100mg OD, or Clarithromycin 500mg bd.
3. Note: Do not use dual antibiotics for low-risk CAP. NICE NG138.

options.label: Moderate / High Risk (Score ≥ 2)

2. Dual Antibiotics (Moderate): Amoxicillin + Clarithromycin.
3. High Severity: Co-amoxiclav + Clarithromycin (usually IV in hospital). NICE NG138.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer TB service. Diagnosis: FNA or biopsy; culture. Treat per NICE NG33 (RIPE). Screen contacts.
2. NICE NG33, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Notify public health. Macrolide (e.g. azithromycin) if <21 days of cough to reduce spread; may not change course. Supportive for paroxysms.
2. Refer if infant <6 months, severe paroxysms, or complications. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Mastoiditis (postauricular swelling, protrusion), facial palsy, intracranial complications, recurrent AOM (≥3 in 6 months or ≥4 in 12 months). Consider grommets. NICE NG91.

options.label: Consultant Treatment Philosophy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Goal**: Not 'normalcy', but 'functional alignment'. 
2. **Multimodal**: Medication (Stimulants) + Executive Function Coaching + Social adjustment.
3. **Biological**: Correcting fronto-striatal dopaminergic deficit. Medication provides the 'brakes' for the brain.
4. **Psycho-Social**: Reducing the 'shame cycle' associated with executive dysfunction. Occupational/Educational adjustments (reasonable adjustments) are essential.

options.label: Clinical Criteria
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DSM-5: 6/9 symptoms of Inattention and/or Hyperactivity-Impulsivity (5/9 for adults) in ≥2 settings, present before age 12.
2. ICD-11 (6A05): Persistent pattern (≥6 months) of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity across settings.

options.label: Referral Pathway
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Child: Refer to Community Paediatrics or CAMHS.
2. Adult: Specialist ADHD service referral. Document impact on work, relationships, and driving safety. NICE NG87.

options.label: Lisdexamfetamine (Elvanse)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line for adults. Prodrug (decreased abuse potential).
2. Dose: 30mg-70mg. 
3. Side effects: Insomnia, increased BP, appetite suppression.

options.label: Methylphenidate (Choice of IR/ER)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line for children/young people. 
2. Brands: **Conserta XL** (22% IR/78% ER) or **Medikinet XL** (50% IR/50% ER). 
3. Shared Care: GP takes over prescribing only after stabilization (usually 3 months) under Specialist Protocol.

options.label: Non-Stimulants (Atomoxetine)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice if stimulants contraindicated or high risk of diversion/misuse.
2. Warning: Rare risk of severe liver injury and suicidal ideation.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History and exclusion diet or IgE/skin test as appropriate. Avoid allergen; adrenaline auto-injector if anaphylaxis risk.
2. Refer if severe reaction, multiple allergies, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CG116, CKS.

options.label: IM Adrenaline (999)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Adrenaline 1:1000 IM (anterolateral mid-thigh). Adult: 500mcg (0.5ml). Child 6-12: 300mcg. Child <6: 150mcg. Repeat every 5 mins if no improvement. High-flow O2. NICE NG193.

options.label: Step 1: SABA prn
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Symptoms < 3 times/week and no night-waking.
2. Warning: If using SABA ≥3 times/week, move to Step 2. BTS/SIGN Guidelines.

options.label: Step 2: Low-dose ICS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Beclometasone (e.g. Clenil 100mcg bd). Prevents airway remodelling and reduces exacerbation risk. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Step 3: Add LABA (Combined Inhaler)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: ICS + LABA (e.g. Fostair or Symbicort). MART (Maintenance and Reliever Therapy) is the specialist preference for improved adherence.
2. Review: If still poorly controlled on moderate-dose ICS+LABA, consider LTRA (Montelukast). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Moderate (PEFR 50-75% best)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treatment: SABA 2-5 puffs via spacer every 10-20 mins. Oral Prednisolone 40-50mg for 5 days. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Severe (PEFR 33-50% / RR ≥ 25 / HR ≥ 110)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Immediate hospital admission (999). High-flow Oxygen. Nebulised SABA + Ipratropium. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Life-Threatening (PEFR <33% / SpO2 <92% / Silent Chest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999. Do not delay. Life-threatening features (33-92-CHEST). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Step 1: SABA prn
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Symptoms < 3 times/week and no night-waking.
2. Warning: If using SABA ≥3 times/week, move to Step 2. BTS/SIGN Guidelines.

options.label: Step 2: Low-dose ICS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Beclometasone (e.g. Clenil 100mcg bd). Prevents airway remodelling and reduces exacerbation risk. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Step 3: Add LABA (Combined Inhaler)
options.guidance:

2. Review: If still poorly controlled on moderate-dose ICS+LABA, consider LTRA (Montelukast). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Moderate (PEFR 50-75% best)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treatment: SABA 2-5 puffs via spacer every 10-20 mins. Oral Prednisolone 40-50mg for 5 days. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Severe (PEFR 33-50% / RR ≥ 25 / HR ≥ 110)
options.guidance:

1. Triage: Immediate hospital admission (999). High-flow Oxygen. Nebulised SABA + Ipratropium. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Life-Threatening (PEFR <33% / SpO2 <92% / Silent Chest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999. Do not delay. Life-threatening features (33-92-CHEST). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emollients; topical steroid for eczema flares. Step up if uncontrolled. Consider allergy testing if food/trigger suspected.
2. Refer if severe eczema, failure of topical therapy, or need for systemic. NICE NG80, CKS.

options.label: Consultant Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Ethos**: Transition from a 'medical model' (fixing deficits) to a 'social model' (adjusting environment).
2. **Co-morbidity**: High rates of ADHD, Anxiety, and Dyspraxia. Always screen for co-occurring conditions.
3. **Biological**: Meds have NO role in core ASD features. Used only for co-morbidities (e.g. Melatonin for sleep, SSRIs for OCD).
4. **Social**: Educational (EHCP) and Workplace adjustments are the primary interventions.

options.label: Child/Young Person
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Local multi-agency ASD pathway (Paediatrics/CAMHS).
2. Screening: SCQ (Social Communication Questionnaire). 
3. Assessment: ADOS and ADI-R (Gold standard tools).

options.label: Adult suspected ASD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Screening: **AQ-10** (Score ≥6 = Refer).
2. Referral: Specialist diagnostic assessment only if significant impact on social/working life. NICE CG142.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Parenting strategies; behavioural interventions. Rule out ADHD, anxiety, learning difficulty.
2. Refer if severe, family crisis, or suspected conduct disorder. NICE NG158, CKS.

options.label: Safe for Home
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCPCH):
1. Hydration: Ensure ≥ 50-75% normal fluid intake. Check for ≥2 wet nappies in 12h.
2. Admission: Refer if SpO2 < 92% (in air), RR > 70, or apnea reported.
3. No Meds: Do not use inhalers, steroids, or antibiotics. NICE NG9 / RCPCH.

options.label: Refer to Hospital
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: RR > 70, saturations < 92%, apnoeas, or persistent reduced feeding (<50%).
2. Action: Urgent Paediatric referral. NICE NG9.

options.label: Safe for Home
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCPCH):
1. Hydration: Ensure ≥ 50-75% normal fluid intake. Check for ≥2 wet nappies in 12h.
2. Admission: Refer if SpO2 < 92% (in air), RR > 70, or apnea reported.
3. No Meds: Do not use inhalers, steroids, or antibiotics. NICE NG9 / RCPCH.

options.label: Refer to Hospital
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: RR > 70, saturations < 92%, apnoeas, or persistent reduced feeding (<50%).
2. Action: Urgent Paediatric referral. NICE NG9.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: paracetamol (avoid ibuprofen); calamine; keep cool. Isolate until lesions crusted.
2. Refer: Immunocompromised, neonatal, pregnant contact, complications (encephalitis, pneumonia, bacterial sepsis). Aciclovir if high risk. NICE CKS.

options.label: Women – uncomplicated cystitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. MSU: Send if recurrent, pregnant, or pyelonephritis suspected; otherwise can treat empirically. First-line: nitrofurantoin 100 mg MR bd 3 days, OR trimethoprim 200 mg bd 3 days (check local resistance). Avoid nitrofurantoin if eGFR <45. Alternative: pivmecillinam 400 mg tds 3 days.
2. If pregnant: MSU; treat 7 days; avoid trimethoprim in first trimester (folate). NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Men / pyelonephritis / recurrent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Men: MSU; treat 7 days (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim). Consider prostatitis if tender prostate; longer course.
2. Pyelonephritis: MSU + bloods; consider admission if systemically unwell. Oral: cefalexin or co-amoxiclav 7–10 days (per local resistance).
3. Recurrent: MSU when symptomatic; consider prophylaxis (e.g. nitrofurantoin at night) or referral. NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Catheter / pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Catheter: Only treat if symptomatic; MSU from catheter; replace catheter if long-term. Consider prophylaxis only if recurrent and symptomatic.
2. Pregnancy: MSU; 7-day course; avoid trimethoprim first trimester. Follow up MSU.
3. Refer: Pyelonephritis not improving; recurrent UTI; structural abnormality; children. 2WW if visible haematuria. NICE NG109, NG12.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Increase fibre, fluids, activity. Consider bulk-forming (e.g. ispaghula). NICE NG99.

options.label: Osmotic / stimulant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Osmotic: macrogol. Stimulant: senna or bisacodyl short-term. Avoid long-term stimulant. NICE NG99.

options.label: Refractory / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refractory: Consider prucalopride if chronic and laxatives failed. Exclude obstruction, hypothyroid, drugs.
2. Refer: Red flags (weight loss, rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit), suspected malignancy. NICE NG99, NG12.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Circumcision: Not routinely recommended for physiological phimosis (resolves with time). If pathological phimosis or parental request after discussion: refer to paediatric surgery/urology.
2. Phimosis: Topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.05% once daily for 4–8 weeks) if ballooning or infection; refer if failed or scarring. NICE CKS.
3. Hypospadias: Refer to paediatric urology (surgical correction). Do not circumcise before referral. NICE NG11, NG111, CKS.

options.label: Workup (BSG Guidelines)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bloods: IgA-TtG (Tissue Transglutaminase) AND Total IgA level (to exclude IgA deficiency). Must be on gluten-containing diet (1 meal/day for 6 weeks).
2. Referral: Refer to GI if TtG positive.
3. Non-Biopsy Pathway: In select cases (TtG > 10x normal), a second sample (EMA) may allow diagnosis without biopsy in adults (specialist decision). NICE NG20, CKS.

options.label: Follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Usually shared care with cardiology. Monitor growth, saturations, medication. Endocarditis prophylaxis per NICE NG64. NICE CKS.

options.label: Follow-up
options.guidance:

1. Usually shared care with cardiology. Monitor growth, saturations, medication. Endocarditis prophylaxis per NICE NG64. NICE CKS.

options.label: Diagnosis & exclusion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breastfed: Maternal exclusion of cow's milk (and egg if suspected).
2. Formula-fed: Trial extensively hydrolysed formula (EHF) for 2–4 weeks. If IgE-mediated, consider skin prick/sIgE.
3. Reintroduction: Supervised challenge to confirm. NICE CG116, BSACI.

options.label: First-line formula
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-IgE / delayed: EHF (e.g. Nutramigen, Aptamil Pepti).
2. IgE-mediated / anaphylaxis: EHF or amino-acid formula (AAF e.g. Neocate) if EHF not tolerated.
3. Avoid: Soya under 6 months; rice formula not first-line. NICE CG116.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dietitian: If multiple exclusions, faltering growth, or weaning advice.
2. Paediatric allergy: Anaphylaxis, diagnostic uncertainty, or need for AAF. NICE CG116.

options.label: Mild (Croupy cough, no stridor at rest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCPCH):
1. Treatment: Single dose of Dexamethasone (0.15 mg/kg) - can use soluble tablets (e.g. 500mcg/tablet) mixed in water.
2. Note: All children with croup should receive a steroid dose as it reduces future severity.
3. Safety-net: Return if stridor at rest or increased work of breathing.

options.label: Moderate / Severe (Stridor at rest / Recession)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Immediate hospital referral (A&E). Avoid upsetting the child (no tongue depressors).
2. Treatment: High-flow Oxygen if SpO2 < 92%; Nebulised Adrenaline 5ml 1:1000 (specialist initiation). RCPCH.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Newborn blood spot includes CF screening. If positive/screen positive: refer for sweat test and genetics.
2. Support family; ensure follow-up at CF centre. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess: bone age, FSH/LH, oestradiol/testosterone, prolactin. Exclude chronic disease, underweight.
2. Refer paediatric endocrinology if no signs by 14 (boys) or 13 (girls), or constitutional delay needing support. NICE CKS.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

options.label: Referral & support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer community paediatrics or child development team. Consider hearing/vision, genetic if dysmorphism.
2. Early intervention and family support. Safeguarding if neglect suspected. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Referral & support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer community paediatrics or child development team. Consider hearing/vision, genetic if dysmorphism.
2. Early intervention and family support. Safeguarding if neglect suspected. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess reading/spelling; exclude vision/hearing. Educational support and reasonable adjustments.
2. Refer for formal assessment if needed for exam access or EHCP. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mild potency (body)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Mild eczema on body: Use mild potency – e.g. hydrocortisone 0.1–1%, 2.5%. Apply once daily to affected area until clear (review by 2 weeks).
2. Emollient first; steroid for flares. Step down when controlled. NICE CKS.

options.label: Moderate potency (body)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Moderate eczema on body: Moderately potent – e.g. clobetasone 0.05% (Eumovate), betamethasone valerate 0.025% (Betnovate-RD). Once daily until clear; review by 2 weeks.
2. Avoid long-term continuous use. NICE CKS.

options.label: Potent / very potent (body only)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Severe eczema on body: Potent – e.g. betamethasone valerate 0.1% (Betnovate), betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%. Very potent (short courses only): clobetasol 0.05% (Dermovate).
2. Do not use potent/very potent on face, flexures, or genitals. Review within 2 weeks; limit duration. NICE CKS.

options.label: Face, flexures, genitals
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use mild potency only (e.g. hydrocortisone 0.5–1%). If insufficient, moderate potency for max 5 days. Never use potent/very potent on these sites (atrophy risk).
2. Consider tacrolimus or pimecrolimus for face/neck if steroid-sparing needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: Tacrolimus & pimecrolimus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Second-line only: when adequate topical steroid would cause unacceptable risk (e.g. skin atrophy), or for face/neck in moderate–severe eczema. Not first-line; not for mild eczema. NICE TA82.
2. Tacrolimus 0.03% (child 2–15) or 0.1% (adult); pimecrolimus 1% (face/neck, child 2–16, moderate). Apply twice daily until clear; can use for maintenance. Warn initial burning/itching. Avoid in immunocompromised; sun protection. NICE CKS.

options.label: Paediatric (same principles)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Match potency to severity and site. Face/flexures: mild only; limit duration. Emollients first-line.
2. Tacrolimus: licensed from 2 years. Pimecrolimus: face/neck, 2–16 years, moderate eczema. Use under dermatology or experienced prescriber if initiating calcineurin inhibitor. NICE CKS, NG80.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat constipation first: macrogol; adequate fluid/fibre; toileting routine. Disimpaction if faecal loading.
2. Refer if treatment failure, soiling with no constipation, or behavioural/psychological concerns. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: stridor, drooling, toxic. Do not examine throat. 999; senior anaesthetics/ENT. Keep child calm; oxygen if needed.
2. Now rare (HiB vaccine). IV antibiotics after secure airway. NICE CKS.

options.label: First Seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Urgency: Refer to 'First Seizure Clinic' (within 2 weeks). NICE NG217.
2. Investigation: EEG + MRI Brain (Standard protocol including coronal T2/FLAIR sessions). 
3. Safety: High-risk activities (driving, swimming, working at heights) must stop until specialist review.

options.label: Focal Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Lamotrigine or Levetiracetam (Keppra). NICE NG217.

options.label: Generalized Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Sodium Valproate (Epilim) - **Strict warning: Not for use in women/girls of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place.**
2. Alternative: Levetiracetam or Lamotrigine.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; rule out illness (red flags). Support parents; responsive feeding. Trial of reduced-allergen formula or maternal diet exclusion only if cow's milk allergy suspected. Do not recommend simethicone or herbal remedies as evidence poor.
2. CKS Infantile colic.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Plot weight/height on centile charts; assess intake, swallowing, reflux, red flags (cardiac, neuro).
2. Dietitian if weaning/feeding advice; refer paediatrician if significant faltering or organic concern. NICE NG75, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance: most simple febrile seizures are benign. Antipyretics for comfort only (do not prevent recurrence).
2. Refer if complex, prolonged (>15 min), focal, or recurrent in same illness. Exclude meningitis. NICE NG143, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; antipyretics for comfort. Exclude meningitis (red flags). Most simple febrile seizures don't need EEG or imaging.
2. Refer if complex, prolonged, or parental concern. NICE NG143, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; antipyretics for comfort. Exclude meningitis (red flags). Most simple febrile seizures don't need EEG or imaging.
2. Refer if complex, prolonged, or parental concern. NICE NG143, CKS.

options.label: Green (Low Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

options.label: Amber (Intermediate Risk)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.label: Red (High Risk / Sepsis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

options.label: Green (Low Risk)
options.guidance:

1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.guidance:

1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.guidance:

1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

options.guidance:

1. Management: Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for distress (not for fever alone).
2. Hydration: Encourage fluids. Check for rash.
3. Safety-net: Advise on amber/red signs. NICE NG143.

1. Assessment: Check for focus (ears, urine, chest). Consider urine dip.
2. Disposition: Refer if no focus or clinical concern. NICE NG143.

options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, status epilepticus, or RR > 60.
2. Action: Emergency 999 Admission. NICE NG143.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History and exclusion diet or IgE/skin test as appropriate. Avoid allergen; adrenaline auto-injector if anaphylaxis risk.
2. Refer if severe reaction, multiple allergies, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CG116, CKS.

options.label: Uninvestigated Dyspepsia / GORD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle: Weight loss, stop smoking, avoid late meals/triggers.
2. Medication: PPI (e.g. Omeprazole 20mg or Lansoprazole 30mg) for 4 weeks.
3. H. pylori: Test (stool/breath) and treat if positive. NICE CG184.

options.label: Refractory Symptoms
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review: Check compliance and timing (30-60m before food).
2. Dose: Increase PPI to twice daily or switch PPI.
3. Referral: Consider referral for endoscopy if symptoms persist despite high-dose PPI. NICE CG184.

options.label: Urgent Referral (2WW)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dysphagia: Any age with difficulty swallowing.
2. Weight Loss: Age ≥55 with weight loss AND (dyspepsia OR reflux).
3. Action: Refer via 2WW pathway. NICE NG12.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Plot height/weight on centiles; assess growth velocity. Exclude chronic disease, hypothyroidism.
2. Refer if height <0.4th centile, growth velocity poor, or delayed puberty. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: fluids, paracetamol/ibuprofen for discomfort. Usually self-limiting.
2. Refer if dehydration, meningism, or immunocompromised. NICE CKS.

options.label: Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Head lice: wet combing or dimeticone/lotion (check resistance). Two applications 7 days apart. Pubic lice: permethrin or malathion; treat contacts.
2. NICE CKS.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Most cases self-limiting: supportive care, rest until symptoms resolve. Analgesia (paracetamol/ibuprofen) for joint/abdominal pain.
2. Monitor: BP, urinalysis (blood/protein), serum creatinine and electrolytes. Repeat urine at 1–2 weeks and after resolution (risk of nephritis).
3. Refer: Nephritis, severe abdominal pain, GI bleed, orchitis, or organ-threatening disease. Urgent if unwell or renal impairment. NICE CKS.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Circumcision: Not routinely recommended for physiological phimosis (resolves with time). If pathological phimosis or parental request after discussion: refer to paediatric surgery/urology.
2. Phimosis: Topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.05% once daily for 4–8 weeks) if ballooning or infection; refer if failed or scarring. NICE CKS.
3. Hypospadias: Refer to paediatric urology (surgical correction). Do not circumcise before referral. NICE NG11, NG111, CKS.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

options.label: IBD / colitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IBD: refer; maintain on treatment per specialist. Microscopic colitis: consider budesonide. Rectal bleeding: FIT, sigmoidoscopy/colonoscopy per pathway.
2. NICE NG129, NG12.

options.label: Liver / rare
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Autoimmune hepatitis/PBC/PSC: refer hepatology. Haemochromatosis: venesection. Wilson's: refer. Gastroparesis: diet, prokinetic; refer. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use Green Book schedule; give at minimum intervals (4 weeks for inactivated; no need to restart). MMR, pre-school booster, HPV, MenACWY as per schedule.
2. Refer to immunisation clinic if complex or travel. NICE CKS, Green Book.

options.label: Localised (Non-bullous)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: Hydrogen peroxide 1% cream (Crystacide) for 5 days.
2. Alternative: Topical fusidic acid 2% tds for 5 days (if peroxide unsuitable).
3. Hygiene: Crusts can be gently soaked off with warm water. NICE CKS.

options.label: Widespread or Bullous
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Oral Antibiotics: Flucloxacillin 500mg qds for 5 days (clarithromycin if allergic).
2. Bullous: Always use oral antibiotics as it is usually staphylococcal.
3. Hygiene: Handwashing, separate towels, avoid scratching. NICE CKS.

options.label: Exclusion / Contagion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. School/Work: Exclude until lesions are crusted and healed, OR 48 hours after starting antibiotics.
2. Recurrence: Consider nasal swab (MRSA?) and skin de-colonization. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Improving consultations for children with additional needs – Management

steps.question: Consultations for children with additional needs

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider communication needs, sensory environment, reasonable adjustments. Involve family and carers.
2. Use clear language; allow time; avoid assumptions. NICE NG76, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Signpost to local SEND and family support. Coordinate with education and social care where appropriate. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; rule out illness (red flags). Support parents; responsive feeding. Trial of reduced-allergen formula or maternal diet exclusion only if cow's milk allergy suspected. Do not recommend simethicone or herbal remedies as evidence poor.
2. CKS Infantile colic.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use NICE threshold graphs (gestational age, hours of life). Phototherapy or exchange if above threshold.
2. Refer if conjugated jaundice, prolonged, or unwell. Check TFTs if prolonged. NICE CG98, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: persistent joint swelling, morning stiffness, limp. Urgent paediatric rheumatology referral. NSAIDs for symptom relief.
2. DMARDs/biologics as per paediatric rheumatology. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: fever ≥5 days + rash, conjunctivitis, cracked lips, lymph nodes, palm/sole changes. Urgent paediatric referral.
2. IVIG + aspirin to reduce coronary aneurysm risk. Echocardiography. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: fever ≥5 days + rash, conjunctivitis, cracked lips, lymph nodes, palm/sole changes. Urgent paediatric referral.
2. IVIG + aspirin to reduce coronary aneurysm risk. Echocardiography. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Septic arthritis/osteomyelitis: emergency referral. Do not delay for imaging. Bloods (FBC, CRP), blood culture if febrile.
2. Transient synovitis: supportive; review if not improving. NICE NG143, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive; notify public health. Vitamin A in areas of deficiency or severe disease.
2. Refer if complications: encephalitis, pneumonia, severe dehydration. MMR for prevention. NICE CKS.

options.label: Fever + non-blanching rash
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Treat as meningococcal disease until proved otherwise. Immediate parenteral antibiotic (ceftriaxone or benzylpenicillin). Emergency admission. NICE NG51.

options.label: No fever, well child
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider ITP, HSP. FBC, clotting. Refer paediatrics if unwell or platelets <20. NICE CKS.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

options.label: Self-limiting
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Usually resolve in 6–18 months. Reassurance; avoid squeezing. Consider topical (e.g. potassium hydroxide) or referral if extensive/facial. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: analgesia, fluids. Notify public health. Avoid contact with non-immune.
2. Refer if meningoencephalitis, orchitis (supportive + consider analgesia), pancreatitis. MMR for prevention. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Innocent murmur: soft, systolic, varies with position, no other signs. Reassure; no echo needed.
2. Refer if symptomatic, diastolic, harsh, or uncertain. Echo for suspected structural. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Barrier cream (e.g. zinc); frequent nappy changes; air time. If candida (satellite lesions): add topical antifungal (e.g. clotrimazole).
2. Refer if severe, infected, or not improving. NICE CKS.

options.label: Low Risk (Green)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting and follow-up. Provide written instructions on when to seek help. NICE NG51.

options.label: High Risk (Amber/Red)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
999 Ambulance. NEWS2 score calculation. ABCDE assessment. O2 to target 94-98%. IV access. Pre-hospital antibiotics if >1h from hospital. NICE NG51.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nocturnal: Enuresis alarm first-line; desmopressin if alarm not suitable or for short-term (e.g. sleepover). Reward systems.
2. Daytime wetting: Exclude UTI/constipation; bladder diary; timed voiding. Refer if persistent or red flags. NICE NG111, CKS.

options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance: self-limiting; resolves when growth plate fuses. Rest from aggravating activity; ice after sport; simple analgesia.
2. Physiotherapy: quadriceps stretching and strengthening. Consider patellar strap.
3. Refer if diagnostic uncertainty, severe pain, or bilateral with systemic features. NICE CKS.

options.label: Soft tissue / tendon
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rest, ice, analgesia; physio. Plantar fasciitis: stretch, orthotics. Tennis elbow: eccentric exercises. Rotator cuff: physio; consider subacromial injection. De Quervain's: splint, NSAID; steroid injection first dorsal compartment – see 'De Quervain's – injection' pathway. NICE CKS, NG124.

options.label: Joint / arthritis / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GCA: urgent high-dose steroid; same-day rheumatology. Polymyalgia: steroid; monitor. Pseudogout: NSAID. Septic arthritis: emergency referral – do not delay. Hot swollen joint: aspirate (MC&S), admit. NICE NG210, NG100.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Septic arthritis, GCA, cord compression, acute compartment syndrome. Routine: Persistent despite conservative treatment; diagnostic uncertainty; need for surgery or specialist injection. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mild, no systemic illness
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting; paracetamol/ibuprofen. Most resolve in 3 days. No antibiotic first-line. NICE NG91.

options.label: Systemically unwell or high risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Amoxicillin 5–7 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergic). Consider if <2 years bilateral, or otorrhoea. NICE NG91.

options.label: When to refer / complications
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Mastoiditis (postauricular swelling, protrusion), facial palsy, intracranial complications, recurrent AOM (≥3 in 6 months or ≥4 in 12 months). Consider grommets. NICE NG91.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History: timing, IgE vs non-IgE. Consider SPT/sIgE if IgE-mediated. Trial exclusion for non-IgE.
2. Refer if anaphylaxis, multiple foods, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CG116.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Most viral rashes: supportive. Exclude meningococcal (non-blanching, unwell), Kawasaki, HSP.
2. Safety-net: Traffic light (NG143). Refer if non-blanching, fever + unwell, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG143, CKS.

tools.title: Paediatrics – gastroenteritis, limp, scarlet fever, inguinal hernia, TB contact, anxiety

options.label: Gastroenteritis and dehydration
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess hydration (CG84): red flags — altered consciousness, sunken eyes, tachycardia/tachypnoea, reduced skin turgor, cold extremities, prolonged CRT, hypotension (shock). Risk: <1 year (esp. <6 months), low birth weight, ≥6 stools or ≥3 vomits in 24 h, unable to tolerate fluids, stopped breastfeeding, malnourished.
2. No dehydration: continue breast/formula/normal diet, extra fluids, offer ORS (Dioralyte) 5 mL/kg after each loose stool if at risk; avoid fruit juice/fizzy drinks. Clinical dehydration: ORS 50 mL/kg over 4 h PLUS maintenance, little and often (syringe/spoon 5 mL every 1–2 min); continue breastfeeding; NG tube/admit if refusing or vomiting persistently; shock → 999/IV fluids.
3. Drugs: no antidiarrhoeals in children; ondansetron 0.15 mg/kg single oral dose (off-label, often used in ED) can enable oral rehydration; antibiotics only for specific pathogens (Salmonella <6 months/immunocompromised, Shigella, Campylobacter severe, C. difficile, giardia) — stool culture if blood/mucus, recent travel, immunocompromised, >7 days, or outbreak.
4. Safety-net: diarrhoea usually 5–7 days (stops by 2 weeks), vomiting 1–2 days (stops by 3 days); return if signs of dehydration, blood in stool, bilious vomiting, severe abdominal pain, fever persisting. Exclusion from school/nursery 48 h after last episode; no swimming 2 weeks; hand hygiene; notify if outbreak/E. coli O157/bloody diarrhoea. Post-gastroenteritis lactose intolerance — temporary.

options.label: Limping child
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SAME DAY referral (paediatrics/orthopaedics): any limp with fever or unwell (septic arthritis/osteomyelitis — Kocher: non-weight-bearing, temp >38.5, ESR >40, WCC >12), non-weight-bearing, limp in child <3 years, pain at rest/night, history of trauma with inability to weight bear, suspected non-accidental injury, limp >1 week without diagnosis, systemic signs (weight loss, bruising, pallor — leukaemia).
2. Transient synovitis (irritable hip): 3–10 years, after viral URTI, mild limp, afebrile/low-grade, can weight-bear, well — if Kocher criteria 0 and bloods normal (FBC, CRP/ESR): ibuprofen, rest, review 48 h and at 1 week; USS shows effusion; must resolve within 1–2 weeks — if not, re-refer (Perthes).
3. Perthes disease: 4–8 years, boys, insidious limp, hip/knee pain, restricted abduction/internal rotation → X-ray AP + frog-lateral (may be normal early → MRI), orthopaedic referral (urgent). SUFE: 10–16 years, often overweight, hip/knee/thigh pain, externally rotated leg, loss of internal rotation → SAME-DAY orthopaedics, non-weight-bearing (frog-lateral X-ray — never miss; bilateral in 20–40%). Also: DDH in toddlers (Trendelenburg gait, leg-length discrepancy — X-ray after 6 months), JIA (morning stiffness, swelling — rheumatology), reactive arthritis, malignancy (osteosarcoma/Ewing's — night pain, mass → 2WW/X-ray within 48 h per NG12), discitis, psoas abscess, appendicitis, testicular torsion (examine).

options.label: Scarlet fever, inguinal hernia, TB, anxiety
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Scarlet fever (group A strep): sandpaper rash starting trunk, flushed cheeks with perioral sparing, strawberry tongue, fever, sore throat; Centor/FeverPAIN. Treat ALL suspected cases: phenoxymethylpenicillin — 1–11 months 62.5 mg qds, 1–5 years 125 mg qds, 6–11 years 250 mg qds, ≥12 years 500 mg qds for 10 days (UKHSA 2023: amoxicillin liquid acceptable if penicillin V unavailable; clarithromycin if allergic). NOTIFIABLE — notify UKHSA. Exclude from school until 24 h of antibiotics. Safety-net: invasive GAS (iGAS) signs — drowsiness, breathing difficulty, poor feeding, rash not fading, persistent fever >48 h on antibiotics, limb pain/swelling (necrotising fasciitis) → 999/same day. Complications: quinsy, otitis media, rheumatic fever, post-strep glomerulonephritis (urinalysis if oedema/haematuria 2–3 weeks later).
2. Inguinal hernia: groin swelling that may extend to scrotum, worse crying/straining, reducible; infants <1 year — URGENT paediatric surgical referral (herniotomy within weeks; incarceration risk 30% in first year); irreducible/tender/vomiting → EMERGENCY (incarceration — attempt to reduce only if trained, do not delay transfer). Hydrocele: transilluminates, cannot get above it is false — can get above; most resolve by 2 years; refer if persists >2 years. Umbilical hernia: wait until 4–5 years unless large/symptomatic.
3. TB in children: contact of smear-positive case → notify/refer to TB service (Mantoux or IGRA ≥2 years; chest X-ray; latent TB — 3 months rifampicin + isoniazid or 6 months isoniazid; <2 years exposed → immediate chemoprophylaxis). Active TB: persistent cough >3 weeks, fever, weight loss/faltering growth, lymphadenopathy, from high-incidence country/contact → urgent chest X-ray + TB service (NG33); notifiable; BCG for eligible infants (high-incidence areas/parents from countries ≥40/100,000).
4. Anxiety in children: screen (RCADS, SCARED), explore school, bullying, family, neurodevelopment (ASD/ADHD), sleep, screen time, physical symptoms (abdominal pain/headache). First line: psychoeducation, parent-led CBT (books/online — e.g. 'Helping your child with fears and worries'), school support/ELSA, guided self-help via Mental Health Support Teams; CBT via CAMHS/CYP-IAPT for moderate–severe or functional impairment (school refusal); sertraline (CAMHS-initiated, 25 mg → 50–100 mg) for severe/unresponsive; safeguarding and self-harm/suicide screen always; refer CAMHS urgently if self-harm, eating restriction, psychosis.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspected Perthes (limp, hip/knee pain, 4–8 years): Urgent orthopaedic referral. X-ray and/or MRI.
2. Avoid weight-bearing if confirmed; physiotherapy; containment if indicated. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Circumcision: Not routinely recommended for physiological phimosis (resolves with time). If pathological phimosis or parental request after discussion: refer to paediatric surgery/urology.
2. Phimosis: Topical steroid (e.g. betamethasone 0.05% once daily for 4–8 weeks) if ballooning or infection; refer if failed or scarring. NICE CKS.
3. Hypospadias: Refer to paediatric urology (surgical correction). Do not circumcise before referral. NICE NG11, NG111, CKS.

options.label: Low Risk (Score 0-1)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG138):
1. Treatment: Amoxicillin 500mg tds for 5 days. 
2. Allergic: Doxycycline 200mg day 1 then 100mg OD, or Clarithromycin 500mg bd.
3. Note: Do not use dual antibiotics for low-risk CAP. NICE NG138.

options.label: Moderate / High Risk (Score ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Consider hospital admission for Score 2; Mandatory for Score ≥ 3.
2. Dual Antibiotics (Moderate): Amoxicillin + Clarithromycin.
3. High Severity: Co-amoxiclav + Clarithromycin (usually IV in hospital). NICE NG138.

tools.title: Postnatal care  the maternal 6-week check – Management

options.label: Consultant Care Ethos
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Priority**: Balance the needs of maternal mental health with fetal/infant safety.
2. **Meds**: Avoid 'blind' stopping of effective medication in pregnancy; risk of relapse is high. Consult specialized databases (e.g. BUMPS).
3. **Safety**: Vigilant monitoring for Postpartum Psychosis—a true psychiatric emergency.
4. **Support**: Immediate referral to Specialist Perinatal Mental Health Teams (PMHT).

options.label: Depression / Psychosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Postnatal Depression (PND): SSRIs (Sertraline/Paroxetine) generally preferred if breastfeeding (low milk excretion).
2. Postpartum Psychosis: **Psychiatric Emergency**. Immediate referral to Parent & Baby Unit (MBU). Specialist management with Lithium/Antipsychotics. High risk of infanticide/suicide. NICE CG192.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent paediatric endocrinology referral: puberty before 8 (girls) or 9 (boys). LH/FSH, oestradiol/testosterone, bone age, pelvic USS (girls).
2. Treat underlying cause; GnRH analogue if central precocious puberty. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Proprioception and sleep for children with additional needs – Management

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sleep hygiene; sensory factors; routine. Exclude medical causes (OSA, pain). NICE NG76, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Behavioural strategies; melatonin only if indicated per NICE. Refer sleep clinic if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude red flags (weight loss, nocturnal pain, family history IBD). Reassurance; dietary review; stress/school.
2. Refer if red flags, persistent, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive. Fever then rash (HHV-6). Exclude other causes if unwell. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive. Notify if confirmed. Avoid contact with pregnant women.
2. Refer if congenital exposure in pregnancy. MMR for prevention. NICE CKS.

options.label: Med3 (Fit Notes)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First 7 days: Patient self-certifies (Employer cannot demand Med3).
2. >7 days: Clinician issues Med3 based on clinical assessment.
3. Note: Focus on what patient 'can' do (phased return, amended duties) where possible.

options.label: Safeguarding (Adult/Child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify: Physical, emotional, sexual abuse, or neglect (including self-neglect in adults).
2. Action: Discuss with Designated Lead. Urgent referral to MASH (Children) or Adult Social Care if risk is immediate.
3. Documentation: Use factual, objective language. Do not promise confidentiality if disclosure is required for safety.

options.label: Continuity & QOF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Disease: Annual review (QOF) including bloods and symptom score.
2. Polypharmacy: Holistic medication review (SMR) with clinical pharmacist for patients on >10 meds.
