options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess curve (Adam's forward bend); if suspected, refer orthopaedics/spinal. Monitor if mild and growing.
2. Red flags: rapid progression, pain, neurology, infantile/juvenile. NICE CKS.

options.label: Risk Assessment (RCPsych)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Immediate: Assess method, intent, and access to means. 
2. Safety Planning: Identify warning signs, coping strategies (e.g., grounding), and 'Safe People'. Provide 24/7 Crisis numbers (988 / 111 / Local Crisis Team).
3. Referral: Emergency department if lethal act or active intent. Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) for persistent self-harm. NICE NG225.

options.label: Safeguarding
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Follow safeguarding policy; do not investigate alone. Refer to social care/police as per local protocol. Document. NICE NG76.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive care. Avoid contact with pregnant women (risk of fetal hydrops).
2. Refer if aplastic crisis (e.g. sickle cell), immunocompromised, or pregnancy exposure. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sleep hygiene: routine, consistent bedtime, limit screens. Behavioural strategies (controlled crying, gradual retreat) if appropriate.
2. Refer if sleep disorder suspected, OSA, or significant family impact. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect in obese adolescent with hip/knee pain or limp. Emergency orthopaedic referral; non-weight-bearing until assessed.
2. Surgical pinning to prevent further slip. NICE CKS.

options.label: Score 0–1 (no antibiotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Safety-net: if worsening or no improvement in 1 week, re-assess. NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 2–3+ (antibiotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg qds 5–10 days (or clarithromycin if penicillin allergic). Do not use amoxicillin if glandular fever suspected (rash). NICE NG84.

options.label: Glandular fever / quinsy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Glandular fever: supportive; avoid amoxicillin (rash). Consider monospot/EBV serology if prolonged or diagnostic uncertainty.
2. Quinsy (peritonsillar abscess): admit for drainage; do not manage in primary care. Stridor or severe dysphagia – urgent. NICE NG84, CKS.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recurrent tonsillitis: refer per local criteria (e.g. ≥7 in 1 year, ≥5/year for 2 years). 2WW: hoarseness >3 weeks, suspected cancer. Quinsy, stridor – urgent. NICE NG84, NG12.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hearing test; assess language and social communication. Early intervention (SLT) if delayed.
2. Refer if red flags (regression, no words by 18 months), or for autism assessment if indicated. NICE NG128, CKS.

options.label: Advice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; teething rings; paracetamol/ibuprofen for distress. Do not attribute fever, diarrhoea or rash to teething alone – assess for other cause.
2. CKS Teething.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Growth, hips (Ortolani/Barlow), heart (murmur), eyes (red reflex), testes. Maternal mental health. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Mebendazole 100 mg single dose (repeat at 2 weeks if reinfection). Treat whole household. Hygiene: handwashing, wash sleepwear/bedding.
2. Avoid in pregnancy (hygiene measures only). NICE CKS.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer by 6 months (corrected for prematurity) for surgical opinion. Do not confuse with retractile. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer by 6 months (corrected for prematurity) for surgical opinion. Do not confuse with retractile. NICE NG11, CKS.

options.label: Woman (Non-pregnant)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg MR bd (if eGFR ≥45) or Trimethoprim 200mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: Man
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Always send MSU. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg MR bd.
2. Duration: 7 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: Pregnant Woman
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Always send MSU. 1st-line: Nitrofurantoin 100mg (avoid at term) or Cefalexin.
2. Duration: 7 days. NICE NG109.

options.label: Child / recurrent / pyelonephritis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Child: Send MSU; treat per local guidance; refer if ≤3 months or atypical/severe. Consider imaging if recurrent.
2. Recurrent: Consider prophylaxis (nitrofurantoin at night) or self-start. Pyelonephritis: Send MSU, consider admission or 7–14 days oral (e.g. cefalexin). NICE NG109.

options.label: Women – uncomplicated cystitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. MSU: Send if recurrent, pregnant, or pyelonephritis suspected; otherwise can treat empirically. First-line: nitrofurantoin 100 mg MR bd 3 days, OR trimethoprim 200 mg bd 3 days (check local resistance). Avoid nitrofurantoin if eGFR <45. Alternative: pivmecillinam 400 mg tds 3 days.
2. If pregnant: MSU; treat 7 days; avoid trimethoprim in first trimester (folate). NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Men / pyelonephritis / recurrent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Men: MSU; treat 7 days (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim). Consider prostatitis if tender prostate; longer course.
2. Pyelonephritis: MSU + bloods; consider admission if systemically unwell. Oral: cefalexin or co-amoxiclav 7–10 days (per local resistance).
3. Recurrent: MSU when symptomatic; consider prophylaxis (e.g. nitrofurantoin at night) or referral. NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Catheter / pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Catheter: Only treat if symptomatic; MSU from catheter; replace catheter if long-term. Consider prophylaxis only if recurrent and symptomatic.
2. Pregnancy: MSU; 7-day course; avoid trimethoprim first trimester. Follow up MSU.
3. Refer: Pyelonephritis not improving; recurrent UTI; structural abnormality; children. 2WW if visible haematuria. NICE NG109, NG12.

options.label: Women – uncomplicated cystitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. MSU: Send if recurrent, pregnant, or pyelonephritis suspected; otherwise can treat empirically. First-line: nitrofurantoin 100 mg MR bd 3 days, OR trimethoprim 200 mg bd 3 days (check local resistance). Avoid nitrofurantoin if eGFR <45. Alternative: pivmecillinam 400 mg tds 3 days.
2. If pregnant: MSU; treat 7 days; avoid trimethoprim in first trimester (folate). NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Men / pyelonephritis / recurrent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Men: MSU; treat 7 days (nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim). Consider prostatitis if tender prostate; longer course.
2. Pyelonephritis: MSU + bloods; consider admission if systemically unwell. Oral: cefalexin or co-amoxiclav 7–10 days (per local resistance).
3. Recurrent: MSU when symptomatic; consider prophylaxis (e.g. nitrofurantoin at night) or referral. NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Catheter / pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Catheter: Only treat if symptomatic; MSU from catheter; replace catheter if long-term. Consider prophylaxis only if recurrent and symptomatic.
2. Pregnancy: MSU; 7-day course; avoid trimethoprim first trimester. Follow up MSU.
3. Refer: Pyelonephritis not improving; recurrent UTI; structural abnormality; children. 2WW if visible haematuria. NICE NG109, NG12.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Usually identified after UTI or antenatally (dilatation). Imaging: USS kidneys/ureters/bladder; consider MCUG if indicated (e.g. recurrent UTI, dilatation).
2. Management: Many low-grade VUR resolve. Prophylactic antibiotics may be used in selected cases. Treat UTIs promptly per NICE NG224.
3. Refer: Paediatric nephrology/urology for high-grade VUR, bilateral VUR, breakthrough UTIs, or renal scarring. NICE NG224, CKS UTI children.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Most viral rashes: supportive. Exclude meningococcal (non-blanching, unwell), Kawasaki, HSP.
2. Safety-net: Traffic light (NG143). Refer if non-blanching, fever + unwell, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG143, CKS.

options.label: Step 1: SABA prn
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication: Symptoms < 3 times/week and no night-waking.
2. Warning: If using SABA ≥3 times/week, move to Step 2. BTS/SIGN Guidelines.

options.label: Step 2: Low-dose ICS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Beclometasone (e.g. Clenil 100mcg bd). Prevents airway remodelling and reduces exacerbation risk. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Step 3: Add LABA (Combined Inhaler)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: ICS + LABA (e.g. Fostair or Symbicort). MART (Maintenance and Reliever Therapy) is the specialist preference for improved adherence.
2. Review: If still poorly controlled on moderate-dose ICS+LABA, consider LTRA (Montelukast). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Moderate (PEFR 50-75% best)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treatment: SABA 2-5 puffs via spacer every 10-20 mins. Oral Prednisolone 40-50mg for 5 days. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Severe (PEFR 33-50% / RR ≥ 25 / HR ≥ 110)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triage: Immediate hospital admission (999). High-flow Oxygen. Nebulised SABA + Ipratropium. BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Life-Threatening (PEFR <33% / SpO2 <92% / Silent Chest)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999. Do not delay. Life-threatening features (33-92-CHEST). BTS/SIGN.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Notify public health. Macrolide (e.g. azithromycin) if <21 days of cough to reduce spread; may not change course. Supportive for paroxysms.
2. Refer if infant <6 months, severe paroxysms, or complications. NICE CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat cause; stop nephrotoxics; correct volume/electrolytes. Monitor U&E, eGFR, urine output.
2. Refer if cause unclear, stage 3 AKI, no improvement, or complications. NICE NG148, NG203.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer if cause unclear, stage 3 AKI, no improvement, or complications. Stop nephrotoxics; correct volume/electrolytes. NICE NG148, NG203.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Do not treat except in pregnancy (prevents pyelonephritis) or before urological surgery. Treat in pregnancy with antibiotic per sensitivities.
2. No treatment in diabetic women, elderly, or catheterised unless symptomatic. NICE NG109, CKS.

options.label: Consultant Management Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Ethos**: Transition from a 'medical model' (fixing deficits) to a 'social model' (adjusting environment).
2. **Co-morbidity**: High rates of ADHD, Anxiety, and Dyspraxia. Always screen for co-occurring conditions.
3. **Biological**: Meds have NO role in core ASD features. Used only for co-morbidities (e.g. Melatonin for sleep, SSRIs for OCD).
4. **Social**: Educational (EHCP) and Workplace adjustments are the primary interventions.

options.label: Child/Young Person
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Referral: Local multi-agency ASD pathway (Paediatrics/CAMHS).
2. Screening: SCQ (Social Communication Questionnaire). 
3. Assessment: ADOS and ADI-R (Gold standard tools).

options.label: Adult suspected ASD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Screening: **AQ-10** (Score ≥6 = Refer).
2. Referral: Specialist diagnostic assessment only if significant impact on social/working life. NICE CG142.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Visible haematuria (any age): 2WW urology. Non-visible: exclude UTI; if persistent and ≥45y or other risk factors, refer 2WW. Dipstick in pregnancy: exclude UTI/pre-eclampsia.
2. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude UTI, pathology. Multimodal: analgesia, bladder training, stress management. Amitriptyline or cimetidine may help. Refer urology for cystoscopy/Hunner's if refractory.
2. NICE NG123, CKS Bladder pain syndrome.

tools.title: CKD

options.label: Staging & monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stage by eGFR (G1–G5) and ACR (A1–A3). Confirm with repeat eGFR/ACR – CKD if persistent ≥3 months. Exclude UTI before attributing haematuria/proteinuria to CKD.
2. Monitoring: G1–2 + A1: annual. G3a: annual. G3b: 6-monthly. G4–5: 3-monthly (or per nephrology). U&E, eGFR, ACR, BP. NICE NG203, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. BP: Target <140/90 (or <130/80 if ACR >70 or diabetic). ACEi/ARB first-line; titrate. Avoid NSAIDs; review nephrotoxics (e.g. gentamicin, contrast).
2. SGLT2i: Offer if T2DM and eGFR ≥20 (dose per licence). Cardiovascular risk: statin. Anaemia: check if eGFR <60 (Hb, ferritin, B12, folate); treat and refer if ESA needed. NICE NG203.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer nephrology: eGFR <30 (G4–G5); rapid decline (>5 ml/min/1.73 m²/year); ACR ≥70 with haematuria; suspected glomerulonephritis or vasculitis; refractory hypertension; recurrent AKI; genetic/surgical cause. Urgent if RPGN, hyperkalaemia with ECG changes, or severe AKI. NICE NG203, NG12.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Antibiotics: ofloxacin or ceftriaxone if STI likely; co-amoxiclav if UTI/enteric. Exclude torsion (urgent surgical referral if suspected).
2. 2WW: testicular mass. Support, scrotal elevation, analgesia. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude vascular, diabetes, psychological. PDE5i first-line (sildenafil, tadalafil); advise on use. Check testosterone if low libido.
2. Refer if failure of oral treatment, penile deformity, or young with vascular concern. NICE NG23, CKS.

tools.title: Male LUTS, BPH and prostate cancer – assessment, PSA, treatment, referral

options.label: LUTS assessment and PSA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess (CG97): IPSS score and bother, 3-day frequency–volume chart, urinalysis, DRE (size, consistency, nodules), PVR if voiding symptoms, U&E if chronic retention suspected; medication review (anticholinergics, decongestants, diuretics). Red flags: haematuria (2WW ≥45), retention (catheterise), palpable bladder, renal impairment, recurrent UTI, stones, neurological symptoms.
2. PSA: offer counselling (PCRMP) before testing any man ≥50 who asks, or earlier if Black ethnicity/family history/BRCA; no screening programme. Do not test within 6 weeks of UTI/prostatitis, 48 h of ejaculation/vigorous exercise, 1 week of DRE. Age-specific referral thresholds (NG12 2024/PCRMP): 40–49 >2.5; 50–59 >3.5; 60–69 >4.5; 70–79 >6.5 micrograms/L; ≥80 use clinical judgement — refer 2WW if above threshold OR prostate feels malignant on DRE (regardless of PSA). Finasteride/dutasteride halve PSA — double the result after 6 months.
3. Mild symptoms (IPSS ≤7) or not bothered: reassure, lifestyle — reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; bladder training; double voiding; treat constipation; review annually.

options.label: BPH drug treatment and when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Moderate–severe voiding LUTS: alpha-blocker — tamsulosin 400 micrograms od MR (alfuzosin 10 mg MR, doxazosin 4 mg MR alternatives); benefit within 1–2 weeks; warn postural hypotension, ejaculatory dysfunction, floppy-iris (tell ophthalmologist before cataract surgery).
2. Prostate >30 g (or PSA >1.4 micrograms/L as proxy) and risk of progression: add 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor — finasteride 5 mg od or dutasteride 500 micrograms od (combination capsule Combodart); takes 3–6 months; reduces retention/surgery risk; sexual side effects, breast changes (report lumps), MHRA depression/suicidal ideation warning; halves PSA.
3. Storage symptoms persisting on alpha-blocker with PVR <200 mL: add antimuscarinic (tolterodine 4 mg MR/solifenacin 5 mg) or mirabegron 50 mg (CG97/NG123). Nocturnal polyuria: desmopressin 50 micrograms (Noqdirna) with Na monitoring. PDE5 inhibitor (tadalafil 5 mg od) if co-existing erectile dysfunction (licensed for BPH-LUTS).
4. Refer urology (routine): symptoms bothersome despite drugs, PVR >200–300 mL, recurrent UTI, bladder stones, haematuria, renal impairment from obstruction, patient preference for surgery — options TURP, HoLEP, UroLift (NICE MTG58; preserves ejaculation), Rezum, prostate artery embolisation. Acute retention → same-day catheter + alpha-blocker 2–3 days before trial without catheter.

options.label: Prostate cancer — after diagnosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pathway: 2WW → multiparametric MRI (Likert ≥3 → targeted biopsy) → Gleason/ISUP grade, PSA, staging (CAPRA/NICE risk groups); bone scan/PSMA-PET if intermediate/high risk.
2. Low risk (PSA <10, Gleason 6, T1–2a): ACTIVE SURVEILLANCE (NG131) — PSA every 3–4 months year 1, DRE, repeat MRI at 12–18 months, biopsy if change; GP: reassure, support, avoid unnecessary PSA outside protocol. Intermediate: surveillance (favourable), radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy (external beam ± brachytherapy) with 6 months ADT; high risk/locally advanced: radiotherapy + 2–3 years ADT, or prostatectomy + nodes; metastatic: ADT (GnRH agonist leuprorelin/goserelin/triptorelin 3-monthly, or antagonist degarelix/relugolix oral) PLUS docetaxel or abiraterone/enzalutamide/apalutamide (NICE TAs), bone protection (zoledronate/denosumab) for bone metastases.
3. GP role on ADT: cardiovascular risk (BP, lipids, HbA1c annually), osteoporosis — DEXA at baseline, calcium/vitamin D, bisphosphonate if T ≤−2.5 or fracture; hot flushes (medroxyprogesterone 20 mg od, cyproterone 50 mg bd, venlafaxine, gabapentin); fatigue (exercise programme), sexual dysfunction, gynaecomastia (prophylactic tamoxifen/radiotherapy), mood, anaemia, metabolic syndrome. Post-treatment: PSA at 6 weeks then 6-monthly for 2 years then annual; biochemical recurrence (PSA >0.2 post-surgery or nadir +2 post-radiotherapy) → oncology. Spinal cord compression (back pain + leg weakness/numbness/retention) = EMERGENCY — dexamethasone 16 mg + same-day MRI whole spine (NG75).

tools.title: Urinary incontinence, overactive bladder and nocturia
niceRefs: NICE CKS Incontinence – urinary, in women

options.label: Assessment (all)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Categorise: stress (leak on cough/exertion), urge/OAB (urgency ± leak, frequency >8/day, nocturia), mixed (treat the dominant symptom first), overflow (poor stream, retention — check post-void residual), functional (mobility/cognition). 3-day bladder diary (volumes, times, fluid intake); urinalysis ± MSU; post-void residual (bladder scan) if voiding symptoms, recurrent UTI, neurological disease, men; examine abdomen, pelvic floor strength (women), prolapse, prostate (men), neurology; medication review (diuretics, alpha-blockers in women → stress incontinence, antimuscarinic burden, sedatives, lithium, SGLT2i).
2. Red flags → refer: visible haematuria (2WW ≥45), microscopic haematuria with dysuria/raised WCC in ≥60 (2WW), recurrent UTI with haematuria ≥60 (2WW), palpable bladder/pelvic mass, suspected fistula, neurological disease (new), persistent pain, previous pelvic surgery/radiotherapy complications, faecal incontinence, voiding difficulty/retention.
3. Lifestyle for all: caffeine reduction, fluid 1.5–2 L/day (not restricted unless excessive), avoid fizzy/alcohol/artificial sweeteners, weight loss if BMI >30, stop smoking, treat constipation, bladder training (urge), timed voiding, containment products (NHS continence service), pelvic floor exercises.

options.label: Stress and urge/OAB — women
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stress: supervised pelvic floor muscle training ≥3 months (8 contractions ×3/day; physio/continence nurse; apps/pessary as adjunct); duloxetine 40 mg bd only if surgery declined/unsuitable (nausea; second line); refer urogynaecology if not improved — options (NG123, after MDT): colposuspension, autologous fascial sling, urethral bulking; mid-urethral mesh tape currently under high-vigilance restriction — specialist shared decision.
2. OAB/urge: bladder training ≥6 weeks FIRST; then antimuscarinic with lowest anticholinergic burden — solifenacin 5 mg od (→10 mg), tolterodine 2 mg bd/4 mg MR, trospium 20 mg bd (does not cross BBB — preferred in elderly/cognitive impairment); AVOID oxybutynin IR in frail older women (NG123, cognitive decline). Review at 4 weeks then 12 months (6 months if >75). If ineffective/not tolerated: mirabegron 50 mg od (25 mg if renal/hepatic impairment; check BP — contraindicated if uncontrolled hypertension ≥180/110) — may combine with antimuscarinic; vibegron (newer beta-3, NICE 2024 — check).
3. Nocturia specifically: evening fluid/caffeine/alcohol restriction, leg elevation afternoon (oedema), treat sleep apnoea/heart failure/diabetes, review diuretic timing (midday); desmopressin 25 micrograms (women)/50 micrograms (men) sublingual (Noqdirna) at bedtime for nocturnal polyuria (>33% of 24-h output at night) if age <65 or Na checked (baseline, day 3–7, 1 month; avoid if Na <135, heart failure, age >65 without specialist).
4. Refractory OAB: urology/urogynaecology — botulinum toxin A 100 units intravesical (NG123; teach self-catheterisation risk 5–10%), percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, sacral neuromodulation; vaginal oestrogen (estriol 0.1% cream/estradiol 10 microgram pessary) for post-menopausal women with OAB/atrophy — safe long term.

options.label: Men — incontinence and post-prostatectomy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urge/OAB in men: exclude obstruction (IPSS, flow, PVR >200 mL → treat BPH first — see LUTS tool); bladder training; antimuscarinic (solifenacin/tolterodine) or mirabegron — safe to combine with alpha-blocker (tamsulosin) if PVR <200 mL; review retention risk.
2. Stress incontinence after prostatectomy: pelvic floor training (physio-led) started before and continued after surgery for ≥6–12 months — most improve by 12 months; containment; refer urology at 6–12 months if persistent: male sling or artificial urinary sphincter (NG123/BAUS); duloxetine off-label.
3. Overflow/retention: PVR >300 mL, dribbling, palpable bladder → catheterise/urology; chronic retention with hydronephrosis or renal impairment → urgent.
4. Functional incontinence (dementia, immobility): timed toileting, commode, clothing adaptations, continence products, treat constipation, avoid antimuscarinics where possible, OT/continence service, carer support.

2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.guidance:
