1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

tools.title: Urinary tract infection – women, men, pregnancy, recurrent, and painful bladder syndrome
niceRefs: UKHSA Diagnosis of UTI quick reference 2024
NICE CKS Urinary tract infection (lower) – women

options.label: Women (non-pregnant) — acute and recurrent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnose on symptoms (UKHSA 2024): ≥2 of dysuria, new nocturia, cloudy urine = treat empirically (dipstick adds little in <65s; NO dipstick in >65s or catheterised — asymptomatic bacteriuria is common and not treated). Send MSU if: pregnancy, men, recurrent, treatment failure, resistance risk (care home, recent antibiotics, travel), haematuria, age >65 with symptoms. Exclude vaginal cause (discharge/irritation → STI/candida), urethritis, atrophic vaginitis.
2. Uncomplicated cystitis: back-up/delayed prescription or immediate; self-care — paracetamol/ibuprofen, fluids; NOT cranberry/alkalinisers as treatment. First line 3 days: nitrofurantoin MR 100 mg bd (if eGFR ≥45) or trimethoprim 200 mg bd (if low resistance risk/not used in past 3 months); second: pivmecillinam 400 mg stat then 200 mg tds (3 days), fosfomycin 3 g single dose. Pyelonephritis (loin pain, fever, rigors, vomiting): cefalexin 500 mg bd–tds 7–10 days or co-amoxiclav 625 mg tds/ciprofloxacin 500 mg bd 7 days; admit if septic, pregnant, vomiting, no improvement 48 h.
3. Recurrent (≥2 in 6 months / ≥3 in 12 months, NG112): MSU each episode, review contraception (switch from spermicide/diaphragm), post-coital voiding, fluids; post-menopausal — vaginal oestrogen (estriol 0.1% cream twice weekly) FIRST; D-mannose 2 g od and cranberry (no strong evidence; may try); methenamine hippurate 1 g bd (ALTAR trial — as effective as prophylactic antibiotics; avoid eGFR <10/alkalinising agents); single-dose post-coital antibiotic (trimethoprim 100 mg/nitrofurantoin 50–100 mg) if coital trigger; otherwise 3–6 months prophylaxis trimethoprim 100 mg nocte or nitrofurantoin 50–100 mg nocte (review at 6 months; nitrofurantoin long-term lung/liver risk, FBC/LFT/pulmonary symptoms). Refer urology: haematuria, recurrent despite prophylaxis, stones, structural abnormality, poor emptying (USS KUB + PVR).

options.label: Men, catheters, pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Men: always send MSU before antibiotics; treat 7 days — trimethoprim 200 mg bd or nitrofurantoin MR 100 mg bd (only if no prostatic involvement suspected); if prostatitis features (perineal/low back pain, fever, tender prostate, systemically unwell) → ciprofloxacin 500 mg bd 14 days (or trimethoprim 200 mg bd 14 days if quinolone unsuitable; MHRA restrictions) — do NOT massage prostate; admit if septic. Investigate ALL men with UTI: PVR, consider USS renal tract/flexible cystoscopy via urology if recurrent, haematuria, retention, or age >60 (NG12 2WW if visible haematuria ≥45 or unexplained non-visible haematuria + dysuria/raised WCC ≥60). STI screen if <35 or risk.
2. Catheter-associated UTI: do not dipstick/culture or treat bacteriuria without symptoms; symptoms = fever, rigors, new flank/suprapubic pain, new confusion/delirium, visible haematuria; change the catheter (if in >7 days) and send CSU from the new one; 7 days antibiotics (NG113) — nitrofurantoin/trimethoprim/amoxicillin per sensitivities, or if upper tract/septic → cefalexin/co-amoxiclav/ciprofloxacin; consider removing catheter; no prophylactic antibiotics for long-term catheters.
3. Pregnancy: send MSU at booking and treat ASYMPTOMATIC bacteriuria (confirmed on a second sample) — reduces pyelonephritis/preterm birth; symptomatic or bacteriuria → 7 days nitrofurantoin MR 100 mg bd (AVOID at term ≥36 weeks — neonatal haemolysis), amoxicillin 500 mg tds (only if sensitive), cefalexin 500 mg bd; AVOID trimethoprim in first trimester (folate antagonist — if unavoidable give folic acid 5 mg) and quinolones throughout; test of cure MSU 7 days after; group B strep in urine → inform maternity (intrapartum prophylaxis). Pyelonephritis in pregnancy → ADMIT.

options.label: Bladder pain syndrome / interstitial cystitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Suspect: suprapubic pain related to bladder filling, relieved by voiding, frequency/urgency/nocturia >6 weeks with repeatedly NEGATIVE MSU and no other cause (UTI, stones, OAB, endometriosis, prostatitis, cancer — cystoscopy to exclude carcinoma in situ in >40s/smokers/haematuria). Often co-exists with IBS, fibromyalgia, vulvodynia, anxiety/depression.
2. First line (BAUS/EAU/AUA): education, bladder diary, dietary modification (avoid caffeine, alcohol, acidic/spicy foods, artificial sweeteners — individual triggers), stress management/CBT, pelvic floor physiotherapy (down-training — NOT Kegels), analgesia (paracetamol; amitriptyline 10 mg nocte titrating to 25–75 mg; or gabapentin/pregabalin via pain clinic), antihistamine (cimetidine 400 mg bd, hydroxyzine 25–50 mg nocte — modest evidence), avoid repeated antibiotic courses without positive cultures.
3. Refer urology (routine; urgent if haematuria) for cystoscopy ± hydrodistension (Hunner lesions → fulguration/triamcinolone), intravesical treatments (hyaluronic acid/chondroitin — Cystistat/iAluRil; DMSO; lidocaine cocktails), botulinum toxin A, pentosan polysulfate (Elmiron — NICE TA; MHRA pigmentary maculopathy warning, eye checks), neuromodulation; multidisciplinary pain service; patient support (Bladder Health UK).

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE NG109 UTI lower 2018; NG111 pyelonephritis 2018; NG112 recurrent UTI 2018; NICE CKS UTI (lower) women / men / Recurrent / Bladder pain syndrome 2024; UKHSA diagnosis of UTI 2024; BAUS/EAU BPS; BNF)

options.label: Insertion & care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aseptic technique; correct size (e.g. 12–14Ch). Trial without catheter when appropriate. Document indication and review date.
2. Long-term: change per protocol; screen for infection only if symptomatic. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pelvic floor exercises; pessary if preferred. Avoid heavy lifting; treat constipation.
2. Refer gynaecology if symptomatic or for surgery. NICE NG23, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude torsion (urgent surgical referral). USS if mass or uncertainty. Hydrocele: refer if symptomatic or diagnostic uncertainty. Varicocele: refer if symptomatic or size concern.
2. 2WW: testicular mass. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ANCA-associated vasculitis: urgent nephrology/rheumatology. Biopsy for diagnosis. Immunosuppression (e.g. rituximab, cyclophosphamide + steroids).
2. Supportive: BP control; avoid nephrotoxics. NICE NG203, CKS.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Paediatric renal tumour: abdominal mass, haematuria, hypertension. Urgent paediatric oncology referral. Do not biopsy in primary care.
2. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

options.label: Assessment & 2WW
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Examine: lump, nipple change, axillary nodes. 2WW breast if: discrete lump (any age), lump in ≥30y, nipple change, skin tethering, or strong family history concern. Under 30: benign features may be observed with urgent referral if concern. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Cyst vs solid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. USS in younger women; mammography + USS in ≥40. Simple cyst: aspirate if symptomatic; discharge if no blood. Solid: 2WW. Triple assessment (clinical, imaging, biopsy) in secondary care. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Lactational mastitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Continue breastfeeding; empty breast (feed or express). Flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 10–14 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergy). If no improvement in 24–48 h or abscess suspected: refer. Incision and drainage if abscess. NICE CKS.

options.label: Non-lactational / abscess
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Flucloxacillin; consider USS to exclude abscess. Periductal mastitis: may need anaerobic cover (metronidazole). Abscess: drain; send pus for MC&S. Refer if recurrent, male breast lump, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CKS, NG12.

options.label: Routine & follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Invite per national screening programme (25–64). If abnormal: refer colposcopy per HPV triage.
2. Manage anxiety; ensure result and follow-up communicated. NICE NG12, CSP.

tools.title: Chronic pelvic pain, vulvodynia, vaginismus and breast pain

options.label: Chronic pelvic pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ≥6 months intermittent/constant lower abdominal/pelvic pain not exclusively with menstruation/intercourse. Causes often overlap: endometriosis/adenomyosis, PID sequelae/adhesions, IBS, interstitial cystitis/painful bladder, musculoskeletal (pelvic floor myalgia, hernia, nerve entrapment — pudendal), psychosocial (abuse history, depression — ask sensitively), post-surgical.
2. Work-up: pregnancy test, STI screen (chlamydia/gonorrhoea), urinalysis/MSU, FBC/CRP, transvaginal USS; pain diary (cyclical pattern suggests endometriosis — NG73); examine for trigger points, pelvic floor tenderness.
3. Management: explain pain mechanisms early; NSAID/paracetamol; hormonal suppression trial 3–6 months (CHC continuous, desogestrel, LNG-IUS) if cyclical even with normal USS; IBS treatment (antispasmodic, low FODMAP, linaclotide); pelvic floor physiotherapy; amitriptyline 10–50 mg or gabapentin for neuropathic component; CBT/pain management programme. Refer gynaecology if suspected endometriosis, no response at 3–6 months, or abnormal USS; laparoscopy for diagnosis/treatment; MDT pelvic pain clinic for refractory. Red flags → 2WW (mass, ascites, PMB, weight loss).

options.label: Vulvodynia and vaginismus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Vulvodynia (burning vulval pain ≥3 months, no visible cause; provoked at entrance — Q-tip test — or unprovoked/generalised): exclude candida (swab), lichen sclerosus/planus, dermatitis (irritants, soaps), atrophy (menopause), herpes, neuropathy. Management: vulval skin care (emollient/soap substitute, cotton underwear, avoid wipes/panty liners), topical lidocaine 5% ointment 15–20 min before intercourse (or overnight), amitriptyline 10 mg → 25–75 mg or gabapentin, pelvic floor physiotherapy (first line for provoked), CBT/psychosexual counselling (Relate/COSRT), vaginal dilators; vulval pain clinic/dermatology if persistent; vestibulectomy rarely.
2. Vaginismus (involuntary pelvic floor spasm preventing penetration; often fear/pain cycle; may follow painful first experiences, trauma, vulvodynia): explain, examine only with consent/with the woman in control; graded self-exploration and dilator programme with pelvic floor physiotherapist; psychosexual therapy; treat underlying vulvodynia/atrophy; botulinum toxin via specialist in refractory cases. Local lubricant; avoid blaming partner dynamics. Refer psychosexual service.

options.label: Breast pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cyclical (bilateral, diffuse, luteal phase, premenopausal, examination normal): reassure — not cancer (pain alone <1% cancer risk); supportive bra (day and night), paracetamol/ibuprofen or topical NSAID (diclofenac gel), reduce caffeine (weak evidence), review HRT/CHC (consider lower oestrogen, progestogen change or stopping); evening primrose oil no longer recommended. Persistent severe cyclical pain >6 months affecting life → breast clinic for danazol/tamoxifen (specialist, off-label).
2. Non-cyclical: localised — costochondritis (Tietze — tender costal cartilage; NSAID), trauma, cysts (USS/aspiration), periductal mastitis (smokers; co-amoxiclav), mastitis/abscess (lactational — flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 10–14 days, continue feeding, USS if not settling 48 h → aspiration), herpes zoster, cervical/thoracic referred pain, cardiac (if exertional/left-sided).
3. NG12: 2WW breast clinic for any unexplained lump (age ≥30), skin change, nipple change/discharge (≥50 unilateral), or any lump with pain; pain with no lump and normal examination does NOT need 2WW — reassure and review in 6–8 weeks; consider routine breast clinic if persistent unilateral non-cyclical pain.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

tools.title: Contraception

options.label: Combined / POP / implant / IUS / IUD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Combined pill: check UKMEC (avoid if VTE risk, migraine with aura, breast cancer). POP: safe in most; desogestrel more reliable for ovulation suppression. Implant: 3 years. IUS: 5–8 years; first-line for HMB. IUD: 5–10 years; check UKMEC. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: Emergency contraception
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg single dose (within 72 h; use up to 96 h if needed). Ulipristal 30 mg single dose (within 120 h; more effective; avoid with enzyme inducers). Cu-IUD: most effective; within 5 days of UPSI or 5 days after earliest ovulation. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: Special situations
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breastfeeding: POP, implant, IUD/IUS (from 4 weeks); avoid COCP until 6 months. Migraine with aura: avoid COCP (VTE). VTE risk: avoid COCP; POP/IUD/IUS usually OK. Perimenopause: continue to 55 if no contraindication. NICE NG3, UKMEC, CKS.

aliases: Effective contraception provision during the COVID-19 pandemic – Management

options.label: Contraception & HMB
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HMB: Levonorgestrel IUS first-line; tranexamic acid 1 g tds during bleed; mefenamic acid; COCP or cyclical progestogen if preferred. Pelvic US if fibroids/suspected structural cause. NICE NG88.
2. Contraception: choice per UKMEC; COCP/POP/implant/IUS/IUD per need. Emergency: levonorgestrel or ulipristal or Cu-IUD. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: Bleeding – IMB / PCB / 2WW
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IMB/PCB: speculum; swabs; cervical visualisation. PMB: 2WW gynaecology (any bleeding after menopause). 2WW: ovarian/endometrial/cervical concern. NICE NG12, NG88.

options.label: Vaginal infection & pelvic pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Candida: clotrimazole or fluconazole. BV: metronidazole. Trichomonas: metronidazole; treat contacts. Pelvic pain: exclude PID (screen chlamydia/gonorrhoea; ofloxacin + metronidazole); consider endometriosis. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: Pregnancy & breast
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Miscarriage: expectant/medical/surgical; anti-D if Rh-negative. Hyperemesis: antiemetics; exclude molar. Pre-eclampsia: BP, urine; refer. Breast lump: 2WW. Mastitis: flucloxacillin; empty breast. NICE NG126, NG88, NG12, CKS.

options.label: 2WW & when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 2WW: Postmenopausal bleeding, breast lump with concern, suspected ovarian/endometrial/cervical cancer. Urgent: ectopic, torsion, severe PID, haemodynamically unstable. Routine: HMB not controlled, endometriosis, recurrent thrush, contraception complex. NICE NG12, NG88.

options.label: Cold sore
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aciclovir 5% cream 5×/day 5 days, or oral aciclovir 200 mg 5×/day 5 days if early/severe.
2. Suppression: consider if ≥6 episodes/year. NICE CKS.

options.label: First episode genital
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aciclovir 400 mg tds 7–10 days (or valaciclovir). Screen for other STIs. Counsel on transmission.
2. Suppression if recurrent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

tools.title: Gynaecological cancer – ovarian, endometrial, cervical, vulval (2WW)
niceRefs: NICE CKS Gynaecological cancers – recognition and referral

options.label: Ovarian
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NG12/CG122: measure CA125 in any woman (especially ≥50) with persistent or frequent (>12×/month) bloating, early satiety/loss of appetite, pelvic/abdominal pain, urinary urgency/frequency, new IBS-type symptoms (IBS rarely starts >50), unexplained weight loss, fatigue, or change in bowel habit. Examine abdomen/pelvis.
2. CA125 ≥35 IU/mL → urgent pelvic/abdominal USS; USS suggestive of cancer → 2WW gynaecology (RMI = USS score × menopausal score × CA125 calculated in secondary care). Ascites and/or pelvic/abdominal mass (not fibroids) on examination → 2WW directly, no need to wait for CA125/USS. Normal CA125 with persistent symptoms → USS anyway or reassess; keep safety-net (CA125 raised in endometriosis, PID, fibroids, pregnancy, any peritoneal irritation; normal in 50% of early-stage cancer).
3. Management (specialist): staging CT, surgery (TAH/BSO/omentectomy) ± platinum/taxane chemotherapy; PARP inhibitors (olaparib, niraparib) for BRCA/HRD; germline BRCA testing offered to all high-grade serous cases — cascade testing for relatives. GP: symptom control, bowel obstruction awareness, palliative care liaison. Family history (two first-degree relatives, BRCA) → genetics referral; risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy.

options.label: Endometrial
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NG12: 2WW for women ≥55 with POSTMENOPAUSAL BLEEDING (any bleeding >12 months after last period); consider 2WW if <55 with PMB. Consider direct-access transvaginal USS for ≥55 with unexplained vaginal discharge (new, thrush treated, or with thrombocytosis/haematuria) or visible haematuria with low Hb/thrombocytosis/high glucose.
2. Premenopausal risk (obesity, PCOS/anovulation, tamoxifen, Lynch syndrome, unopposed oestrogen): persistent IMB/HMB → TVUSS ± hysteroscopy/biopsy. Endometrial thickness ≥4 mm postmenopausal → hysteroscopy and biopsy. Bleeding on HRT: see HRT tool.
3. Management: hysterectomy + BSO ± lymph node assessment; radiotherapy/chemotherapy by stage; Lynch screening (MMR immunohistochemistry) on all tumours — refer genetics if deficient. Prevention counselling: weight, LNG-IUS/CHC protect in PCOS.

options.label: Cervical
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NG12: 2WW if the cervix LOOKS abnormal/suspicious of cancer on speculum (friable, ulcerated, mass, contact bleeding from a lesion) — do not take a smear (delays referral, smear is a screening not diagnostic test). Symptoms prompting speculum: post-coital bleeding, IMB, PMB, persistent offensive discharge, pelvic pain. Persistent PCB with a normal cervix → colposcopy referral (routine/urgent by age — see Menstrual tool).
2. Screening (NHS CSP): HPV primary screening every 3 years 25–49, 5 years 50–64 (moving to 5-yearly for HPV-negative in England from 2025); abnormal results managed per programme (colposcopy for HPV+ with abnormal cytology or persistent HPV at 24 months). HPV vaccination 12–13.
3. Management: LLETZ/cone for CIN/early; radical hysterectomy or chemoradiation by stage; fertility-sparing trachelectomy. Avoid smears in pregnancy unless overdue high-risk.

options.label: Vulval
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NG12: 2WW gynaecology for an unexplained vulval lump, ulceration or BLEEDING. Also refer persistent vulval itch/soreness not responding to 6–12 weeks of treatment for lichen sclerosus/candida, pigmented or raised plaque (VIN/melanoma), non-healing ulcer.
2. Lichen sclerosus (white atrophic plaques, 'figure of eight', architectural change; 2–5% lifetime SCC risk): clobetasol propionate 0.05% ointment once daily 4 weeks, alternate days 4 weeks, twice weekly 4 weeks then as needed; emollient/soap substitute; avoid irritants; annual review — biopsy any thickened/persistent/eroded area (vulval dermatology/gynaecology). Lichen planus, Paget's disease, VIN (HPV-related, young smokers) → vulval clinic for biopsy.
3. Management: wide local excision ± sentinel node/groin dissection; radiotherapy. Smoking cessation (VIN); lifelong follow-up.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Heavy Menstrual Bleeding (HMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG88):
1. 1st-line: Mirena IUS (if acceptable).
2. 2nd-line: Tranexamic Acid (1g tds during period) +/- Mefenamic Acid (500mg tds).
3. Hormonal: COCP or High-dose Progestogens (Medroxyprogesterone).
4. Investigation: Pelvic US if uterus large/fibroids, or fail medical tx.

options.label: PCOS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BMS/RCOG):
1. Diagnosis: Rotterdam criteria (2 of 3: Anovulation, Hyperandrogenism, Polycystic ovaries).
2. Protection: Prevent endometrial hyperplasia via IUS or COCP (ensure ≥4 bleeds/year).
3. Metabolic: Screen for T2DM (HbA1c) and CVD risk. Metformin if insulin resistant. NICE NG28, CKS PCOS.

options.label: Endometriosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG73):
1. Trial: 3-6 months COCP or POP. NSAIDs for pain.
2. Imaging: Pelvic US (specialist endometriosis scan if deep involvement suspected).
3. Referral: To BSGE Endometriosis centre if severe/refractory or bowel/bladder involvement.

options.label: Post-Menopausal Bleeding (PMB)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG/NICE):
1. Triage: Any vaginal bleeding in a post-menopausal woman not on HRT, or unexpected bleeding on HRT.
2. Action: Urgent 2WW Referral for Ultrasound +/- Hysteroscopy/Biopsy.
3. Cut-off: Endometrial thickness > 4mm in PMB requires biopsy. NICE NG12.

options.label: Small / fluctuant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Incision and drainage; send pus if recurrent or cellulitis. Do not use antibiotic alone for uncomplicated abscess.
2. Consider flucloxacillin if cellulitis or systemic symptoms. NICE NG141.

options.label: Recurrent boils
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hygiene; nasal decolonisation (mupirocin) if nasal carriage. Screen household. Consider referral if persistent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Lactational mastitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Continue breastfeeding; empty breast (feed or express). Flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 10–14 days (or erythromycin if penicillin allergy). If no improvement in 24–48 h or abscess suspected: refer. Incision and drainage if abscess. NICE CKS.

options.label: Non-lactational / abscess
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Flucloxacillin; consider USS to exclude abscess. Periductal mastitis: may need anaerobic cover (metronidazole). Abscess: drain; send pus for MC&S. Refer if recurrent, male breast lump, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CKS, NG12.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude lump (examine; refer if lump). Cyclical: reassurance, supportive bra; consider evening primrose oil. Non-cyclical: exclude musculoskeletal. NICE CKS.

options.label: No uterus – oestrogen only
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen only (patch/gel preferred for VTE risk). Review annually. NICE NG23.

options.label: With uterus – combined
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Oestrogen + cyclical or continuous progestogen. Sequential if perimenopausal; continuous if postmenopausal. NICE NG23.

options.label: Contraindications / alternatives
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Contraindications: breast cancer, VTE, stroke. Consider non-hormonal (clonidine, CBT) or topical oestrogen for urogenital. NICE NG23.

tools.title: Menopause – HRT choice, risks, bleeding on HRT, non-hormonal options

options.label: Diagnosis and HRT prescribing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnose clinically in women >45 (vasomotor symptoms + irregular/absent periods); FSH only if 40–45 with atypical symptoms, <40 (suspect POI — two FSH >25 IU/L 4–6 weeks apart), or on hormonal contraception. Also assess: sleep, mood, joint pain, cognition, libido, genitourinary symptoms, cardiovascular risk, bone risk (FRAX), contraception needs (until 2 years after LMP if <50, 1 year if >50; or 55).
2. HRT first line for vasomotor symptoms (and low mood/anxiety due to menopause — NG23 2024: do not offer SSRIs for low mood in menopause without depression). Oestrogen: transdermal preferred (patch 25–50 micrograms/24 h, gel 0.5–1 mg/2 pumps, spray) — no VTE/stroke increase, use if BMI >30, migraine, VTE/CVD risk, gallbladder disease, on enzyme inducers; oral estradiol 1–2 mg otherwise. Progestogen for endometrial protection if uterus: micronised progesterone (Utrogestan) 200 mg nocte 12 days/cycle (sequential, if periods within 12 months) or 100 mg daily (continuous combined, ≥12 months after LMP or ≥54), or LNG-IUS (Mirena, 5 years for HRT — also contraception), or combined patches/tablets. Start low; review at 3 months then annually (BP, weight, bleeding, breast awareness, symptoms); no arbitrary limit on duration — continue while benefits outweigh risks; taper or stop abruptly when stopping (same recurrence rate).
3. Vaginal oestrogen (estradiol 10 microgram pessary, estriol cream/gel, Gina OTC) for genitourinary syndrome — can be used long term, with or without systemic HRT, and in most women with breast cancer history (specialist advice). Vaginal moisturisers (Replens/YES), lubricants. Testosterone gel (Testogel/Tostran, ~5 mg/day off-label) for low libido after optimising HRT — check total testosterone baseline/3 months.

options.label: Risks, contraindications and bleeding on HRT
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breast cancer: oestrogen-only — little/no increase; combined HRT — small increase (about 4 extra cases per 1000 women over 5 years at 50–59, similar to 2 units alcohol/day or obesity), declining after stopping; micronised progesterone/dydrogesterone lower risk than synthetic progestogens. No increase in all-cause mortality in NG23 analyses. Contraindicated: current/past breast cancer (specialist), oestrogen-dependent cancer, undiagnosed PV bleeding, active VTE/thrombophilia (transdermal possible via haematology), active liver disease, uncontrolled hypertension (control first). Migraine with aura: transdermal OK. Diabetes, hypertension, previous MI/stroke: transdermal with specialist advice; starting <60 or within 10 years of menopause is cardioprotective/neutral.
2. VTE: oral HRT ~2× risk (absolute low); transdermal no increase — use transdermal in BMI >30, previous VTE, thrombophilia, smokers, immobility. Stroke: oral slight increase >60; transdermal none. Gallbladder disease: oral increases.
3. Bleeding on HRT: sequential — expect monthly withdrawal bleed; investigate if heavy, prolonged, >6 months of irregular bleeding, or bleeding after 6 months on continuous combined, or any bleeding after amenorrhoea on continuous combined → TVUSS (endometrial thickness threshold on HRT ~5 mm) ± hysteroscopy/biopsy; 2WW if ≥55 and postmenopausal bleeding not clearly HRT-related. Check adherence, missed progestogen, drug interactions (enzyme inducers, St John's wort), weight. Unscheduled bleeding in first 3–6 months is common — reassure and review.

options.label: Non-hormonal and lifestyle options
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle: regular exercise, weight management, reduce alcohol/caffeine/spicy food, layered clothing/fans, sleep hygiene, stop smoking; CBT (NG23 2024 — recommended for vasomotor symptoms, sleep and mood; group/online — Menopause: Stress, Mood etc.).
2. Drugs when HRT declined/contraindicated: fezolinetant 45 mg od (NICE TA1033 2024, neurokinin-3 antagonist — LFT monitoring); SSRI/SNRI — venlafaxine 37.5–75 mg, citalopram/escitalopram 10–20 mg, paroxetine 10 mg (avoid with tamoxifen), desvenlafaxine (not UK) — modest vasomotor benefit; gabapentin 300 mg nocte–900 mg/day (night sweats, sleep); clonidine 50–75 micrograms bd (limited, hypotension); oxybutynin 2.5–5 mg (off-label). Not recommended: black cohosh/isoflavones (unregulated, interactions), compounded 'bioidentical' hormones.
3. Breast cancer survivors: vaginal moisturisers first; low-dose vaginal oestrogen with oncology agreement (not with aromatase inhibitors without discussion); CBT, fezolinetant, venlafaxine/gabapentin for flushes. Bone health: calcium/vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, FRAX/DEXA if risk; HRT is first-line for osteoporosis prevention in women <60 with POI/early menopause.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Osteoporosis – fracture / DEXA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. FRAX; DEXA if indicated. Calcium + vitamin D. First-line: oral bisphosphonate (alendronate/risedronate); ensure correct administration. Consider IV zoledronate if oral not tolerated. NICE NG146, CKS.

options.label: Osteoporosis – denosumab / teriparatide
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Denosumab: 6-monthly SC; do not miss doses (rebound fracture risk). Monitor calcium/vitamin D. Teriparatide: specialist; limited duration. NICE NG146, CKS.

options.label: Osteomalacia / Paget's
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Osteomalacia: vitamin D repletion; treat cause. Paget's: refer or bisphosphonate per specialist. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Menstrual problems – dysmenorrhoea, PMS, IMB/PCB, amenorrhoea, adenomyosis

options.label: Dysmenorrhoea and adenomyosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Primary (onset 6–12 months after menarche, cramping with periods, normal examination): NSAID first line — ibuprofen 400 mg tds or naproxen 500 mg stat then 250 mg tds, or mefenamic acid 500 mg tds — started at onset/1 day before; paracetamol add-on; heat; TENS; combined hormonal contraception (continuous/extended), LNG-IUS, desogestrel or implant if contraception also wanted.
2. Secondary (onset after years of painless periods, pain before/throughout period, dyspareunia, heavy bleeding, bulky uterus): endometriosis (NG73 — transvaginal USS; refer gynaecology if suspected/not responding to 3–6 months of treatment; laparoscopy is diagnostic), adenomyosis (USS/MRI 'globular' uterus; LNG-IUS first line, CHC, tranexamic acid for bleeding, GnRH analogue via gynaecology; hysterectomy definitive), fibroids, PID (test chlamydia/gonorrhoea), copper IUD, cervical stenosis.
3. Refer: pain not controlled after 3–6 months of NSAID + hormonal therapy, suspected endometriosis/adenomyosis affecting fertility, abnormal examination/USS.

options.label: PMS / PMDD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnose with a prospective symptom diary over 2 cycles (symptoms in luteal phase, resolve by end of menstruation, symptom-free week). PMDD = severe with functional impairment; screen for depression/anxiety which worsen premenstrually (not the same).
2. Lifestyle: exercise, sleep, reduce alcohol/caffeine/smoking; CBT (first line for moderate PMS, RCOG); vitamin B6 ≤10 mg (MHRA limit), calcium/vitamin D.
3. Drug options: continuous or extended combined pill containing drospirenone (Yasmin/Lucette — licensed evidence) first-line hormonal; SSRI — sertraline 50–100 mg or fluoxetine 20 mg either continuously or luteal-phase only (day 14 to menses), effective within days; escitalopram 10–20 mg. Severe/refractory → gynaecology: GnRH analogue with add-back HRT, LNG-IUS + transdermal oestrogen, bilateral oophorectomy as last resort. Avoid progesterone-only treatments (worsen mood).

options.label: Intermenstrual / post-coital bleeding
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History: contraception (breakthrough bleeding common in first 3 months of CHC/POP/implant/IUS), missed pills, STI risk, smear status, pregnancy (test), anticoagulants. Examine: speculum (cervical ectropion, polyp, cervicitis, visible lesion), bimanual; swabs — chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT; smear only if due.
2. NG12: 2WW gynaecology if cervix looks suspicious (do not wait for smear); refer colposcopy for persistent PCB (>4 weeks) with normal-looking cervix in women ≥35 or with risk factors; endometrial cancer 2WW if ≥55 with postmenopausal bleeding (consider if <55); transvaginal USS for persistent IMB ≥45 or with risk factors (obesity, PCOS, tamoxifen, Lynch).
3. Benign: ectropion (reassure; cryotherapy/silver nitrate if troublesome), polyp (remove via gynaecology/hysteroscopy), infection (treat), hormonal contraception (change method if >3–6 months), perimenopausal anovulation (see HMB tool).

options.label: Amenorrhoea
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Primary: no menses by 15 with secondary sexual characteristics (or by 13 without) → FSH/LH, oestradiol, prolactin, TFT, karyotype (Turner's), pelvic USS (Müllerian agenesis, imperforate hymen); refer paediatric/adolescent gynaecology or endocrinology.
2. Secondary (≥3–6 months absent after previous cycles): PREGNANCY test first. Then: FSH/LH, oestradiol, prolactin, TFT, testosterone/SHBG/free androgen index, HbA1c; pelvic USS; ask about weight loss/exercise/eating disorder (functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea — low LH/FSH/oestradiol; restore energy balance; DEXA if >6 months), stress, drugs (antipsychotics → prolactin; depot medroxyprogesterone; opioids), hot flushes.
3. Causes and actions: PCOS (Rotterdam: oligo/anovulation + hyperandrogenism ± polycystic ovaries) — induce withdrawal bleed every 3–4 months (medroxyprogesterone 10 mg 10 days) or CHC/LNG-IUS to protect endometrium, metformin for metabolic features, weight, fertility (letrozole via gynaecology); hyperprolactinaemia (>1000 mU/L after repeat → pituitary MRI, endocrinology; cabergoline); premature ovarian insufficiency (<40, FSH >25 on two samples 4 weeks apart → HRT/CHC until 51, DEXA, fertility counselling, endocrinology/gynaecology); thyroid disease; Asherman's/cervical stenosis after instrumentation (hysteroscopy); hypopituitarism (Sheehan's).

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Management options
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm viability (USS if uncertain). Options: expectant (7–14 days), medical (misoprostol), or surgical (ERPC). Offer choice; support emotionally. Rh-negative: anti-D after 12 weeks or if surgical. NICE NG126, RCOG.

options.label: When to refer / emergency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: haemodynamically unstable, suspected ectopic (pain, bleeding, positive pregnancy test – refer same-day gynae). Recurrent miscarriage (≥3): refer for investigation. NICE NG126, NG12.

options.label: Benign Lumps (Indications for GP Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: Symptomatic (pain, inflammation, interference with function). 
2. Lipomas: Usually only if >5cm or rapidly growing (refer for US first to exclude sarcoma).
3. Sebaceous Cysts: Excise if recurrently infected (wait for infection to settle first).
4. Exclusions: Cosmetic removal is generally not routinely publicly funded.

options.label: Red Flags (Refer to 2WW / Plastic Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Changing Naevi: Refer to 2WW Dermatology.
2. Irregular, fixed, or hard masses: Urgent referral.
3. Note: Never excise a lesion where malignancy is suspected in primary care minor surgery clinic.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rotterdam criteria; exclude thyroid, prolactin, NCAH. NICE NG38, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle; metformin if metabolic need; COCP for cycle/androgen; fertility referral if trying to conceive. NICE NG38.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rotterdam criteria; exclude thyroid, prolactin, NCAH. NICE NG38, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle; metformin if metabolic need; COCP for cycle/androgen; fertility referral if trying to conceive. NICE NG38.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rotterdam criteria; exclude thyroid, prolactin, NCAH. NICE NG38, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle; metformin if metabolic need; COCP for cycle/androgen; fertility referral if trying to conceive. NICE NG38.

options.label: Diagnosis & treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider PID if pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness/adnexal tenderness. Screen: chlamydia, gonorrhoea (NAAT); MSU if UTI possible. Treat: ofloxacin 400 mg bd 14 days + metronidazole 400 mg bd 14 days (or doxycycline 100 mg bd 14 days + metronidazole). Contact tracing. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: When to refer / admit
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit if: severe illness, tubo-ovarian abscess, pregnancy, or no response to oral therapy. 2WW: if cancer suspected. IUD: consider removal after 24–48 h of antibiotics. NICE NG3, NG12.

options.label: Diagnosis & treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider PID if pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness/adnexal tenderness. Screen: chlamydia, gonorrhoea (NAAT); MSU if UTI possible. Treat: ofloxacin 400 mg bd 14 days + metronidazole 400 mg bd 14 days (or doxycycline 100 mg bd 14 days + metronidazole). Contact tracing. NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: When to refer / admit
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit if: severe illness, tubo-ovarian abscess, pregnancy, or no response to oral therapy. 2WW: if cancer suspected. IUD: consider removal after 24–48 h of antibiotics. NICE NG3, NG12.

options.label: 2WW referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Any vaginal bleeding in a woman who is postmenopausal (no period ≥12 months) or unexpected bleeding on HRT: urgent 2WW gynaecology for transvaginal US ± hysteroscopy/biopsy.
2. Do not attribute to atrophy without investigation. Endometrial thickness >4 mm on US in PMB requires biopsy. NICE NG12, RCOG, CKS.

options.label: On HRT – expected vs unexpected
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sequential HRT: withdrawal bleed is expected. Unexpected bleeding (heavy, intermenstrual, or after 12 months amenorrhoea on continuous): 2WW.
2. Continuous combined: any bleeding after 6 months – investigate (2WW). NICE NG23, NG12.

options.label: Holistic Consultant Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Biological**: Antidepressants (SSRIs 1st-line) + optimize physical health (sleep/exercise/thyroid).
2. **Psychological**: Evidence-based CBT, IPT, or Psychodynamic therapy. Strategy is to change cognitive distorting loops.
3. **Social**: Stabilize housing, employment, and social isolation. Review significant relational stressors.
4. **Remission Goal**: Total symptomatic relief, not just improvement. Continue meds for 6-12 months post-recovery. NICE NG222.

options.label: MDD Diagnosis (DSM-5 / PHQ-9)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Core: ≥5 of 9 symptoms for ≥2 weeks. Must include Mood or Anhedonia.
2. Severity Stratification: 
   - Mild: PHQ-9 10-14. 
   - Moderate: PHQ-9 15-19.
   - Severe: PHQ-9 ≥20 OR presence of psychotic features (delusions of guilt/poverty).
3. Risk: Mandatory assessment of suicide/self-harm intent and access to means. NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 1 & 2: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Choice: SSRI (Sertraline 50-200mg or Fluoxetine 20-40mg). 
2. Monitoring: Review in 1-2 weeks. Full effect takes 4-6 weeks at therapeutic dose.
3. Adjunct: High-intensity CBT or IPT (Interpersonal Therapy). NICE NG222.

options.label: Step 3: Treatment Resistance (TRD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Definition: Failure of ≥2 adequate trials of different antidepressant classes.
2. Switch: Transition to SNRI (Venlafaxine MR 75-375mg) OR NASSA (Mirtazapine 15-45mg).
3. Augmentation: 
   - Lithium (Level 0.6-0.8 mmol/L).
   - Atypical Antipsychotic (Quetiapine 150-300mg or Aripiprazole 2.5-5mg).
4. ECT: Urgent specialist referral if life-threatening (catatonia, severe food/fluid refusal). NICE NG222.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

options.label: First Seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Urgency: Refer to 'First Seizure Clinic' (within 2 weeks). NICE NG217.
2. Investigation: EEG + MRI Brain (Standard protocol including coronal T2/FLAIR sessions). 
3. Safety: High-risk activities (driving, swimming, working at heights) must stop until specialist review.

options.label: Focal Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Lamotrigine or Levetiracetam (Keppra). NICE NG217.

options.label: Generalized Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Sodium Valproate (Epilim) - **Strict warning: Not for use in women/girls of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place.**
2. Alternative: Levetiracetam or Lamotrigine.

options.label: Stage 1 (Clinic ≥140/90, Home ≥135/85)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Diagnosis):
1. Confirm with HBPM (average of 4-7 days) or ABPM.
2. Targets: <140/90 clinic (<135/85 home) if age <80. <150/90 clinic (<145/85 home) if age ≥80.
3. Offer drug treatment if: Target organ damage, CVD, Real disease, Diabetes, or QRISK3 ≥10%. NICE NG136.

options.label: Stage 2 (Clinic ≥160/100, Home ≥150/95)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Treat all patients regardless of age or CVD risk.
2. Review for target-organ damage (ECG, U&E, Albumin:Creatinine Ratio).
3. Recheck BP in 1-2 weeks. NICE NG136.

options.label: Accelerated / Severe (≥180/120)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Check for papilloedema and new-onset confusion (Hypertensive Crisis).
2. Same-day specialist referral if signs of crisis or retinal haemorrhage.
3. If no complications, start treatment immediately. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age < 55 (Non-Black African/Caribbean)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor (e.g. Ramipril 2.5mg-10mg OD) or ARB (e.g. Losartan 50mg-100mg OD).
2. Monitor: U&E before and 1-2 weeks after starting/increasing dose. NICE NG136.

options.label: Age ≥ 55 OR Black African/Caribbean (any age)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CCB (Calcium Channel Blocker) e.g. Amlodipine 5mg-10mg OD.
2. If CCB not tolerated (edema), use Thiazide-like diuretic (e.g. Indapamide 2.5mg OD). NICE NG136.

options.label: Type 2 Diabetes (Any age/ethnicity)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACE inhibitor or ARB (regardless of age or ethnicity). NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 2 (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. (A + C) OR (A + D).
2. A = ACEi/ARB. C = CCB. D = Diuretic (e.g. Indapamide).
3. If CCB not tolerated, use D. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 3 (Triple Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. A + C + D.
2. Ensure all at optimal-tolerated doses before proceeding to Step 4. NICE NG136.

options.label: Step 4 (Resistant Hypertension)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Review adherence/White-coat effect.
2. Check K+.
3. If K+ ≤ 4.5: Add Spironolactone 25mg OD (monitor U&E carefully).
4. If K+ > 4.5: Add Alpha-blocker (Doxazosin) or Beta-blocker. NICE NG136.

options.label: Symptomatic relief
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify cause (GI, drugs, vestibular, metabolic, CNS). Cyclizine 50 mg tds or prochlorperazine 5 mg tds; metoclopramide 10 mg tds (avoid if young or parkinsonism).
2. Red flags: Headache, abdominal pain, dehydration – assess and refer as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit: Severe dehydration, suspected bowel obstruction, head injury, raised ICP. 2WW: Unexplained persistent nausea/vomiting with weight loss.
2. Pregnancy: Exclude hyperemesis; treat and refer if severe. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: TSH >10
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Overt hypothyroidism. Start levothyroxine 25–50 mcg OD (lower if elderly/cardiac). Recheck TSH in 6–8 weeks; titrate to TSH 0.4–2.0. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH 4.5–10, normal T4
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check TPO antibodies. Consider trial of levothyroxine if symptomatic or TPO+ or TSH >10. NICE NG145.

options.label: TSH <0.1 / hyperthyroid
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check T4/T3. Refer endocrinology (Graves, nodule, thyroiditis). If on levothyroxine: reduce dose. NICE NG145.

options.label: Pregnancy / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pregnancy: Aim TSH <2.5 in first trimester; levothyroxine often increased. Check TFT each trimester. 2. Refer: Thyroid nodule, ophthalmopathy, amiodarone-induced, resistance. NICE NG145, CKS.

tools.title: Pregnancy in general practice – early pregnancy, hyperemesis, antenatal care, pre-eclampsia, VTE, mental health, postnatal bleeding
niceRefs: NICE NG126 Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage
NICE CG192 Antenatal and postnatal mental health

options.label: Early pregnancy bleeding / pain — ectopic and miscarriage
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Any woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain, shoulder-tip pain, collapse, or PV bleeding → pregnancy test. Positive test + pain or bleeding (or risk: previous ectopic, tubal surgery, IUD, IVF, PID) → refer EARLY PREGNANCY ASSESSMENT UNIT (same day if pain, haemodynamically unstable, shoulder-tip pain, or >6 weeks; 999 if collapse/severe pain). Do NOT do a bimanual to 'check for ectopic'.
2. NG126: EPAU does TVUSS ± serial hCG (48 h rise <63% suggests ectopic/non-viable); ectopic — expectant (hCG <1000 falling), methotrexate 50 mg/m² IM (hCG <1500–5000, no pain, unruptured, able to follow up; avoid conception 3 months), or laparoscopic salpingectomy/salpingotomy. Anti-D 250 IU for rhesus-negative women after surgical management (not for threatened/complete miscarriage <12 weeks or medical management).
3. Miscarriage: expectant (7–14 days), medical (misoprostol 800 micrograms PV/oral ± mifepristone 200 mg 48 h before — NG126 2023 update), or surgical (MVA/ERPC); bleeding/pain advice, pregnancy test 3 weeks after; Miscarriage Association support; recurrent (≥3) → recurrent miscarriage clinic (antiphospholipid antibodies, karyotype, pelvic USS).

options.label: Hyperemesis and antenatal care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nausea/vomiting of pregnancy (PUQE score): first line — ginger, acupressure, small frequent meals; antiemetics (RCOG/UKTIS): cyclizine 50 mg tds, prochlorperazine 5–10 mg tds (buccal 3–6 mg bd), promethazine 25 mg nocte, or doxylamine/pyridoxine (Xonvea) 10/10 mg; second line metoclopramide 10 mg tds (max 5 days) or ondansetron 4–8 mg bd–tds (small orofacial cleft risk <10 weeks — informed decision); third line prednisolone (specialist). Hyperemesis gravidarum (weight loss >5%, ketonuria, dehydration, electrolyte disturbance) → day-unit/admission for IV fluids (Hartmann's/saline + KCl, NOT dextrose first), thiamine (Wernicke's prevention), VTE prophylaxis; check TFT (gestational thyrotoxicosis), USS (molar/multiple). PPI/H2RA for reflux. Pregnancy Sickness Support.
2. Booking (NG201): by 10 weeks — refer to midwife at first contact; folic acid 400 micrograms (5 mg if previous NTD, diabetes, epilepsy, BMI ≥30, sickle/thalassaemia, antiepileptics) until 12 weeks; vitamin D 10 micrograms throughout; stop smoking/alcohol; review medications (stop ACE-i/ARB, statins, warfarin→LMWH, valproate/topiramate, methotrexate, isotretinoin, lithium with specialist); aspirin 75–150 mg from 12 weeks if pre-eclampsia risk (see below); screening offered — bloods (FBC, group/antibodies, HIV, hepatitis B, syphilis, haemoglobinopathy), combined screening 11–14 weeks, anomaly scan 18–20+6, gestational diabetes OGTT 24–28 weeks if risk (BMI ≥30, previous GDM/macrosomia, family history, South Asian/Black Caribbean/Middle Eastern). Vaccines: pertussis from 16 weeks, influenza, COVID, RSV from 28 weeks (2024). Antenatal infections: asymptomatic bacteriuria MSU at booking (treat — nitrofurantoin avoid at term, trimethoprim avoid first trimester); chickenpox/parvovirus/rubella contact → check serology; listeria/toxoplasma food advice; group B strep — no routine screening; genital herpes first episode in third trimester → GUM/obstetrics (aciclovir, consider CS).

options.label: Pre-eclampsia, VTE, mental health, postnatal bleeding
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pre-eclampsia (NG133): new hypertension ≥140/90 after 20 weeks with proteinuria (ACR ≥8 mg/mmol or PCR ≥30) or organ dysfunction; symptoms — headache, visual disturbance, epigastric/RUQ pain, oedema, reduced fetal movements. SAME-DAY obstetric assessment (maternity triage) for BP ≥140/90 with proteinuria or symptoms; ≥160/110 is severe → urgent admission (labetalol 200 mg oral, or nifedipine MR). Aspirin 75–150 mg nightly from 12 weeks for high risk (previous pre-eclampsia, chronic hypertension, CKD, diabetes, autoimmune disease) or ≥2 moderate factors (first pregnancy, age ≥40, BMI ≥35, family history, multiple pregnancy, interval >10 years). Chronic hypertension: labetalol/nifedipine/methyldopa (stop methyldopa within 2 days postnatal — depression). Postnatal: BP check day 3–5 and 2 weeks; pre-eclampsia doubles later cardiovascular risk — annual BP, lifestyle.
2. VTE (RCOG 37a): assess risk at booking, each admission and postnatally; LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg od; weight-adjusted) antenatally if score ≥4 (≥3 from 28 weeks), 6 weeks postnatal if ≥2 or caesarean/other risk; previous VTE → LMWH throughout + 6 weeks. Suspected DVT/PE in pregnancy → same-day obstetric/medical assessment (D-dimer unreliable; duplex/CTPA or V/Q); start LMWH while awaiting imaging. Warfarin and DOACs contraindicated.
3. Mental health (CG192): ask about mood/anxiety at booking and postnatally (Whooley questions, EPDS); previous bipolar/psychosis/severe depression → refer perinatal mental health team pre-conception/at booking (postpartum psychosis risk 25–50%); suicidal ideation, psychosis, thoughts of harming baby, rapid deterioration → same-day perinatal/crisis team. Medication: sertraline preferred SSRI in pregnancy/breastfeeding; do not stop antidepressants abruptly; lithium/valproate — specialist; CBT/IAPT fast-track for perinatal women. Postnatal depression: EPDS ≥13 → treat (CBT, sertraline), health visitor, partner support.
4. Secondary postpartum haemorrhage (abnormal/excessive bleeding 24 h–12 weeks after birth): endometritis (offensive lochia, fever, tender uterus — co-amoxiclav 625 mg tds 7 days, or clindamycin + gentamicin if admitted) or retained products (USS — ERPC); heavy bleeding/unwell → same-day maternity assessment/999 if soaking pads hourly or faint. Also: perineal wound infection, mastitis, VTE, pre-eclampsia up to 6 weeks, anaemia (ferritin; iron), contraception from day 21 (LARC; avoid CHC <6 weeks if breastfeeding or VTE risk), 6–8 week check (mood, BP, contraception, smear if due, pelvic floor).

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Low Risk (Green)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Safety-netting and follow-up. Provide written instructions on when to seek help. NICE NG51.

options.label: High Risk (Amber/Red)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
999 Ambulance. NEWS2 score calculation. ABCDE assessment. O2 to target 94-98%. IV access. Pre-hospital antibiotics if >1h from hospital. NICE NG51.

options.label: Candida (thrush)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical clotrimazole (e.g. 10% 1 applicator nocte 1–3 nights) or fluconazole 150 mg single dose. Recurrent (≥4/year): prolong treatment; consider maintenance fluconazole; screen for diabetes. Avoid in pregnancy (topical only). NICE CKS.

options.label: Bacterial vaginosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Metronidazole 400 mg bd 5–7 days or 2 g single dose. Alternative: intravaginal clindamycin. Treat in pregnancy if symptomatic (reduces late miscarriage/PTB). Avoid alcohol with metronidazole. NICE CKS, NG3.

options.label: Trichomonas
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Metronidazole 400 mg bd 5–7 days (or 2 g stat). Sexual contacts: test and treat. Refer if pregnant (discuss treatment). NICE NG3, CKS.

options.label: When to refer / 2WW
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 2WW: Postmenopausal bleeding, cervical concern, suspected cancer. Refer if recurrent/persistent, pregnant, diagnostic uncertainty, or pelvic pain (exclude PID). NICE NG12, CKS.

tools.title: Vaginal discharge and STIs – chlamydia, gonorrhoea, BV, trichomonas, candidiasis
niceRefs: BASHH guidelines (chlamydia 2018/2023, gonorrhoea 2019, BV 2022, TV 2021, VVC 2019)

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History: colour/odour/itch, new partner, condom use, symptoms in partner, contraception, pregnancy, douching, last smear, abdominal pain/dyspareunia/fever (PID — see below). Examine if symptoms persistent, pain, PCB/IMB, pregnancy, or age <25 with risk (speculum, bimanual, pH of discharge).
2. Tests: self-taken vulvovaginal swab NAAT for chlamydia + gonorrhoea (first-void urine in men); high vaginal swab (charcoal) for BV/TV/candida only if symptoms atypical/recurrent/pregnant; HIV + syphilis serology with any STI (window: HIV 45 days 4th-gen, syphilis 12 weeks). Offer full screen at GUM/sexual health (also hepatitis B/C if risk, rectal/pharyngeal swabs by exposure). Mycoplasma genitalium NAAT if urethritis/PID/PCB not explained.
3. Pattern: thin grey fishy (pH >4.5) = BV; frothy yellow-green, itch, strawberry cervix = trichomonas; thick white curdy, itch, pH <4.5 = candida; mucopurulent cervicitis/PCB = chlamydia/gonorrhoea; physiological — clear/white, no odour, cyclical.
4. PID (lower abdominal pain, deep dyspareunia, cervical motion tenderness, discharge, fever): swabs then treat empirically WITHOUT waiting — ceftriaxone 1 g IM stat + doxycycline 100 mg bd 14 days + metronidazole 400 mg bd 14 days; admit if pregnant, severe, tubo-ovarian abscess, or not improving 72 h; remove IUD only if no improvement; partner treatment.

options.label: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chlamydia: doxycycline 100 mg bd for 7 days (first line, also covers M. genitalium poorly — avoid azithromycin single dose now except pregnancy). Pregnancy/breastfeeding: azithromycin 1 g stat then 500 mg od 2 days (or amoxicillin 500 mg tds 7 days; erythromycin). Test of cure only in pregnancy, rectal infection, or persistent symptoms (at ≥3 weeks). Re-test at 3 months (reinfection). Abstain 7 days after both partners treated. Partner notification (all partners in 6 months) — GUM/health adviser; opportunistic screening <25.
2. Gonorrhoea: ceftriaxone 1 g IM stat (if sensitivities unknown); ciprofloxacin 500 mg stat only if cipro-sensitive on culture. ALWAYS take culture (charcoal swab) before treatment for resistance; test of cure for ALL at 2 weeks (NAAT) — BASHH; refer to GUM preferably (resistance surveillance, pharyngeal/rectal sites, partner notification). Disseminated (arthritis, pustular rash) → admit.
3. Notify HIV/syphilis results; hepatitis B vaccination for MSM/risk; advise condoms; consider PrEP referral for HIV-negative at ongoing risk.

options.label: BV, trichomonas, candidiasis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. BV (treat if symptomatic, pregnant with symptoms, or before gynaecological procedures/TOP): metronidazole 400 mg bd 5–7 days (or 2 g stat — not in pregnancy), or metronidazole 0.75% vaginal gel od 5 days, or clindamycin 2% cream nocte 7 days; avoid alcohol with metronidazole; avoid douching/scented products. Recurrent (≥4/year): confirm diagnosis, treat, then suppressive metronidazole gel twice weekly for 4–6 months (BASHH), consider lactic acid gel/probiotics (weak evidence), change contraception from copper IUD; partners not treated (male).
2. Trichomonas (STI): metronidazole 400 mg bd 5–7 days (or 2 g stat; 2 g avoided in pregnancy — 400 mg bd); treat partner; test of cure not routine; full STI screen; GUM referral for partner notification.
3. Candidiasis: clotrimazole 500 mg pessary stat (or 200 mg 3 nights) ± clotrimazole 1% cream for vulva, or fluconazole 150 mg oral stat (not pregnancy — use topical 7 days). Avoid tight synthetic clothing, soaps; manage diabetes, antibiotics. RECURRENT (≥4 episodes/year, confirmed by culture): induction fluconazole 150 mg every 72 h ×3 then maintenance 150 mg weekly for 6 months (BASHH); check HbA1c, HIV, iron; non-albicans (C. glabrata) → GUM — nystatin pessaries 14 days/boric acid; consider stopping oestrogen-containing contraception; no need to treat asymptomatic partners.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Lichen planus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Topical potent steroid (e.g. betamethasone) for limited disease. Mouth: topical steroid or specialist.
2. Refer if widespread, genital, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE CKS.

options.label: Lichen sclerosus
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Potent topical steroid (e.g. clobetasol) initially; reduce to maintenance. Long-term follow-up (malignancy risk).
2. Refer if diagnostic uncertainty or not responding. NICE CKS.

options.label: Small / fluctuant
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Incision and drainage; send pus if recurrent or cellulitis. Do not use antibiotic alone for uncomplicated abscess.
2. Consider flucloxacillin if cellulitis or systemic symptoms. NICE NG141.

options.label: Recurrent boils
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hygiene; nasal decolonisation (mupirocin) if nasal carriage. Screen household. Consider referral if persistent. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Addressing vaccine hesitancy in primary care – Management

options.label: Support
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Listen; address concerns with evidence. Offer reliable resources (PHE, national). No coercion.
2. Document; offer catch-up. NICE CKS, PHE Green Book.

tools.title: Bites – animal and human
niceRefs: NICE CKS Bites – human and animal

options.label: Wound care and assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Irrigate thoroughly with warm running water/saline; remove foreign material; do not close puncture wounds or hand bites primarily. Assess depth, tendon/joint/bone involvement, neurovascular status. X-ray if fracture, foreign body (tooth) or joint involvement suspected.
2. Tetanus: give booster (Td/IPV) if >10 years since last dose or incomplete course; tetanus immunoglobulin if high-risk wound and incomplete immunisation.
3. Rabies: any bite abroad in a rabies-endemic country, or any bat contact in the UK → same-day UKHSA advice for post-exposure vaccine ± immunoglobulin.
4. Human bite: assess blood-borne virus risk (hepatitis B vaccination/HBIG, HIV PEP if source high-risk — see Needlestick); consider safeguarding/assault documentation.

options.label: Antibiotics
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cat bite or human bite that has broken skin and drawn blood: prophylactic antibiotics. Dog bite: prophylaxis only if broken skin AND (drawn blood, deep/puncture, hand/foot/face/genitals, prosthetic joint/valve, immunosuppressed, diabetes, asplenia, cirrhosis).
2. First line: co-amoxiclav 625 mg tds for 3 days (prophylaxis) or 5–7 days (infected). Penicillin allergy: doxycycline 200 mg stat then 100 mg bd + metronidazole 400 mg tds. Children: co-amoxiclav by weight; co-trimoxazole + metronidazole if allergic.
3. Review at 24–48 h for hand bites and infected wounds.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same day plastics/orthopaedics/ED: hand or face bites with tendon/joint involvement, deep puncture, devitalised tissue, foreign body, spreading infection, systemic illness, immunosuppressed, bites to genitals, uncontrolled bleeding.
2. Plastics: cosmetic facial wounds needing closure (within 24 h).
3. Infection not responding at 48 h → admit for IV antibiotics.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: First episode
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stop precipitant antibiotic(s) if possible. Oral vancomycin 125 mg qds 10 days or fidaxomicin 200 mg bd 10 days (fidaxomicin preferred if first recurrence or high risk). Avoid antimotility agents. NICE NG199, CKS.
2. Isolate; hand hygiene. Repeat toxin test only if relapse. NICE NG199.

options.label: Recurrence
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First recurrence: fidaxomicin 200 mg bd 10 days (or vancomycin). Multiple recurrences: consider vancomycin taper (e.g. pulse/taper regimen) or fidaxomicin. Refer if refractory. Bezlotoxumab (monoclonal) may be considered in selected cases (specialist). NICE NG199, CKS.

options.label: Mild / moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Flucloxacillin 500 mg qds 7 days (clarithromycin if penicillin allergic). Elevate limb; mark margin; review at 48 h.
2. Consider CRP if diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG141, CKS.

options.label: Severe / facial / systemic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit for IV antibiotics if systemically unwell, facial cellulitis, or rapid spread. Blood culture if febrile. NICE NG141.

options.label: Periorbital / orbital / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Periorbital: Swelling limited to lids; oral antibiotics; same-day review if worsening.
2. Orbital: Proptosis, limited eye movement, vision change – admit urgently (ophthalmology/ENT). Do not confuse with periorbital. NICE NG141.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

options.label: Immunocompetent adults
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Both cause a glandular-fever-like illness (fever, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, atypical lymphocytes, mild hepatitis) with negative monospot. Tests: CMV IgM/IgG (± avidity), toxoplasma IgM/IgG (IgG avidity to time infection), LFT, FBC/film, EBV serology, HIV test.
2. Management supportive — no antivirals in immunocompetent adults; toxoplasma chorioretinitis or severe disease → ophthalmology/ID (pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + folinic acid, or co-trimoxazole).
3. Toxoplasma exposure advice: avoid undercooked meat, wash fruit/veg, gloves for gardening/cat litter.

options.label: Pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Primary CMV in pregnancy (commonest congenital infection): if suspected (seroconversion, symptoms, fetal USS findings) → refer fetal medicine urgently; high-dose valaciclovir 8 g/day in first trimester seroconversion reduces transmission (specialist); amniocentesis for fetal PCR after 21 weeks. Hygiene advice for all pregnant women with toddlers: hand washing after nappies/saliva contact, do not share utensils.
2. Toxoplasmosis in pregnancy: confirm with reference lab (IgG avidity); spiramycin 1 g tds to reduce transmission until fetal infection excluded; if fetal infection (amniotic PCR) — pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine/folinic acid from 18 weeks; fetal medicine.
3. Congenital CMV in neonate: urine/saliva CMV PCR within 21 days of birth; valganciclovir 6 months for symptomatic infants (hearing/neurology) — paediatric ID.

options.label: Immunocompromised
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HIV (CD4 <50–100), transplant, chemotherapy: CMV retinitis (floaters, visual loss → same-day ophthalmology; valganciclovir 900 mg bd induction), colitis, pneumonitis, encephalitis; toxoplasma encephalitis (focal neurology, seizures, ring-enhancing lesions → emergency admission; pyrimethamine/sulfadiazine or co-trimoxazole).
2. Prophylaxis: co-trimoxazole 480–960 mg od for toxoplasma-seropositive HIV patients with CD4 <200; CMV monitoring/pre-emptive valganciclovir per transplant protocol. All managed with the specialist team; GP checks FBC (neutropenia on valganciclovir).

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Bacterial conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds (max 5 days). Fusidic acid 1% if pregnant. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day. RCOphth; NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected corneal ulcer / Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Contact lens wear? Pain, photophobia? Same-day ophthalmology. Stop contact lenses. Do not use steroid. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Scleritis (deep boring pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Deep scleral pain; systemic associations (rheumatoid, ANCA). Same-day ophthalmology. Urgent within 24 h. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Acute uveitis / Angle-closure glaucoma
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Uveitis: ciliary flush, small pupil – same-day ophthalmology (steroid + dilating drops specialist). Angle-closure: pain, hard globe, nausea – emergency; acetazolamide if remote. RCOphth; NICE NG81.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: pain, photophobia, reduced vision, contact lens wear, trauma, chemical. Avoid topical steroid until cause known. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Antiviral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or remdesivir for highest-risk if within 5 days. Follow local protocol. NICE NG159, CKS.

options.label: 1. Assessment & red flags
options.guidance:
ASSESSMENT:
• History: travel, contacts, animals, bites, immunosuppression, recent antibiotics. Severity and focus of infection. Screening: age-appropriate programmes (cancer, CVD, diabetic eye).
• Examination: focus (skin, chest, abdomen); sepsis screening (NEWS2, qSOFA).
• Red flags: Sepsis, meningitis, non-blanching rash – emergency. HIV/TB risk – test and refer. NICE NG51, NG33, NG12.

options.label: 2. Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT:
• Sepsis: immediate antibiotic per NG51; fluid; emergency referral. CAP: CURB-65; amoxicillin 5 days (low risk). Cellulitis: flucloxacillin; mark margin; admit if severe. Use local resistance data; 5-day courses. NICE NG138, NG141.
• HIV: test; PrEP/PEP per NG122. TB: refer TB service. C. difficile: stop precipitant antibiotic; vancomycin or fidaxomicin. NICE NG199, NG33.
• Viral: no antibiotic for cold, sinusitis <10 days, acute bronchitis. Influenza: oseltamivir if at-risk and <48 h. NICE NG84, NG120.

options.label: 3. Referral & screening
options.guidance:
REFERRAL:
• Emergency: Sepsis, meningitis, severe infection, necrotising fasciitis. NICE NG51.
• 2WW: HIV positive, TB suspected. Routine: Recurrent infection, HIV management, travel medicine. NICE NG33.
• Screening: Bowel (FIT 56–74), breast (50–71), cervical (25–64). CVD: NHS Health Check 40–74; QRISK3. Diabetic retinopathy: annual. AAA: men 65. NICE NG12, CG181.

tools.title: Fever in the returning traveller – dengue, typhoid and other imported infections
niceRefs: NICE CKS Fever in returning travellers (via UKHSA/NaTHNaC)

options.label: First actions — exclude malaria
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Fever within 12 months of travel to the tropics = MALARIA until proven otherwise: same-day blood film ×3 (and rapid antigen) via ED/acute medicine; do not wait for GP results if unwell. Falciparum can kill within 24–48 h.
2. Also same day: FBC, U&E, LFT, CRP, blood cultures, urinalysis, glucose; dengue NS1/PCR, typhoid cultures (blood ± stool), HIV test. Ask: countries, dates, rural/urban, mosquito bites, food/water, freshwater exposure, animal contact, sexual contact, vaccinations/prophylaxis, onset relative to return (incubation).
3. Admit if unwell, bleeding, dehydration, confusion, jaundice, pregnancy, or any positive malaria test. Notifiable diseases: malaria, typhoid, dengue (suspected), leptospirosis, brucellosis.

options.label: Arboviruses — dengue, chikungunya, Zika
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dengue (S/SE Asia, Americas, Africa; incubation 4–10 days): fever, severe myalgia/'breakbone', retro-orbital headache, rash day 3–5, thrombocytopenia, raised ALT. Supportive: paracetamol, oral fluids — AVOID NSAIDs/aspirin (bleeding). WARNING signs (days 3–7, as fever settles): abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, bleeding, lethargy, fluid accumulation, rising haematocrit with falling platelets → admit (dengue shock). Daily FBC until recovery.
2. Chikungunya: fever + severe symmetrical polyarthralgia (hands/feet), may persist months; supportive, NSAIDs once dengue excluded; rheumatology if chronic arthritis.
3. Zika: mild rash/conjunctivitis/arthralgia; PREGNANCY — fetal microcephaly risk: refer obstetrics/fetal medicine; avoid conception for 2 months (women) / 3 months (men) after travel; barrier contraception. Testing via UKHSA RIPL.

options.label: Bacterial — typhoid, leptospirosis, brucellosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Typhoid/paratyphoid (South Asia; incubation 6–30 days): sustained fever, headache, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhoea, relative bradycardia, rose spots, leucopenia. Blood cultures before antibiotics; treat in secondary care/ID: IV ceftriaxone 2 g od (fluoroquinolone resistance in South Asia; azithromycin 500 mg–1 g od 7 days for uncomplicated oral treatment). Exclude from food handling until clearance stools.
2. Leptospirosis (freshwater exposure, rats, Weil's disease): fever, myalgia (calves), conjunctival suffusion, jaundice, AKI, haemorrhage; serology/PCR via UKHSA; doxycycline 100 mg bd 7 days (mild) or IV benzylpenicillin/ceftriaxone (admit if jaundice/AKI). Prophylaxis doxycycline 200 mg weekly for high-risk exposure.
3. Brucellosis (unpasteurised dairy, Middle East/Mediterranean): undulant fever, sweats, arthralgia, sacroiliitis, epididymo-orchitis; serology; doxycycline 100 mg bd 6 weeks + rifampicin 600–900 mg od 6 weeks (or + gentamicin/streptomycin) — ID-led. Notify.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Score 0–1 (no antibiotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol/NSAID. No antibiotic. Safety-net: if worsening or no improvement in 1 week, re-assess. NICE NG84.

options.label: Score 2–3+ (antibiotic)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg qds 5–10 days (or clarithromycin if penicillin allergic). Do not use amoxicillin if glandular fever suspected (rash). NICE NG84.

options.label: Glandular fever / quinsy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Glandular fever: supportive; avoid amoxicillin (rash). Consider monospot/EBV serology if prolonged or diagnostic uncertainty.
2. Quinsy (peritonsillar abscess): admit for drainage; do not manage in primary care. Stridor or severe dysphagia – urgent. NICE NG84, CKS.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recurrent tonsillitis: refer per local criteria (e.g. ≥7 in 1 year, ≥5/year for 2 years). 2WW: hoarseness >3 weeks, suspected cancer. Quinsy, stridor – urgent. NICE NG84, NG12.

tools.title: Helicobacter pylori – testing and eradication
niceRefs: NICE CKS Dyspepsia – proven GORD/unidentified cause

options.label: Testing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Test and treat for uninvestigated dyspepsia without alarm features (after 4 weeks PPI trial or first line if high-prevalence background), proven peptic ulcer, MALT lymphoma, before long-term NSAID, unexplained iron deficiency after GI work-up, ITP.
2. Test: carbon-13 urea breath test or stool antigen — patient must be OFF PPI for 2 weeks and antibiotics for 4 weeks. Serology not recommended (remains positive after cure).
3. Retest for eradication (breath test, 4 weeks post-treatment) only if: ulcer, MALT lymphoma, persistent symptoms, family history gastric cancer, or patient preference.

options.label: First-line eradication (7 days, all tds bd as listed)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. PPI (omeprazole 20 mg bd / lansoprazole 30 mg bd / esomeprazole 20 mg bd) + amoxicillin 1 g bd + clarithromycin 500 mg bd OR metronidazole 400 mg bd — choose metronidazole if clarithromycin exposure in past year, clarithromycin if metronidazole exposure.
2. Penicillin allergy: PPI + clarithromycin 500 mg bd + metronidazole 400 mg bd. Penicillin allergy with prior clarithromycin: PPI + bismuth subsalicylate 525 mg qds + metronidazole 400 mg bd + tetracycline 500 mg qds (bismuth quadruple).
3. Counsel: adherence (failure usually = resistance or non-adherence), metallic taste, avoid alcohol with metronidazole, diarrhoea; interactions — clarithromycin with statins (hold simvastatin), warfarin, DOACs.

options.label: Second line and failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Second line (7 days): PPI + amoxicillin 1 g bd + whichever of clarithromycin/metronidazole was NOT used first; if both used before: PPI + amoxicillin + levofloxacin 250 mg bd (or tetracycline 500 mg qds). Penicillin allergy: PPI + metronidazole + levofloxacin; or bismuth quadruple.
2. Third line: refer gastroenterology for culture-guided therapy (OGD with biopsies for sensitivities); rifabutin-based regimen by specialist.
3. Persistent symptoms after confirmed eradication → manage as functional dyspepsia; OGD if alarm features (dysphagia, weight loss, haematemesis, anaemia, age ≥55 with persistent symptoms — NG12).

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CKS / BNF / named guideline)

options.label: Diagnosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Prodrome (malaise, nausea, anorexia, fever) then jaundice, dark urine, pale stool, RUQ pain; ALT often >1000. Hepatitis A: travel, shellfish, MSM, outbreaks, household contact (incubation 2–6 weeks). Hepatitis E: UK pork products (genotype 3 — autochthonous, older men), travel (genotype 1), may be anicteric; neurological complications (Guillain–Barré, neuralgic amyotrophy).
2. Tests: LFT, INR, FBC, U&E, hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis E IgM/IgG + HEV RNA, hepatitis B surface antigen/core IgM, hepatitis C antibody, EBV/CMV, paracetamol level if relevant, autoimmune screen if persisting. Both are NOTIFIABLE on suspicion (UKHSA arranges contact prophylaxis).

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive: rest, fluids, antiemetics (cyclizine), avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic drugs (review paracetamol dose ≤2 g/day, statins, methotrexate); itch — chlorphenamine/colestyramine. Most recover in 2–8 weeks; hepatitis A never chronic; hepatitis E chronic only if immunosuppressed (ribavirin via hepatology).
2. Hygiene: hand washing, no food handling/preparation for others until 1 week after jaundice onset; exclude from school/work 7 days from onset.
3. Repeat LFT/INR weekly until improving; check pregnancy (hepatitis E in pregnancy carries 20% mortality in genotype 1 — specialist care).

options.label: Referral and prevention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit: INR >1.5, encephalopathy (confusion, drowsiness), bilirubin rising with falling ALT, vomiting/unable to maintain hydration, pregnancy with hepatitis E, immunosuppressed, age >60 with hepatitis E.
2. Hepatitis A prevention: vaccine for travellers to endemic areas, MSM, PWID, chronic liver disease, haemophilia, occupational risk; post-exposure — vaccine within 14 days to household/close contacts (UKHSA), HNIG in addition for >60, chronic liver disease, immunosuppressed. No hepatitis E vaccine in UK — cook pork thoroughly.
