options.label: Painful (subacute / De Quervain's thyroiditis)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Often viral; self-limiting. NSAID for pain; beta-blocker if thyrotoxic symptoms. Monitor TFTs (may go through thyrotoxic then hypothyroid phase).
2. Refer if severe, prolonged, or diagnostic uncertainty. NICE NG145, CKS.

options.label: Painless / postpartum
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Monitor TFTs (may fluctuate). Treat hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism as per NICE NG145. Postpartum: often resolves; recheck at 6 months. NICE CKS.

options.label: Headache (migraine / tension / red flags)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Migraine: triptan + NSAID at onset; prophylaxis if ≥2/month (propranolol, amitriptyline, topiramate). Tension: paracetamol/NSAID; avoid medication-overuse. Red flags: thunderclap – 999; new ≥50y or progressive – 2WW. NICE NG150, NG12.

options.label: Seizure / epilepsy / TIA / stroke
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First seizure: refer. Epilepsy: drug review; driving (DVLA). TIA: aspirin 300 mg then 75 mg; refer same-day. Stroke: 999. NICE NG217, NG128.

options.label: Cranial nerve / neuropathy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bell's palsy: steroid within 72 h; eye care. Trigeminal neuralgia: carbamazepine; refer for MRI. Peripheral neuropathy: B12, glucose, thyroid; refer if cause unclear. Myasthenia/MND: refer. NICE NG150, CKS.

options.label: BPPV (Epley)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Dix-Hallpike (torsional nystagmus). Treatment: Epley manoeuvre (can be done in primary care or refer to physio/ENT). Repeat if recurrence. NICE CKS.

options.label: Labyrinthitis / vestibular neuritis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supportive; prochlorperazine or antihistamine short-term for vomiting (limit to few days – can delay recovery). Exclude stroke (HINTS if central concern). Usually self-limiting. NICE CKS.

options.label: Meniere's
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Triad: vertigo, hearing loss, tinnitus. Acute: prochlorperazine. Prophylaxis: betahistine (off-label). Refer ENT for confirmation and monitoring. NICE CKS.

options.label: Red flags / sudden hearing loss
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sudden sensorineural hearing loss (unilateral, <72 h): urgent ENT same-day – steroids may improve outcome. Central vertigo (focal neurology, negative HINTS) – urgent imaging. NICE NG98, CKS.

tools.title: Vertigo – BPPV, vestibular neuritis/labyrinthitis, Ménière's
niceRefs: NICE CKS Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo

options.label: Is it central? (red flags)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day stroke pathway if: sudden persistent vertigo with any of — new headache/neck pain, diplopia, dysarthria, dysphagia, ataxia/unable to stand, limb weakness/numbness, vertical or direction-changing nystagmus, abnormal HINTS (normal head impulse test in acute vestibular syndrome = central), hearing loss with vertigo (AICA stroke or labyrinthitis), age >60 with vascular risk factors and first episode.
2. Also urgent: vertigo with fever/otalgia/discharge (suppurative labyrinthitis, cholesteatoma), head injury, sudden hearing loss (see Hearing loss).
3. Chronic/non-rotatory dizziness: cardiovascular (orthostatic BP, arrhythmia), medication (antihypertensives, sedatives), anxiety/PPPD, anaemia, hypoglycaemia.

options.label: BPPV and vestibular neuritis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. BPPV: brief (<1 min) rotatory vertigo on turning in bed/looking up, no hearing loss. Dix–Hallpike positive (torsional upbeat nystagmus after latency, fatigable) → Epley manoeuvre in clinic (cures 80% after 1–2 attempts); teach Brandt–Daroff exercises if Epley unavailable; no medication; avoid driving until symptom-free. Refer ENT/balance clinic if persistent after 3–4 weeks, atypical nystagmus, or recurrent (>3 episodes/year).
2. Vestibular neuritis (vertigo days, no hearing loss) / labyrinthitis (with hearing loss/tinnitus): acute — prochlorperazine 5 mg tds (or buccal 3 mg bd) or cyclizine 50 mg tds for ≤3 days ONLY (prolonged use delays compensation); short course prednisolone (specialist); early mobilisation and vestibular rehabilitation exercises (Cawthorne–Cooksey); improvement over 2–6 weeks. Refer if not improving at 2–4 weeks, hearing loss (urgent — audiology/ENT), or recurrent.

options.label: Ménière's disease
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Episodic vertigo 20 min–12 h with fluctuating low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, tinnitus and aural fullness in the same ear. Diagnosis requires audiometry — refer ENT for confirmation and MRI (exclude schwannoma).
2. Acute attack: prochlorperazine (buccal 3 mg) or cyclizine; lie still; admit if dehydrated/prolonged.
3. Prevention: salt restriction (<2 g/day), limit caffeine/alcohol, stress; betahistine 16 mg tds (up to 48 mg tds) — limited evidence but commonly tried for 3–6 months; ENT options — intratympanic steroids/gentamicin, hearing aid, vestibular rehab. Inform DVLA (must not drive during attacks; notify for Group 1 if recurrent sudden disabling vertigo); Ménière's Society support.

options.label: First-line (Drops)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Olive oil drops 2-3 times daily for 2 weeks. Avoid cotton buds. Sodium bicarbonate drops if oil fails. NICE CKS.

options.label: Mechanical removal
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Electronic irrigation or microsuction if drops fail and no perforation/recent surgery. Check for history of ear infections.

options.label: Discussion & ReSPECT / DNAR form
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Document preferences: CPR (yes/no/conditional), treatment escalation, preferred place of death. Use ReSPECT or local DNAR form; ensure copy to OOH/ambulance. Review with patient and family; update if wishes change. NICE NG108, Local formulary.

options.label: When to complete / who can sign
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Any competent adult can refuse CPR; document. DNAR: usually senior clinician; can be completed in advance with patient consent. In emergency without form: senior clinical decision; document afterwards. Do not delay CPR while searching for form. NICE NG108.

tools.title: Altitude medicine  heightening understanding of “travel consultations” – Management

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Altitude: assess AMS risk; advise gradual ascent; consider acetazolamide for prophylaxis. Expedition: pre-travel health, kit, evacuation. NICE CKS Travel.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:

options.label: Assessment

options.label: Indication & sampling
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic or therapeutic. Send for cell count, protein, culture, cytology if indicated. Albumin if considering SBP.
2. Consider coagulation; ultrasound guidance. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

options.label: When & how
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Before antibiotics if sepsis/bacteraemia suspected. Clean skin; multiple sets from different sites if indicated. Document indication.
2. Do not delay empiric antibiotics for culture. NICE NG51, CKS.

options.label: Insertion & care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aseptic technique; smallest gauge for indication. Secure; document site and date. Remove when no longer needed.
2. Monitor for phlebitis/infection. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: Capacity assessment (MCA)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess per MCA: can they understand, retain, weigh, and communicate the decision? Decision-specific (e.g. capacity for treatment A not necessarily for B). Document. If lacking capacity: act in best interests; involve family/IMCA. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Consent – child / Gillick
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Under 16: Gillick competence if child has sufficient understanding. Otherwise parental consent (or court). Document who gave consent. Refusal by competent child may override parent in some circumstances – seek advice. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: DoLS / LPS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Deprivation of liberty: when someone lacks capacity and needs care that amounts to deprivation (e.g. locked ward, continuous supervision). DoLS (England) or LPS when in force; Court of Protection for complex. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Insertion & care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aseptic technique; correct size (e.g. 12–14Ch). Trial without catheter when appropriate. Document indication and review date.
2. Long-term: change per protocol; screen for infection only if symptomatic. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.guidance:

2. Manage anxiety; ensure result and follow-up communicated. NICE NG12, CSP.

tools.title: Consent and capacity – adults, children, minor surgery
niceRefs: Mental Capacity Act 2005 Code of Practice

options.label: Capacity assessment (adults, England & Wales)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. MCA principles: presume capacity; support the person to decide (time, place, communication aids, interpreter — not family as interpreter for key decisions); an unwise decision is not incapacity; best interests; least restrictive option.
2. Two-stage test, decision- and time-specific: (a) impairment/disturbance of mind or brain (dementia, delirium, learning disability, intoxication, mental illness, brain injury); (b) because of it, unable to UNDERSTAND the relevant information, RETAIN it long enough, USE OR WEIGH it, or COMMUNICATE the decision. Failure on any one = lacks capacity for THIS decision.
3. Document: the decision in question, information given, the person's own words, which limb failed and why, who was present, steps taken to support capacity. Reassess if condition fluctuates (delirium — treat and retry).
4. If lacking capacity: check for valid Advance Decision (refusal of treatment — binding if valid and applicable; life-sustaining refusal must be written, signed, witnessed), Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare (verify on OPG register — a finance LPA does NOT cover health), court-appointed deputy; otherwise best-interests decision consulting family/carers; IMCA if no one to consult and serious treatment/accommodation decision. Deprivation of liberty → DoLS/LPS application (care home/hospital). Scotland: Adults with Incapacity Act — s47 certificate.

options.label: Children and young people
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 16–17: presumed competent to consent (Family Law Reform Act 1969); MCA applies; refusal of life-saving treatment can be overridden by a parent or court — seek advice.
2. Under 16: Gillick competent if they understand the nature, purpose and consequences of the treatment and the alternatives, including of not treating — assess and document per decision; a competent child's consent is valid without parental knowledge; encourage parental involvement unless this risks harm. If not competent, a person with parental responsibility consents (mother always; father if married to mother at birth or on birth certificate from 2003; step-parent only with court order/agreement).
3. Fraser guidelines (contraception/sexual health specifically): understands the advice, cannot be persuaded to tell parents, likely to continue sexual activity, health would suffer without treatment, best interests. Under 13: cannot in law consent to sexual activity — safeguarding referral always; 13–15: assess exploitation (age gap, coercion, substances, grooming) and refer if concerns.
4. Disputes between parents or parent and child: do not proceed with elective treatment; involve safeguarding lead, medical defence organisation, and court if necessary (life-saving treatment given in an emergency regardless).

options.label: Consent for minor surgery and procedures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Montgomery standard: disclose material risks THIS patient would attach significance to — not just what a doctor thinks important. Cover: diagnosis and uncertainty, options including no treatment, benefits, risks (common and serious), who will do it, histology plan, scarring, infection (~2–5%), bleeding, pain, recurrence, nerve damage for specific sites (e.g. temporal branch of facial nerve, spinal accessory in posterior triangle), need for further surgery.
2. Written consent for all excisions, joint injections and cryotherapy of lesions where scarring/pigment change possible; verbal (documented) for simple procedures; the person doing the procedure takes consent; allow time to decide; interpreter for non-English speakers.
3. Safety checklist (RCGP minor surgery): identity, site marked and agreed, allergies, anticoagulants/antiplatelets (continue warfarin if INR <3 checked within 72 h; DOACs — omit morning dose for higher-risk sites), pacemaker (bipolar diathermy only), lidocaine max dose 3 mg/kg plain / 7 mg/kg with adrenaline (avoid adrenaline in digits only if peripheral vascular disease), send ALL excised lesions for histology, specimen labelled before leaving room, aftercare and suture removal written.
4. Do not excise in primary care: suspected melanoma (2WW), lesions on face/high-risk BCC sites unless accredited, lesions >2 cm, deep lumps, sarcoma concern. Record capacity if any doubt; a competent refusal must be respected.

MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diabetics: Warn about blood sugar rise (may last 1-2 weeks).
2. Anticoagulation: Safe if INR in therapeutic range (<3.0).
3. Infection: Absolutely contraindicated if skin infection over site or suspected septic arthritis.

options.label: Joint / IM
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aseptic technique; correct site (e.g. Z-track IM). Joint: confirm no sepsis; steroid ± local anaesthetic per indication.
2. Document site, drug, batch. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: Joint / IM
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Aseptic technique; correct site (e.g. Z-track IM). Joint: confirm no sepsis; steroid ± local anaesthetic per indication.
2. Document site, drug, batch. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: Care & prescribing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise dying (GSF, NICE); communicate with family. Anticipatory drugs: analgesia, anti-secretory, antiemetic, anxiolytic. Review and stop non-essential meds.
2. Support family; verify death when appropriate. NICE NG142, GSF.

options.label: Indication & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude raised ICP (imaging if concern). Send CSF for cells, protein, glucose, culture, viral PCR. Consider specialist perform.
2. Post-LP: lie flat; monitor headache. NICE NG51, CKS.

options.label: Section 2 / 3
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Section 2: assessment (up to 28 days). Section 3: treatment (up to 6 months, renewable). Two doctors + AMHP; nearest relative considerations.
2. After detention: inform patient of rights, copy to care team. NICE NG10, MHA 1983 (as amended).

options.label: Sepsis / CAP / antimicrobial
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sepsis: NEWS2/qSOFA; if suspected sepsis give antibiotic per NG51 and fluid; emergency referral. CAP: CURB-65; amoxicillin 500 mg tds 5 days (low risk); admit if CURB-65 ≥2. Cellulitis: flucloxacillin; mark margin; admit if severe/facial. Use local resistance data; 5-day courses where appropriate. NICE NG51, NG138, NG141.

options.label: HIV / TB / viral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. HIV: offer test in high-prevalence settings; if positive refer immediately. PrEP/PEP per NG122. TB: refer TB service; RIPE; contact tracing. COVID antiviral: nirmatrelvir/ritonavir per eligibility. Shingles: aciclovir if <72 h; 2WW if ophthalmic. NICE NG33, NG122, CKS.

options.label: Bites / travel / needlestick
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bite: clean; antibiotic if high risk (co-amoxiclav); rabies/tetanus per risk. Needlestick: wash; encourage bleeding; risk assess source HIV/HBV/HCV; HBV vaccine/immunoglobulin; HIV PEP within 72 h per protocol. Travel: vaccines; malaria prophylaxis per destination. NICE NG33, CKS, NaTHNaC.

options.label: Tick bite / Lyme
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Remove tick with fine-tipped tweezers. Prophylaxis: doxycycline 200 mg single dose if attached ≥36 h and endemic area. Erythema migrans: doxycycline 100 mg bd 21 days. Refer if neurological/joint. NICE NG95, CKS.

options.label: Screening
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cancer: bowel (FIT 56–74), breast (mammography 50–71), cervical (25–64 HPV). CVD: NHS Health Check 40–74; QRISK3; statin if ≥10%. Diabetic retinopathy: annual DES. AAA: men 65. NICE NG12, CG181, NHS.

options.label: Anticipatory Meds (The 'Big 4')
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pain/SOB: Morphine Sulfate 2.5mg - 5mg SC prn.
2. Secretions: Hyoscine Butylbromide 20mg SC prn.
3. Agitation: Midazolam 2.5mg - 5mg SC prn.
4. Nausea: Levomepromazine 6.25mg SC prn.
5. Note: Ensure Just-in-Case box is in house and District Nurses are informed.

options.label: Verification of Death
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm identity.
2. 5 mins observation: No respiratory effort, no palpable pulse, fixed dilated pupils.
3. Documentation: Record time of death and clinical findings clearly.

options.label: Symptomatic relief
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify cause (GI, drugs, vestibular, metabolic, CNS). Cyclizine 50 mg tds or prochlorperazine 5 mg tds; metoclopramide 10 mg tds (avoid if young or parkinsonism).
2. Red flags: Headache, abdominal pain, dehydration – assess and refer as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit: Severe dehydration, suspected bowel obstruction, head injury, raised ICP. 2WW: Unexplained persistent nausea/vomiting with weight loss.
2. Pregnancy: Exclude hyperemesis; treat and refer if severe. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Stepwise analgesia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: paracetamol + NSAID (if appropriate). Step 2: add weak opioid (e.g. codeine or tramadol). Step 3: strong opioid (morphine first-line; oxycodone/fentanyl if needed). Always: regular dose + PRN breakthrough (e.g. 1/6 of 24h dose). Anticipate constipation (laxative) and nausea (anti-emetic). NICE NG142.

options.label: Breakthrough & neuropathic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breakthrough: same opioid, 1/10–1/6 of 24h dose, repeat as needed (e.g. 1-hourly). Neuropathic: add gabapentinoid or amitriptyline. Bone pain: consider NSAID or bisphosphonate. Review regularly. NICE NG142, CKS.

options.label: Stepwise analgesia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: paracetamol + NSAID (if appropriate). Step 2: add weak opioid (e.g. codeine or tramadol). Step 3: strong opioid (morphine first-line; oxycodone/fentanyl if needed). Always: regular dose + PRN breakthrough (e.g. 1/6 of 24h dose). Anticipate constipation (laxative) and nausea (anti-emetic). NICE NG142.

options.label: Breakthrough & neuropathic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breakthrough: same opioid, 1/10–1/6 of 24h dose, repeat as needed (e.g. 1-hourly). Neuropathic: add gabapentinoid or amitriptyline. Bone pain: consider NSAID or bisphosphonate. Review regularly. NICE NG142, CKS.

options.label: Sampling
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Send fluid for protein, LDH, pH, cytology, culture. Light's criteria for exudate vs transudate. Consider image guidance.
2. Therapeutic tap if symptomatic; avoid removing >1.5 L. NICE CKS.

options.label: Indication & technique
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consent; chaperone; explain. Position (left lateral). Inspect; lubricant; assess tone, mass, tenderness, prostate (size, consistency, nodules) if male.
2. Indications: rectal bleeding, change in bowel habit, suspected prostate pathology, constipation/impaction. 2WW if palpable mass or high suspicion. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. History, examination, baseline investigations per procedure type. Optimise comorbidities; document fitness. NICE NG45, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer anaesthetics/pre-op clinic if high risk or unclear fitness. NICE NG45.

options.label: Biopsy / cryotherapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Punch biopsy: consent; suture or cautery. Send in formalin with form. Cryotherapy: liquid nitrogen for warts/keratosis; advise blistering.
2. Follow local dermatology policy. NICE CKS.

options.label: Educational
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. RCGP RCA guidance: structure, safety-netting, shared decision-making. Use NICE CKS to support clinical content. No patient pathway.

options.label: Learning resource
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use for CPD. Apply NICE CKS and local guidelines to practice. No specific patient pathway.

options.label: Recognition & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise: abuse or neglect (physical, sexual, financial, emotional, neglect). Document factually; do not investigate alone. Refer to adult social care per local policy. If immediate risk: police. MARAC if high-risk domestic abuse. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Capacity & consent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If adult has capacity: respect their decision unless others at risk (e.g. children). If lacking capacity: best interests; share information if necessary to protect. Discuss with safeguarding lead. NICE NG108.

options.label: Med3 (Fit Notes)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First 7 days: Patient self-certifies (Employer cannot demand Med3).
2. >7 days: Clinician issues Med3 based on clinical assessment.
3. Note: Focus on what patient 'can' do (phased return, amended duties) where possible.

options.label: Safeguarding (Adult/Child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify: Physical, emotional, sexual abuse, or neglect (including self-neglect in adults).
2. Action: Discuss with Designated Lead. Urgent referral to MASH (Children) or Adult Social Care if risk is immediate.
3. Documentation: Use factual, objective language. Do not promise confidentiality if disclosure is required for safety.

options.label: Continuity & QOF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Disease: Annual review (QOF) including bloods and symptom score.
2. Polypharmacy: Holistic medication review (SMR) with clinical pharmacist for patients on >10 meds.

options.label: Recognition & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise: abuse or neglect (physical, sexual, financial, emotional, neglect). Document factually; do not investigate alone. Refer to adult social care per local policy. If immediate risk: police. MARAC if high-risk domestic abuse. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Capacity & consent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If adult has capacity: respect their decision unless others at risk (e.g. children). If lacking capacity: best interests; share information if necessary to protect. Discuss with safeguarding lead. NICE NG108.

options.label: Issuing (duration & content)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Duration appropriate to condition; no need to state diagnosis. Can advise 'not fit' or 'may be fit for work' with modifications (e.g. phased return, amended duties). Review date; safety-net. Gov.uk fit note guidance, NICE NG12.

options.label: Phased return / may be fit
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 'May be fit for work': suggest modifications (e.g. return gradually, different hours, avoid certain tasks). Employer decides if they can accommodate. Phased return: shorten hours/days initially. Document. Gov.uk fit note guidance.

options.label: Interpretation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Pre- and post-bronchodilator; quality checks. Obstruction: FEV1/FVC <0.7. Restriction: reduced FVC, proportionately. Refer if diagnostic uncertainty or severe.
2. NICE NG115, NG80, BTS.

options.label: Common Injections (Standard Pack)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Drugs: Triamcinolone (Kenalog) 40mg or Depo-Medrone 40mg + 1% Lidocaine.
2. Areas: Shoulder (Subacromial), Knee (Intra-articular), Trigger Finger (Tendon sheath), Carpal Tunnel.
3. Post-op: 48 hours of joint rest. Warn about 'steroid flare' (pain increase for 24-48h).

options.label: Cautions & Consent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diabetics: Warn about blood sugar rise (may last 1-2 weeks).
2. Anticoagulation: Safe if INR in therapeutic range (<3.0).
3. Infection: Absolutely contraindicated if skin infection over site or suspected septic arthritis.

options.label: Closure (suture / glue / strips)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Clean wound; consider closure if <24 h and low risk. Sutures vs glue vs steri-strips by site and tension. Tetanus if indicated. Remove sutures: face 3–5 d, scalp 7 d, limb 7–10 d, joint 10–14 d. NICE CKS.

options.label: Dressings & when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Simple wound: non-adherent dressing; change as needed. Moist wound healing for most. Refer: tendon/nerve/vessel injury, bite (human/animal), high-risk site (hand, face), infected or immunosuppressed. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Ten practical tips for sustainability in primary care – Management

options.label: Practice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Greener practice: inhalers, prescribing, travel, waste. Align with national net zero. NICE CKS, local policy.

tools.title: The Big GP Consultation for AiTs – Management

options.label: Educational
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Structure and communication skills. Use NICE CKS for clinical content. No specific patient pathway.

options.label: 1. Assessment & safety
options.guidance:
ASSESSMENT:
• Consent: capacity (MCA – understand, retain, weigh, communicate); decision-specific. Voluntary; information given. Child: Gillick competence; parental consent where appropriate. Document.
• Safeguarding: child or adult at risk; document factually; follow local policy; discuss with named/designated professional. NICE NG76, NG108.
• Fit note: clinical assessment; duration; phased return; "may be fit" with modifications. NICE NG108, gov.uk.

options.label: 2. Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT:
• Procedures: aseptic technique; consent; correct kit (venepuncture bottles, cannula gauge); document site/date. Venepuncture: tourniquet time; label at bedside. Cannulation: secure; remove when not needed. Wound: clean; closure vs dressings; tetanus; suture removal by site. Minor surgery: consent; sterile technique; histology if excision. NICE CKS.
• Palliative: anticipatory drugs; ReSPECT/DNAR; symptom control (pain, nausea, agitation, secretions). Verification of death: confirm absent pulse, breathing, response; MCCD if expected and within 28 days (14 Scotland). NICE NG142, NG108.

options.label: 3. Referral & governance
options.guidance:
REFERRAL:
• Safeguarding: social care, police, MARAC per policy; do not leave at risk. Capacity: Court of Protection if complex/dispute; IMCA if unbefriended. DoLS/LPS if deprivation of liberty.
• Coroner: unexpected death, unknown cause, industrial disease, or per local protocol. Document; support family. NICE NG108.

options.label: Technique & bottles
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consent; correct bottles and order (e.g. blood culture first if required). Avoid prolonged tourniquet (<1 min). Label at bedside; send promptly. Follow local phlebotomy policy. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: Difficult access / children
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider warming vein; smaller gauge; different site. Child: topical anaesthetic; distraction. If repeated failure consider referral for ultrasound-guided or paediatric phlebotomy. NICE CKS.

options.label: Expected death (MCCD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm absence of pulse, breathing, response; record time. If expected and you attended in last 28 days (14 in Scotland), complete MCCD. Advise family: register death, funeral director. Cremation form if required (different from MCCD). NICE CKS, RCGP.

options.label: Unexpected / coroner
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Do not complete MCCD if cause unknown, suspicious, industrial disease, or referral required. Contact coroner (England/Wales) or procurator fiscal (Scotland) per local protocol. Support family; document clearly. NICE CKS, Local policy.

options.label: Closure (suture / glue / strips)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Clean wound; consider closure if <24 h and low risk. Sutures vs glue vs steri-strips by site and tension. Tetanus if indicated. Remove sutures: face 3–5 d, scalp 7 d, limb 7–10 d, joint 10–14 d. NICE CKS.

MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Simple wound: non-adherent dressing; change as needed. Moist wound healing for most. Refer: tendon/nerve/vessel injury, bite (human/animal), high-risk site (hand, face), infected or immunosuppressed. NICE CKS.

1. Clean wound; consider closure if <24 h and low risk. Sutures vs glue vs steri-strips by site and tension. Tetanus if indicated. Remove sutures: face 3–5 d, scalp 7 d, limb 7–10 d, joint 10–14 d. NICE CKS.

options.guidance:

1. Simple wound: non-adherent dressing; change as needed. Moist wound healing for most. Refer: tendon/nerve/vessel injury, bite (human/animal), high-risk site (hand, face), infected or immunosuppressed. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Acne  getting the management spot on – Management

options.label: Mild (comedones)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Topical: adapalene 0.1% or benzoyl peroxide 5% OD. If inadequate after 12 weeks add topical antibiotic (e.g. clindamycin). NICE NG198.

options.label: Moderate (inflammatory)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Fixed combination: adapalene + benzoyl peroxide, or topical abx + benzoyl peroxide. If inadequate: oral doxycycline 100 mg OD 12 weeks (or lymecycline). NICE NG198.

options.label: Severe or scarring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer dermatology for oral isotretinoin. Exclude pregnancy; contraception. Do not offer oral antibiotic long-term as monotherapy. NICE NG198.

options.label: When to refer / pregnancy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Refer: Severe, scarring, or failed oral antibiotic. Isotretinoin: pregnancy prevention programme; two forms contraception.
2. Pregnancy: Topical only; avoid oral tetracyclines, isotretinoin. Azithromycin if needed. NICE NG198.

tools.title: Addressing health inequalities in cancer  the role of primary care – Management

options.label: Practice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Equitable access to screening and 2WW; address barriers; culturally sensitive communication. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Screening & follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. AUDIT: 0–7 low risk; 8–15 hazardous; 16–19 harmful; 20+ possible dependence. Extended AUDIT for dependence.
2. Brief intervention if 8+; refer if dependence or complex. NICE CG115.

options.label: AUDIT & brief advice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. AUDIT or FAST; feedback on units and risk. Brief advice: reduce consumption; set goals; written info.
2. Signpost to support (e.g. Drink Free Days). Follow-up if harmful use. Refer if dependent or requested. NICE CG115, PH24.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Abstain; thiamine if at risk. LFTs, platelets, INR; consider Fibroscan/elastography. Screen for varices if cirrhosis.
2. Refer hepatology: cirrhosis, decompensation, uncertain diagnosis. 2WW if suspected cancer. NICE CG115, NG50.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Abstain; thiamine if at risk. LFTs, platelets, INR; consider Fibroscan/elastography. Screen for varices if cirrhosis.
2. Refer hepatology: cirrhosis, decompensation, uncertain diagnosis. 2WW if suspected cancer. NICE CG115, NG50.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Abstain from alcohol. Pain control; nutritional support. Treat acute episode per local protocol; refer if severe.
2. Chronic pancreatitis: enzyme replacement, diabetes screening; refer for specialist management. NICE NG104, CKS.

options.label: Holistic Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Stages of Change**: Identify where the patient is (Pre-contemplation to Maintenance).
2. **Harm Reduction**: Reducing units, switching to lower ABV, safe drinking intervals. 
3. **Biological**: Supervised detox if dependent (≥10 units/day or morning shakes) followed by anti-craving meds.
4. **Psychosocial**: Engagement with community services (AA, SMART Recovery) and addressing 'dual diagnosis' (co-morbid anxiety/depression).

options.label: Withdrawal Severity & Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Severity: 
   - Mild (CIWA <10): Supportive, vitamins only.
   - Mod/Severe (CIWA ≥10): Chlordiazepoxide regime.
2. **Wernicke's Triad**: Ophthalmoplegia, Ataxia, Confusion. 
3. **CRITICAL**: Give Pabrinex (Thiamine) BEFORE Glucose to prevent precipitating Wernicke's. NICE CG115.

options.label: Anti-Craving Pharmacotherapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Acamprosate**: 666mg tds. Start day 1 of abstinence.
2. **Naltrexone**: 50mg OD. Monitor LFTs.
3. **Disulfiram**: Specialist only. NICE CG115.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Bulk-forming laxatives; topical GTN or diltiazem. Avoid constipation. Refer if chronic or failed medical. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Assessment and management of obesity – Management

options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

options.label: Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Register (temp or full); asylum seekers exempt from charges. Trauma-informed approach; professional interpreter if needed.
2. Screening: TB (asylum seekers), BBV, mental health, immunisation catch-up. Safeguarding; signpost housing/support. RCGP, GOV.UK, NICE, UKHSA.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Voiding diary; IPSS if available. Exclude: UTI (MSU), retention (palpate/scan bladder, PVR), haematuria (2WW if visible). DRE: size, consistency, nodules – refer if suspicious. PSA: only after counselling (prostate cancer risk, false positives); do not delay referral for haematuria for PSA. NICE NG97, NG12, CKS.

options.label: Medical treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Alpha-blocker (e.g. tamsulosin 400 mcg od) for voiding symptoms; effect within days. Consider 5-alpha reductase inhibitor (finasteride/dutasteride) if prostate enlarged and long-term treatment preferred – slower onset; combine with alpha-blocker if significant symptoms.
2. Review after 4–6 weeks; advise on fluid, caffeine, constipation. NICE NG97, CKS.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 2WW: Visible haematuria; suspected prostate cancer (nodule, raised PSA with counselling). Urgent: Acute retention (catheterise); anuria.
2. Routine: LUTS not controlled; recurrent retention; consideration of surgery. NICE NG97, NG12.

options.label: Consultant Differential
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Normal Grief**: Fluctuating distress with 'pockets of relief'. Usually improves over 6-months. No meds indicated.
2. **Prolonged Grief Disorder (ICD-11)**: Persistent, pervasive yearning/preoccupation for >6 months. Marked functional impairment.
3. **Co-morbid MDD**: If low mood is persistent (not just grief-related) and includes biological symptoms (sleep/appetite/guilt), treat as MDD.

options.label: Supportive Measures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Validation and signposting to bereavement services (e.g. Cruse).
2. Therapy: Complicated Grief Therapy (CGT) if symptoms remain severe >6 months.
3. Meds: Avoid antidepressants for uncomplicated grief—may interfere with the mourning process.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Cachexia = weight loss + metabolic driver (not just underfeeding). Treat reversible causes (thyroid, depression, dysphagia, malabsorption); dietitian input.
2. Trial of ONS may be appropriate; document goals of care. In advanced/terminal illness, avoid forced feeding; focus on symptoms and patient priorities.
3. NICE NG69, CKS.

options.label: Capacity assessment (MCA)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess per MCA: can they understand, retain, weigh, and communicate the decision? Decision-specific (e.g. capacity for treatment A not necessarily for B). Document. If lacking capacity: act in best interests; involve family/IMCA. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Consent – child / Gillick
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Under 16: Gillick competence if child has sufficient understanding. Otherwise parental consent (or court). Document who gave consent. Refusal by competent child may override parent in some circumstances – seek advice. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: DoLS / LPS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Deprivation of liberty: when someone lacks capacity and needs care that amounts to deprivation (e.g. locked ward, continuous supervision). DoLS (England) or LPS when in force; Court of Protection for complex. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Review & safety
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Structured review; indication, interactions, monitoring. Deprescribe where benefit unclear. Antipsychotics for behaviour: only after non-drug approaches; NICE NG97; regular review.
2. Current medication list in care home; DNAR/ACP documented. Anticoagulation: ensure consistent supply and monitoring. NICE NG67, NG114, NG97, CKS.

options.label: Recognition & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise: unexplained/inconsistent injury, developmental concern, parent behaviour, disclosure. Do not investigate alone; document factually.
2. Immediate risk to child: contact police/social care urgently. Otherwise refer to children's social care per local pathway. Discuss with named/designated professional if unsure.
3. NICE NG76, CKS Child abuse, Working Together.

options.label: Initial Screening
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
History: Sleep, stress, diet, drugs. Bloods: FBC, Ferritin, U&E, TFT, HbA1c, Vit D, Bone, LFT, Coeliac screen. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected ME/CFS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Persistent fatigue >3 months. Check NICE NG206 for diagnostic criteria. Do not offer LET or GET. Focus on energy management (pacing).

options.label: Assessment & non-pharmacological
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess: site, impact, red flags (weight loss, night pain, neurology). Biopsychosocial. Set goals. Non-pharmacological first: exercise, physiotherapy, psychological (CBT, ACT). NICE NG193.
2. Paracetamol may be considered; avoid long-term NSAID. NICE NG193.

options.label: Neuropathic pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: gabapentin or pregabalin, or amitriptyline (low dose nocte). Second-line: switch or add. Duloxetine for chronic musculoskeletal pain. Review benefit and harms. NICE NG193, NG173.

options.label: Opioid (only if benefit > harm)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Offer only after non-pharmacological and non-opioid options; shared decision-making. Lowest dose; regular review. Taper if no benefit or harm. Avoid long-term for chronic non-cancer pain where possible. Do not offer codeine. NICE NG193.

options.label: Soft tissue / tendon
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Joint / arthritis / red flags

options.label: When to refer

options.guidance:

options.label: Anticipatory Meds (The 'Big 4')

options.label: Verification of Death
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Confirm identity.
2. 5 mins observation: No respiratory effort, no palpable pulse, fixed dilated pupils.
3. Documentation: Record time of death and clinical findings clearly.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Distinguish syncope (cardiac, orthostatic, carotid sinus) from non-syncopal fall. Medication review (sedatives, hypotensives); vision; footwear; home hazards; bone health.
2. Consider 24h BP if orthostatic; ECG if syncope/cardiac suspected. NICE CG161, NG231, CKS.

options.label: Intervention
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:

options.label: Vasovagal / situational

options.label: Cardiac / unexplained

tools.title: Management of hyperkalaemia in primary care – Management

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Repeat; stop ACEi/ARB/MRA/spironolactone if severe. Consider calcium resonium. Refer if K+ >6 or ECG changes. NICE NG203, CKS.

options.label: Sleep Specialist Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Principle**: Distinguish between Primary Insomnia and secondary to comorbidities (Pain/OSA/Depression).
2. **Therapy**: **CBT-I is the gold standard 1st-line treatment**—superior long-term results to pharmacological options.
3. **Biological**: Circadian rhythm stabilization (melatonin) and conservative use of sedative hypnotics for short-term relief only.
4. **Environment**: Optimization of the sleep environment and addressing 'sleep effort' (the paradoxical anxiety about falling asleep).

options.label: Behavioural Interventions
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. **Sleep Restriction**: Limit time in bed to actual sleep duration (min 5h). Increases 'sleep drive'.
2. **Stimulus Control**: Leave bed if awake for >20 mins. Re-associate bed with sleep only.
3. **Cognitive**: Challenging 'catastrophic' thoughts about sleep loss impact.

tools.title: Managing the risk of drug-induced QT prolongation in primary care – Management

options.label: Assessment

tools.title: Micronutrient deficiencies – zinc, magnesium, vitamin C, vitamin K, multiple

options.label: Magnesium
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hypomagnesaemia (<0.7 mmol/L; severe <0.5): causes — PPIs (long-term; stop/switch to H2RA), diuretics (loop/thiazide), alcohol, diarrhoea/malabsorption, diabetes, refeeding, drugs (cisplatin, ciclosporin, EGFR inhibitors), renal wasting (Gitelman/Bartter). Symptoms: cramps, tremor, arrhythmia, seizures; causes refractory hypokalaemia and hypocalcaemia — check K, Ca, PTH, ECG.
2. Severe (<0.4) or symptomatic/arrhythmia → same-day admission for IV magnesium sulfate 20 mmol over 12–24 h.
3. Mild–moderate asymptomatic: oral magnesium aspartate 10 mmol sachet od–bd (Magnaspartate — licensed) or magnesium glycerophosphate 4 mmol tablets 1–2 tds (unlicensed/'special'); diarrhoea limits dose; recheck 1–2 weeks and after cause addressed; if PPI needed and Mg stays low despite supplements → stop PPI.

options.label: Zinc and vitamin C
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Zinc: suspect in alcohol excess, malabsorption (coeliac, IBD, bariatric), CKD, anorexia, vegan diets, long-term diuretics, acrodermatitis-type rash (periorificial, acral), alopecia, taste loss, poor wound healing, recurrent infection, diarrhoea. Serum zinc <11 micromol/L (fasting, interpret with albumin/CRP — low in inflammation). Treat: zinc sulfate 125 mg (45 mg elemental) od–tds (Solvazinc) for 3 months then reassess; take away from iron/calcium; long-term use depletes copper — check if >6 months.
2. Vitamin C (scurvy): dietary restriction, alcohol, elderly living alone, eating disorder, 'tea and toast'; perifollicular haemorrhage, corkscrew hairs, gum bleeding/swelling, bruising, poor healing, anaemia; plasma ascorbate <11 micromol/L (take on ice) but treat on clinical suspicion. Treat: ascorbic acid 500 mg–1 g daily for 1–2 weeks then 100 mg daily until diet corrected; symptoms improve within days; dietary advice (fruit, peppers, potatoes); dietitian/social support.

options.label: Vitamin K and multiple deficiencies / refeeding
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Vitamin K: prolonged PT with normal APTT/fibrinogen and bleeding (bruising, gum/GI); causes — fat malabsorption (coeliac, cholestasis, pancreatic insufficiency, bariatric), prolonged antibiotics, warfarin, poor intake. Adults: phytomenadione 10 mg orally (Konakion MM) or IV if bleeding/malabsorption, recheck PT 24–48 h; neonates — IM 1 mg at birth (vitamin K deficiency bleeding; oral regimen if parents refuse IM). Warfarin-related high INR — see Anticoagulation tool.
2. Multiple deficiencies (alcohol dependence, bariatric surgery, eating disorders, elderly malnourished, homeless): screen FBC, ferritin, B12, folate, vitamin D, calcium, phosphate, magnesium, zinc, LFT, albumin, PT; MUST score. Alcohol: thiamine 100 mg tds (or 200–300 mg daily) + vitamin B co-strong 1–2 tablets tds; Pabrinex IV in hospital if Wernicke risk (confusion, ataxia, nystagmus) — give BEFORE glucose. Bariatric: lifelong multivitamin (Forceval od), iron, B12 injections 3-monthly, calcium/vitamin D, annual bloods per BOMSS.
3. REFEEDING risk (CG32): BMI <16, >15% weight loss in 3–6 months, little intake >10 days, low K/PO4/Mg before feeding — start feeding at ≤10 kcal/kg/day, thiamine 200–300 mg before and during first 10 days, monitor K, phosphate, Mg daily; admit if high risk or needs enteral support; dietitian referral for all.

curated.by: Claude draft (NICE CG32 Nutrition support 2006/2017; NICE CKS Malnutrition; BNF; SPS hypomagnesaemia guidance)

options.label: Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Prioritise by what matters to the patient; avoid treatment burden. Single-disease targets may be inappropriate; consider quality of life over disease-specific outcomes.
2. Structured review; care planning; deprescribe where benefit unclear. NICE NG56, CKS.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Gabapentin (titrate from 300 mg nocte) or pregabalin, or amitriptyline (10–25 mg nocte, increase if needed). Review at 2–4 weeks. Consider cause (diabetic, post-herpetic, trigeminal). NICE NG173, NG193.

options.label: Second-line & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If inadequate: switch or add; consider duloxetine for musculoskeletal overlap. Refer pain service if refractory or complex. Trigeminal neuralgia: carbamazepine; refer. NICE NG173, NG193.
