options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

options.label: Lifestyle or Single Drug (Mono)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 48 mmol/mol (6.5%).
2. Review: Every 3-6 months until stable. NICE NG28.

options.label: Dual / Triple Therapy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Target: 53 mmol/mol (7.0%).
2. Adjust: Intensify if HbA1c rises to 58 mmol/mol. NICE NG28.

options.label: Frailty / Comorbidities
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Individualise: Consider less stringent target (e.g. 58-64) to avoid hypoglycaemia. NICE NG28.

options.label: Step 1: Metformin First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dose: Start 500mg daily, increase slowly to 1g-2g total daily to avoid GI upset.
2. SGLT2i: Add if CVD, HF, or high risk of CVD (QRISK ≥10%) regardless of HbA1c control. NICE NG28.

options.label: CVD / Heart Failure / High Risk
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor (e.g. Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin) should be added to Metformin as soon as CVD/HF is confirmed. NICE NG28.

options.label: CKD + Albuminuria (ACR ≥3)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. SGLT2 inhibitor is indicated. Monitor eGFR; check local SPC for withdrawal thresholds. NICE NG28.

options.label: Obesity (BMI ≥ 35)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GLP-1 mimetics (e.g. Semaglutide) if BMI ≥35 AND triple therapy not at target (or BMI <35 if insulin would have occupational implications). NICE NG28.

options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

options.label: Suspected OSA (NICE NG202)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Score: Use **Epworth Sleepiness Scale** (>10 is abnormal).
2. Risk: Assess for comorbidities (BMI >30, HTN, Diabetes).
3. Referral: Sleep clinic for Nocturnal Oximetry or Polysomnography.
4. Driving: Advise patient to inform DVLA if excessive daytime sleepiness affects driving. NICE NG202.

options.label: Fit note & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Fit note: duration; 'may be fit for work' with adjustments if appropriate. Employer needs functional impact, not diagnosis; do not disclose without consent.
2. OH referral (with consent): workplace assessment, ill-health retirement, employer request. GMC, GOV.UK fit note guidance.

options.label: Consultant Addiction Strategy
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **Priority**: Reduce fatalities (Overdose prevention).
2. **Assessment**: Frequency, route (IV risk), cost, and criminal justice involvement.
3. **Dual Diagnosis**: High correlation with trauma (PTSD) and EUPD. Treat co-morbidities simultaneously.

options.label: Opioid Dependence (Heroin/Methadone)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. OAT: Opioid Agonist Treatment (Methadone or Buprenorphine) is the standard of care.
2. Safety: Provide Naloxone kits for home use. Screening for Hep C and HIV.

options.label: Cannabis/Cocaine
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Psychosocial (CBT, Motivational Interviewing, Contingency Management).
2. Meds: No licensed maintenance pharmacotherapy. Symptom management only.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Short-term only; prefer paracetamol/NSAID. Assess dependence risk. NICE NG59, CKS.

options.label: Deprescribing
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Taper gradually; treat withdrawal if needed. Multimodal pain management. NICE CKS.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rotterdam criteria; exclude thyroid, prolactin, NCAH. NICE NG38, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Lifestyle; metformin if metabolic need; COCP for cycle/androgen; fertility referral if trying to conceive. NICE NG38.

options.label: Structured review
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Indication for each drug; interactions; renal/hepatic dose; anticholinergic burden. STOPP/START (or equivalent). Deprescribe where benefit unclear or burden high; shared decision-making.
2. High-risk in elderly: NSAIDs, anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, duplicate drug classes. Patient understanding; adherence; monitoring. NICE NG5, NG114, NG67, CKS.

tools.title: Postoperative follow-up of people who have undergone bariatric surgery – Management

options.label: Tier 3 Specialist Service Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Criteria: BMI ≥ 35 with comorbidities (T2DM, OSA, HTN) or BMI ≥ 40.
2. Multidisciplinary: Physician, Dietitian, Psychologist, and Physiotherapist led.
3. Pharmacotherapy: Initiate GLP-1 (e.g. Wegovy/Semaglutide) as per NICE TA875 criteria (BMI ≥ 35 + at least one comorbidity).

options.label: Tier 4 (Bariatric Surgery)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Procedures: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass (RYGB) or Sleeve Gastrectomy.
2. Criteria: BMI ≥ 40 or ≥ 35 with significant comorbidities; failure of Tier 3 intervention for ≥ 6 months.
3. Pre-op: Smoking cessation and psychiatric clearance mandatory. NICE CG189.

tools.title: Prescribing medicines associated with dependence  how can NICE guideline NG215 support ou – Management

options.label: Principles
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Minimise initiation; shortest duration; regular review. Taper when stopping (benzodiazepines, Z-drugs, opioids, gabapentinoids).
2. Shared decision-making; support for withdrawal. Do not stop abruptly. NICE NG215, CKS.

options.label: Equivalence
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same standard of care as community (equivalence). Consent and confidentiality apply; record-keeping. Screening on entry: BBV, mental health, substance use per protocol.
2. Refer to prison healthcare or external services as indicated. NICE, UKHSA.

options.label: Primary
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; avoid cold; gloves. Nifedipine MR 10–20 mg bd if disabling. Screen for connective tissue disease (ANA, nailfold capillaroscopy) if secondary suspected.
2. Refer rheumatology if secondary or digital ulceration. NICE CKS.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Check ferritin; treat iron deficiency. Review drugs (antidepressants, antihistamines). NICE CKS.

options.label: Treatment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dopamine agonist (ropinirole/pramipexole) or gabapentinoid. Low dose; augment with iron if low. NICE CKS.

options.label: Recognition & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise: unexplained/inconsistent injury, developmental concern, parent behaviour, disclosure. Do not investigate alone; document factually.
2. Immediate risk to child: contact police/social care urgently. Otherwise refer to children's social care per local pathway. Discuss with named/designated professional if unsure.
3. NICE NG76, CKS Child abuse, Working Together.

options.label: Med3 (Fit Notes)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First 7 days: Patient self-certifies (Employer cannot demand Med3).
2. >7 days: Clinician issues Med3 based on clinical assessment.
3. Note: Focus on what patient 'can' do (phased return, amended duties) where possible.

options.label: Safeguarding (Adult/Child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify: Physical, emotional, sexual abuse, or neglect (including self-neglect in adults).
2. Action: Discuss with Designated Lead. Urgent referral to MASH (Children) or Adult Social Care if risk is immediate.
3. Documentation: Use factual, objective language. Do not promise confidentiality if disclosure is required for safety.

options.label: Continuity & QOF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Disease: Annual review (QOF) including bloods and symptom score.
2. Polypharmacy: Holistic medication review (SMR) with clinical pharmacist for patients on >10 meds.

options.label: Med3 (Fit Notes)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First 7 days: Patient self-certifies (Employer cannot demand Med3).
2. >7 days: Clinician issues Med3 based on clinical assessment.
3. Note: Focus on what patient 'can' do (phased return, amended duties) where possible.

options.label: Safeguarding (Adult/Child)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify: Physical, emotional, sexual abuse, or neglect (including self-neglect in adults).
2. Action: Discuss with Designated Lead. Urgent referral to MASH (Children) or Adult Social Care if risk is immediate.
3. Documentation: Use factual, objective language. Do not promise confidentiality if disclosure is required for safety.

options.label: Continuity & QOF
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Disease: Annual review (QOF) including bloods and symptom score.
2. Polypharmacy: Holistic medication review (SMR) with clinical pharmacist for patients on >10 meds.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnose: low muscle strength (± low mass) per EWGSOP2 or equivalent. First-line: progressive resistance training; adequate protein (1.2–1.5 g/kg/day). Treat malnutrition, inactivity, vitamin D deficiency.
2. Consider bone health/fracture risk (NG231). No licensed drug for sarcopenia alone. NICE NG231 (falls/bone), CKS, EWGSOP2.

options.label: Immediate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Safeguarding; consent for forensic examination; STI prophylaxis; emergency contraception; psychological first aid. NICE NG76, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sexual Assault Referral Centre (SARC); mental health; follow-up. NICE CKS.

options.label: Immediate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Safeguarding; consent for forensic examination; STI prophylaxis; emergency contraception; psychological first aid. NICE NG76, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sexual Assault Referral Centre (SARC); mental health; follow-up. NICE CKS.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Insomnia: sleep hygiene; CBT-i first-line. Exclude OSA, RLS, psychiatric cause. NICE NG215, CKS.

options.label: Referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Sleep study if OSA suspected. Refer sleep clinic if refractory. NICE CKS.

options.label: NRT
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Nicotine patch + short-acting (gum/lozenge) for cravings. 8–12 weeks. Adjust dose by smoking level. NICE NG92.

options.label: Varenicline
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Varenicline 500 mcg OD 3 days, then 1 mg bd 12 weeks. Start 1–2 weeks before quit date. NICE NG92.

options.label: Bupropion
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Bupropion 150 mg OD 6 days then 150 mg bd 7–9 weeks. Contraindicated in seizure, eating disorder. NICE NG92.

options.label: LAMA+LABA (Dual Therapy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. First-line for patients with persistent breathlessness or exacerbations despite SABA/LAMA mono.
2. Inhalers: e.g. Anoro Ellipta, Ultibro Breezhaler, Spiolto Respimat.
3. Action: Check technique; offer Pulmonary Rehab if MRC ≥ 2. NICE NG115.

options.label: Triple Therapy (LABA+LAMA+ICS)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Indication: Blood eosinophil count ≥ 0.3 x10^9/L OR ≥ 1 severe / 2 moderate exacerbations per year.
2. Inhalers: Trelegy Ellipta or Trimbow.
3. Risk: Discuss increased risk of pneumonia with ICS use. NICE NG115.

options.label: Refractory / Advanced COPD
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chronic Macrolide: Consider Azithromycin 250mg tiw if non-smoker and frequent exacerbations (requires baseline ECG & LFT).
2. Oxygen: Assess for LTOT (Long Term Oxygen Therapy) if pO2 < 7.3 kPa stable.
3. Referral: Lung volume reduction or Transplant assessment. NICE NG115.

options.label: Exacerbation / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Moderate: Increase SABA; add prednisolone 30 mg 5–7 days; consider antibiotic if purulent sputum.
2. Admit: Severe (respiratory failure, confusion, cyanosis), or poor response. NICE NG115, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rest (physical and cognitive) until symptom-free; then gradual return. No return to sport within 24 hours; no competition before 21 days (grassroots). Avoid alcohol.
2. Red flags (999): LOC >5 min, seizure, focal deficit, repeated vomiting, skull fracture, drowsiness, worsening. Refer if symptoms >28 days or repeated concussion. NICE NG232, UK concussion guidance.

tools.title: Superficial venous thrombosis in primary care – Management

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Differentiate from DVT (Wells, D-dimer if needed). If near saphenofemoral junction consider anticoagulation. NICE NG158, CKS.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. NSAID or topical; consider prophylactic dose LMWH if extensive or high risk. NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected GCA
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent high-dose steroid (e.g. prednisolone 40–60 mg); same-day CRP/ESR; refer ophthalmology if visual symptoms. Do not delay steroid for biopsy. NICE NG210.

options.label: Follow-up
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Taper steroid; bone protection. Monitor relapse. NICE NG210, CKS.

options.label: Anaemia (iron / B12 / folate / ACD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Iron: oral ferrous sulfate first; IV if intolerant or urgent. Treat cause; recheck Hb; continue 3 months after normal. B12: hydroxocobalamin IM; check folate first. Folate: folic acid 5 mg; do not give alone if B12 low. ACD: treat cause; IV iron only if CKD/inflammatory barrier. 2WW if unexplained or red flags. NICE NG24, NG241.

options.label: Anticoagulation (DOAC / warfarin / reversal)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DOAC first-line for VTE/AF (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran); renal dose. Warfarin if DOAC unsuitable (mechanical valve, antiphospholipid). Bleeding risk: ORBIT/HAS-BLED; address modifiable. Reversal: idarucizumab (dabigatran); andexanet (apixaban/rivaroxaban, life-threatening); vitamin K + PCC (warfarin). NICE NG196, NG158.

options.label: Thrombosis (DVT/PE / duration / thrombophilia)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: Wells/D-dimer; image if positive. Treat with DOAC ≥3 months; extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk. Refer: thrombophilia (young, family history), cancer-associated, anticoagulation failure. NICE NG158.

options.label: Cytopenia / malignancy (2WW)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 2WW: Unexplained cytopenia, lymphadenopathy, suspected lymphoma/leukaemia, myeloma. Neutropenia: exclude drugs/infection; refer if persistent. Urgent: severe thrombocytopenia with bleeding, major bleed on anticoagulant. NICE NG12, NG24.

options.label: Pre-travel
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Vaccinations per destination (NaTHNaC); malaria chemoprophylaxis if indicated. Altitude: gradual ascent; acetazolamide 125–250 mg bd if AMS risk. Diving: fitness-to-dive assessment; exclude cardiac/respiratory contraindications.
2. Travellers' diarrhoea: hygiene; loperamide for symptoms; standby antibiotic (e.g. azithromycin) per local resistance. Complex (diabetes, anticoagulation, immunosuppression): consider travel clinic. NICE CKS Travel, NaTHNaC.

options.label: Suspected DVT (Wells ≥ 2)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (NICE NG158):
1. Action: Urgent Proximal Leg US within 4h (or interim anticoagulation if wait >4h).
2. Result: If US negative but D-dimer positive, repeat US in 6-8 days.

options.label: Suspected PE (Wells ≥ 4.5)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Immediate: CTPA (Computed Tomographic Pulmonary Angiography). Interim anticoagulation (e.g. Apixaban 10mg bd) if scan delayed >1h.
2. V/Q Scan: Preferred if renal impairment (eGFR <30) or severe allergy to contrast.
3. Note: If PE likely, assess PESI score for suitability of outpatient management.

options.label: Low Probability (Wells < Score threshold)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnostic: D-dimer (age-adjusted if over 50). If negative → VTE unlikely. If positive → Proceed to imaging (US or CTPA).

options.label: Anticoagulation duration / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. DVT/PE: DOAC 3 months minimum. Extend if unprovoked or ongoing risk (cancer, thrombophilia).
2. Refer: Anticoagulation failure, thrombophilia testing (young, family history), cancer-associated. NICE NG158.

options.label: Apixaban (1st-line)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 10mg bd for 7 days, then 5mg bd.
2. Duration: 3 months (provoked/low risk), 6 months+ or indefinite (unprovoked or recurrence). NICE NG158.

options.label: Rivaroxaban (Alternative)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Titration: 15mg bd for 21 days, then 20mg OD.

options.label: Smoking cessation
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. E-cigarettes can support quit attempt. Weigh benefits vs unknown long-term risk. NICE NG209, CKS.

options.label: Safety-net
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Report adverse effects via Yellow Card. Avoid in pregnancy if possible. NICE CKS.

options.label: B12 Deficiency - Replacement
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Non-dietary (e.g. Pernicious Anaemia): Hydroxocobalamin 1mg IM every other day for 2 weeks (loading), then 1mg IM every 3 months for life.
2. Dietary: Oral cyanocobalamin 50-150mcg daily between meals, or two 1mg injections per year.
3. Monitoring: Reticulocyte count at 7-10 days; Hb/MCV at 8 weeks.
4. Review: Exclude co-existing Iron/Folate deficiency if response sub-optimal. NICE CKS.

options.label: Iron deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Oral first: ferrous sulfate 200 mg od (or bd if tolerated) or ferrous fumarate 210 mg od. Take with vitamin C; avoid tea with dose. Recheck Hb in 2–4 weeks; continue 3 months after normal. Treat cause (bleed, malabsorption). NICE NG24.
2. IV iron: if oral intolerant, not absorbing, or urgent (e.g. symptomatic, pre-op). Exclude infection; give per local protocol (e.g. ferric derisomaltose, ferric carboxymaltose). NICE NG24, NG8.

options.label: B12 deficiency
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Hydroxocobalamin 1 mg IM: 3× per week for 2 weeks, then 1 mg every 3 months (or 2-monthly if neurological involvement). Check folate first (replace if low; do not give folate alone if B12 low – risk of subacute degeneration). Oral B12 only if mild, compliant, and no neurological features. NICE NG241, NG24.

options.label: Folate / macrocytic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Folate: folic acid 5 mg od; treat cause (diet, malabsorption, drugs). If macrocytic: check B12 and folate; treat both if both low. If both normal consider alcohol, hypothyroid, MDS – refer if unexplained. NICE NG24.

options.label: Anaemia of chronic disease / 2WW
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. ACD: normocytic; ferritin normal or raised; CRP may be raised. Treat underlying condition. IV iron only if functional deficit and (CKD or inflammatory barrier to oral). ESA only per nephrology in CKD. NICE NG24, NG203.
2. 2WW: Unexplained anaemia with weight loss, bleeding, or other red flags. NICE NG12.

options.label: Deficiency (<30 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Loading: 300,000 IU total over 6-10 weeks (e.g. 20,000 IU twice weekly for 7 weeks or 50,000 IU weekly for 6 weeks).
2. Maintenance: 800-2000 IU daily (or 20,000-40,000 IU monthly) lifelong if risk factors persist.
3. Safety: Avoid loading if primary hyperparathyroidism or renal stones suspected. ROS Guidelines.

options.label: Insufficiency (30-50 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Strategy: Advise dietary sources (oily fish, eggs) and safe sun exposure.
2. Supplement: 800-1000 IU daily as maintenance; loading not routinely required unless symptomatic or high-risk of progression. NICE CKS.

tools.title: Vitamin D deficiency in adults – Management

options.label: Deficiency (<30 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Loading: 300,000 IU total over 6-10 weeks (e.g. 20,000 IU twice weekly for 7 weeks or 50,000 IU weekly for 6 weeks).
2. Maintenance: 800-2000 IU daily (or 20,000-40,000 IU monthly) lifelong if risk factors persist.
3. Safety: Avoid loading if primary hyperparathyroidism or renal stones suspected. ROS Guidelines.

options.label: Insufficiency (30-50 nmol/L)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Strategy: Advise dietary sources (oily fish, eggs) and safe sun exposure.
2. Supplement: 800-1000 IU daily as maintenance; loading not routinely required unless symptomatic or high-risk of progression. NICE CKS.

options.label: Recognition & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Recognise: abuse or neglect (physical, sexual, financial, emotional, neglect). Document factually; do not investigate alone. Refer to adult social care per local policy. If immediate risk: police. MARAC if high-risk domestic abuse. NICE NG108, CKS.

options.label: Capacity & consent
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If adult has capacity: respect their decision unless others at risk (e.g. children). If lacking capacity: best interests; share information if necessary to protect. Discuss with safeguarding lead. NICE NG108.

options.label: Assessment
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. BMI, waist; comorbidities. Set target. Behaviour change; diet and activity. NICE CG189, CKS.

options.label: Pharmacotherapy / referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider orlistat or GLP-1 if criteria met. Refer bariatric if BMI ≥40 or ≥35 with comorbidity. NICE CG189.

tools.title: Womens Health for Primary Care with Dr Anne Connolly – Management

options.label: Learning resource
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Use for CPD. Apply NICE CKS and NG23 (menopause), contraception, gynae guidelines. No single pathway.

options.label: AUDIT & brief advice
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. AUDIT or FAST; feedback on units and risk. Brief advice: reduce consumption; set goals; written info.
2. Signpost to support (e.g. Drink Free Days). Follow-up if harmful use. Refer if dependent or requested. NICE CG115, PH24.

options.label: Mild/Moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lid hygiene (warm compresses). Preservative-free lubricants (e.g. Hylo-Forte, Viscotears). Ointment at night (e.g. Lacri-Lube). NICE CKS Dry Eye.

options.label: Severe or refractory
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to Ophthalmology. Consider punctal plugs or ciclosporin drops. Exclude Sjogren's syndrome (check ANA, Ro/La).

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Warm compress; lid massage. Most resolve in weeks. Refer if large, persistent, or diagnostic uncertainty (exclude sebaceous gland carcinoma).
2. CKS Blepharitis and chalazion.

options.label: Bacterial conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds (max 5 days). Fusidic acid 1% if pregnant. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day. RCOphth; NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected corneal ulcer / Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Contact lens wear? Pain, photophobia? Same-day ophthalmology. Stop contact lenses. Do not use steroid. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Scleritis (deep boring pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Deep scleral pain; systemic associations (rheumatoid, ANCA). Same-day ophthalmology. Urgent within 24 h. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Acute uveitis / Angle-closure glaucoma
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Uveitis: ciliary flush, small pupil – same-day ophthalmology (steroid + dilating drops specialist). Angle-closure: pain, hard globe, nausea – emergency; acetazolamide if remote. RCOphth; NICE NG81.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: pain, photophobia, reduced vision, contact lens wear, trauma, chemical. Avoid topical steroid until cause known. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Suspected Microbial Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. IMMEDIATE: Emergency Same-Day Ophthalmology referral (A&E eye clinic).
2. First Aid: Stop contact lens wear immediately; do not patch the eye.
3. Note: High risk of permanent vision loss/perforation within 24-48h if untreated. Moorfields Guidelines.

options.label: Mild/Moderate
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Lid hygiene (warm compresses). Preservative-free lubricants (e.g. Hylo-Forte, Viscotears). Ointment at night (e.g. Lacri-Lube). NICE CKS Dry Eye.

options.label: Severe or refractory
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to Ophthalmology. Consider punctal plugs or ciclosporin drops. Exclude Sjogren's syndrome (check ANA, Ro/La).

options.label: Dry eyes / Blepharitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dry eye: Preservative-free artificial tears (hypromellose, carmellose); lid hygiene; review screen use. Blepharitis: warm compresses, lid massage, lid hygiene. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Stye / Chalazion / Subconjunctival haemorrhage
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stye (hordeolum): warm compresses; chloramphenicol if infected. Chalazion: warm compresses; refer if large or persistent. Subconjunctival haemorrhage: reassure; check BP if recurrent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Viral/allergic: cool compresses, lubricants. Bacterial: chloramphenicol 0.5% 2-hourly 2 days then qds. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day (RCOphth). NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Glaucoma (chronic open-angle)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Ophthalmology-led. Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. latanoprost) first-line. Monitor IOP and visual fields. Urgent referral if acute angle-closure suspected (pain, nausea, hard globe). NICE NG81; RCOphth.

options.label: When to refer (RCOphth)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: corneal ulcer/keratitis, acute uveitis, acute angle-closure, scleritis, chemical/trauma, sudden vision loss, post-surgery pain. 2WW: referable diabetic retinopathy. Routine: chronic glaucoma, dry eye, chalazion. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE NG12, NG28, NG81.

options.label: Newly diagnosed/Suspected
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Refer to secondary care for diagnosis and treatment initiation. First-line usually Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. Latanoprost). NICE NG81.

options.label: Community Monitoring
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Check IOP, visual fields, and adherence. Beta-blockers (e.g. Timolol) used as adjunctive; check for contraindications (Asthma/Heart Block).

options.label: Sudden painless loss of vision (RAO / CRVO)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Retinal artery occlusion (RAO): Emergency; stroke pathway (TIA workup, carotid/embolic). Same-day ophthalmology/eye casualty.
2. Central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO): Same-day ophthalmology; monitor for neovascularisation. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care.

options.label: Acute angle-closure glaucoma
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Painful red eye, nausea, hard globe, semi-dilated pupil. Emergency ophthalmology. Acetazolamide 500 mg IV or PO if remote from hospital (per local policy). RCOphth; NICE NG81.

options.label: Floaters and flashes (retinal detachment)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Retinal detachment until proven otherwise. Same-day urgent ophthalmology. Do not delay. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care.

options.label: Post-surgery / endophthalmitis / chemical
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Painful red eye after eye surgery: same-day ophthalmology (endophthalmitis). Chemical injury: irrigate with saline immediately then urgent refer. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care.

options.label: Bacterial conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Chloramphenicol 0.5% drops 2-hourly for 2 days then qds (max 5 days). Fusidic acid 1% if pregnant. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day. RCOphth; NICE CKS.

options.label: Suspected corneal ulcer / Keratitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Contact lens wear? Pain, photophobia? Same-day ophthalmology. Stop contact lenses. Do not use steroid. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Scleritis (deep boring pain)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Deep scleral pain; systemic associations (rheumatoid, ANCA). Same-day ophthalmology. Urgent within 24 h. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Acute uveitis / Angle-closure glaucoma
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Uveitis: ciliary flush, small pupil – same-day ophthalmology (steroid + dilating drops specialist). Angle-closure: pain, hard globe, nausea – emergency; acetazolamide if remote. RCOphth; NICE NG81.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: pain, photophobia, reduced vision, contact lens wear, trauma, chemical. Avoid topical steroid until cause known. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Warm compress; lid hygiene. Most resolve. Incision if pointing abscess. Topical antibiotic if associated blepharitis. Refer if orbital spread or recurrence.
2. CKS Hordeola and styes.

options.label: Management
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reassurance; no treatment needed. Check BP if hypertensive. If recurrent or bleeding disorder, consider workup. Red flags: trauma, anticoagulation, painful or visual change – assess fully.
2. CKS Red eye.

options.label: No red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Advise stay active; paracetamol + NSAID short-term. Consider manual therapy. Do not offer imaging. Review at 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Red flags (cauda equina, fracture, infection)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Cauda equina: emergency referral. Consider fracture if trauma/steroids; infection if fever. MRI if nerve root compression suspected for surgical option. NICE NG59.

options.label: Sciatica / nerve root
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Advise stay active; analgesia. Consider pregabalin/gabapentin for neuropathic pain if significant.
2. Refer if severe or progressive; consider MRI for surgical option if not improving after 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Safety net
options.guidance: SAFETY: Reattend if new leg weakness, saddle numbness, urinary retention, or fever with back pain. Cauda equina: emergency. NICE NG59.

options.label: Assessment & non-pharmacological
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Assess: site, impact, red flags (weight loss, night pain, neurology). Biopsychosocial. Set goals. Non-pharmacological first: exercise, physiotherapy, psychological (CBT, ACT). NICE NG193.
2. Paracetamol may be considered; avoid long-term NSAID. NICE NG193.

options.label: Neuropathic pain
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. First-line: gabapentin or pregabalin, or amitriptyline (low dose nocte). Second-line: switch or add. Duloxetine for chronic musculoskeletal pain. Review benefit and harms. NICE NG193, NG173.

options.label: Opioid (only if benefit > harm)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Offer only after non-pharmacological and non-opioid options; shared decision-making. Lowest dose; regular review. Taper if no benefit or harm. Avoid long-term for chronic non-cancer pain where possible. Do not offer codeine. NICE NG193.

options.label: Soft tissue / tendon
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Rest, ice, analgesia; physio. Plantar fasciitis: stretch, orthotics. Tennis elbow: eccentric exercises. Rotator cuff: physio; consider subacromial injection. De Quervain's: splint, NSAID; steroid injection first dorsal compartment – see 'De Quervain's – injection' pathway. NICE CKS, NG124.

options.label: Joint / arthritis / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GCA: urgent high-dose steroid; same-day rheumatology. Polymyalgia: steroid; monitor. Pseudogout: NSAID. Septic arthritis: emergency referral – do not delay. Hot swollen joint: aspirate (MC&S), admit. NICE NG210, NG100.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Urgent: Septic arthritis, GCA, cord compression, acute compartment syndrome. Routine: Persistent despite conservative treatment; diagnostic uncertainty; need for surgery or specialist injection. NICE CKS.

options.label: First-line
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Gabapentin (titrate from 300 mg nocte) or pregabalin, or amitriptyline (10–25 mg nocte, increase if needed). Review at 2–4 weeks. Consider cause (diabetic, post-herpetic, trigeminal). NICE NG173, NG193.

options.label: Second-line & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. If inadequate: switch or add; consider duloxetine for musculoskeletal overlap. Refer pain service if refractory or complex. Trigeminal neuralgia: carbamazepine; refer. NICE NG173, NG193.

options.label: When to taper
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider taper if: no clear benefit, patient request, side effects, high dose, or risk. Shared decision-making; set goals. Do not stop abruptly – risk withdrawal and rebound pain. NICE NG193.

options.label: How to taper
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reduce slowly (e.g. 10% of dose every 1–2 weeks); slower if long-term. Switch to morphine equivalent if mixed opioids; reduce one drug at a time. Support: explain, treat withdrawal symptoms, non-pharmacological options. NICE NG193, CKS.

options.label: When to taper
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Consider taper if: no clear benefit, patient request, side effects, high dose, or risk. Shared decision-making; set goals. Do not stop abruptly – risk withdrawal and rebound pain. NICE NG193.

options.label: How to taper
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Reduce slowly (e.g. 10% of dose every 1–2 weeks); slower if long-term. Switch to morphine equivalent if mixed opioids; reduce one drug at a time. Support: explain, treat withdrawal symptoms, non-pharmacological options. NICE NG193, CKS.

options.label: Principles
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Paracetamol first; add NSAID if no contraindication (short-term; PPI if GI risk). Opioid only if severe; lowest dose, shortest duration (e.g. 3 days); avoid codeine where possible. NICE NG193.
2. Red flags: fracture, infection, cauda equina, ischaemia – urgent. NICE NG59.

options.label: When to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: cauda equina, cord compression, septic arthritis, acute abdomen. 2WW: suspected malignancy, red flags. Routine: persistent after expected healing. NICE NG12, NG59.

options.label: Stepwise analgesia
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Step 1: paracetamol + NSAID (if appropriate). Step 2: add weak opioid (e.g. codeine or tramadol). Step 3: strong opioid (morphine first-line; oxycodone/fentanyl if needed). Always: regular dose + PRN breakthrough (e.g. 1/6 of 24h dose). Anticipate constipation (laxative) and nausea (anti-emetic). NICE NG142.

options.label: Breakthrough & neuropathic
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Breakthrough: same opioid, 1/10–1/6 of 24h dose, repeat as needed (e.g. 1-hourly). Neuropathic: add gabapentinoid or amitriptyline. Bone pain: consider NSAID or bisphosphonate. Review regularly. NICE NG142, CKS.

tools.title: GP Triage – common urgent presentations: 999 / same day / 24–48 h / self-care

options.label: Breathlessness, allergic reaction, choking, severe bleeding
options.guidance:
TRIAGE:
• BREATHLESSNESS — 999: unable to speak in sentences, cyanosis/blue lips, drowsy/confused, chest pain, stridor, new sudden onset at rest, sats <92% if measured, known asthma not responding to 10 puffs salbutamol, anaphylaxis. SAME DAY: worsening over hours, fever + productive cough + unwell (pneumonia), asthma/COPD exacerbation responding partly to inhaler, calf swelling (PE), new ankle oedema/orthopnoea (heart failure). 24–48 h: gradual onset over days, exertional only, no red flags. SELF-CARE: mild URTI with cough, anxiety-related with normal observations — safety-net.
• ALLERGIC REACTION — 999 (ANAPHYLAXIS, CG134/RCUK): airway swelling (lips/tongue/throat tightness, hoarse voice), wheeze/breathlessness, dizziness/collapse/pale/floppy, rapidly spreading rash WITH any of these → use adrenaline auto-injector immediately if available (adult 500 micrograms IM, child 150–300 micrograms), lie flat, legs raised, second dose after 5 min. SAME DAY: urticaria/angioedema without airway or breathing symptoms but spreading, first reaction to a new food/drug/sting, ACE-inhibitor angioedema (stop drug). 24–48 h/SELF-CARE: localised urticaria, mild itch — cetirizine 10 mg (child by age), avoid trigger; refer allergy clinic after any anaphylaxis/systemic reaction (prescribe 2 auto-injectors + training before leaving).
• CHOKING — 999 if cannot cough/speak/breathe (give 5 back blows then 5 abdominal thrusts — chest thrusts in infants <1 year; CPR if unresponsive); after any abdominal thrusts → same-day medical review; SAME DAY if persisting cough/wheeze/stridor after choking episode (inhaled foreign body — chest X-ray; children with peanuts/small objects → paediatrics even if well); SELF-CARE if cleared fully, well, normal breathing.
• SEVERE BLEEDING — 999: bleeding not controlled by 10 min firm direct pressure, spurting/pooling, amputation, bleeding with pallor/faintness/sweating, haematemesis, melaena with dizziness, on anticoagulant with any significant bleed, pregnancy >20 weeks with bleeding, post-partum haemorrhage. SAME DAY: nosebleed >20 min despite pinching soft part leaning forward (ED for packing), rectal bleeding large volume/on anticoagulant, wound needing closure (within 12–24 h — minor injury unit), haematuria with clots. 24–48 h: small rectal bleed, bruising on anticoagulant (INR/FBC). SELF-CARE: minor cut controlled with pressure, small nosebleed stopped.

options.label: Abdominal pain, heavy vaginal bleeding, diabetic unwell, overdose/poisoning
options.guidance:
TRIAGE:
• ABDOMINAL PAIN — 999: collapse/shock, rigid abdomen, pain + vomiting blood, suspected AAA (>50, severe back/abdominal pain, pulsatile mass, known aneurysm), testicular pain sudden onset (torsion — within 6 h; same-day surgical if not 999), pregnancy with severe pain/shoulder-tip pain/faintness (ectopic). SAME DAY: severe constant pain >6 h, RIF pain (appendicitis), fever + pain, bilious/persistent vomiting, unable to pass stool or wind with distension, pain in child <5 with lethargy/drawing up legs (intussusception) or in known diabetic (DKA), first-trimester pain/bleeding (EPAU), loin pain with fever, pain with jaundice, elderly/immunosuppressed with new pain. 24–48 h: colicky intermittent pain, dyspepsia, change in bowel habit without red flags, suspected UTI with mild symptoms. SELF-CARE: mild cramps, known IBS pattern, gastroenteritis tolerating fluids — safety-net.
• HEAVY VAGINAL BLEEDING — 999: soaking a pad every 30–60 min for >2 h with dizziness/fainting/pallor, pregnancy >12 weeks with heavy bleeding, bleeding with severe pain and collapse (ectopic). SAME DAY: heavy bleeding in early pregnancy (EPAU/gynaecology), bleeding + fever/offensive discharge (sepsis), post-menopausal bleeding with large volume, bleeding on anticoagulant, passing large clots and symptomatic (FBC). 24–48 h/ROUTINE: heavy periods without acute symptoms (NG88 — FBC, tranexamic acid 1 g tds during menses, consider LNG-IUS; 2WW if post-menopausal bleeding, ≥55 with unexplained vaginal discharge or thrombocytosis, intermenstrual/post-coital bleeding with pelvic mass/abnormal cervix). SELF-CARE: slightly heavier period, no symptoms of anaemia — book routine review.
• DIABETIC UNWELL / HYPO — 999: unconscious or fitting (give IM glucagon 1 mg if available, do not give oral), unable to swallow, hypo not responding to 3 cycles of 15–20 g fast glucose at 15-min intervals, DKA features (vomiting, abdominal pain, Kussmaul breathing, drowsy, ketones ≥3 mmol/L / 'high'), hyperglycaemia with reduced consciousness. SAME DAY: ketones 1.5–2.9 with hyperglycaemia or unable to keep fluids down (sick-day rules failing), recurrent hypos in last 24 h, hypo on sulfonylurea/long-acting insulin (prolonged — observe), infection in diabetic with foot ulcer/cellulitis, glucose persistently >25 mmol/L. 24–48 h: raised glucose with no ketones and well (medication review; increase monitoring), single explained mild hypo. SELF-CARE: sick-day rules (never stop insulin, check glucose/ketones 2–4 hourly, 100 mL fluid/hour, pause SGLT2i/metformin if vomiting), hypo treated with 15–20 g glucose then long-acting carbohydrate.
• OVERDOSE / POISONING — 999/ED for ALL deliberate overdoses regardless of amount or apparent wellness (paracetamol is silent for 24 h; antidote window), any ingestion with drowsiness/vomiting/arrhythmia, button battery or magnet ingestion in children (EMERGENCY — oesophageal burn within 2 h), caustic/petroleum ingestion, carbon monoxide exposure. SAME DAY: accidental ingestion of medicines in a child (check TOXBASE — many need ED observation, e.g. iron, tricyclics, calcium-channel blockers, sulfonylureas, opioids), plant/mushroom ingestion with symptoms, iron tablets. 24–48 h: accidental minor ingestion confirmed non-toxic on TOXBASE/NPIS 0344 892 0111 (clinician line) — observe at home. Mental health: all deliberate self-harm → same-day psychosocial assessment (liaison psychiatry/crisis team); do not use this tool to decide against assessment.

options.label: Child fever, ear pain, dental emergency, limb injury, burns, swallowed object
options.guidance:
TRIAGE:
• CHILD WITH FEVER (NG143 traffic light) — 999: non-blanching rash, unresponsive/difficult to rouse, grunting/severe respiratory distress, seizure >5 min, mottled/blue/pale with cold extremities, bulging fontanelle with drowsiness, <3 months with temp ≥38 and unwell. SAME DAY (within hours; face-to-face): any infant <3 months with fever ≥38 °C; 3–6 months ≥39 °C; any amber feature — pallor, not responding normally, reduced activity, nasal flaring, tachypnoea/tachycardia, CRT ≥3 s, reduced urine output, fever ≥5 days, limb/joint swelling or not weight-bearing, rigors; parent concern. 24–48 h: fever <5 days, green features, feeding >50%, wet nappies, playful between doses of antipyretic. SELF-CARE: fluids, paracetamol OR ibuprofen (alternate only if distress persists), light clothing, no tepid sponging; check for rash with a glass; return if worse or new symptoms; do not send to nursery.
• EAR PAIN — SAME DAY: severe pain with fever and bulging drum in child <2 (consider antibiotics if bilateral <2 years or discharging — amoxicillin 5–7 days), discharge with mastoid swelling/tenderness or ear pushed forward (MASTOIDITIS — ED), facial weakness, vertigo/severe headache/neck stiffness, diabetic/immunosuppressed with severe otalgia (malignant otitis externa), post-ear-surgery, foreign body in ear with pain/button battery (999). 24–48 h: otitis media without red flags not settling after 3 days of analgesia, otitis externa (acetic acid/antibiotic-steroid drops), ear wax (olive oil drops 5 days then review). SELF-CARE: mild earache with URTI <3 days — paracetamol/ibuprofen, most resolve in 3 days; delayed antibiotic prescription option.
• DENTAL — 999/ED: facial swelling spreading to eye or neck, trismus (cannot open mouth 2 fingers), difficulty swallowing/breathing, drooling (Ludwig's angina), avulsed permanent tooth (reimplant within 1 h — hold by crown, store in milk, dentist/ED immediately), uncontrolled bleeding after extraction. SAME DAY (urgent dental care — NHS 111 dental): dental abscess with fever/swelling (GP may give phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg qds or amoxicillin 500 mg tds 5 days ONLY as a bridge if systemic signs and no dental access — antibiotics do not treat the cause), severe uncontrolled toothache, broken tooth with exposed pulp. 24–48 h: toothache controlled with ibuprofen + paracetamol, lost filling. SELF-CARE: sensitivity, mild pain — ibuprofen 400 mg + paracetamol 1 g, salt-water rinses, book dentist.
• LIMB INJURY — 999: open fracture, deformity with absent pulse/white or blue limb, suspected hip fracture (shortened externally rotated leg, cannot stand), amputation, crush injury, high-energy trauma. SAME DAY (minor injuries/ED): unable to weight-bear 4 steps (Ottawa), bony tenderness at malleoli/navicular/5th metatarsal/patella/fibular head, obvious deformity, wound over joint, suspected scaphoid fracture (snuffbox tenderness after fall on outstretched hand — X-ray even if first negative), hot swollen joint, numbness/weakness distal to injury, tendon rupture (Achilles — cannot plantarflex; biceps 'Popeye'), elderly on anticoagulants with head/limb injury. 24–48 h: sprain with some weight-bearing, soft-tissue swelling without bony tenderness. SELF-CARE: PRICE 48 h, ibuprofen/paracetamol, mobilise early; review if not improving at 1 week.
• BURNS — 999: airway burns (facial burns, singed nasal hair, hoarse voice, soot in sputum), >15% body surface adult (>10% child; palm of patient's hand = 1%), electrical/chemical burns (irrigate 20+ min), full-thickness (white/leathery/painless), circumferential limb/chest burns, burns with other trauma/smoke inhalation. SAME DAY (ED/burns unit): any burn to face, hands, feet, genitals, perineum, flexures or across joints; >1% full/partial thickness in child or >3% adult; all children <5 and >60 years with significant burns; non-accidental injury concern (glove-and-stocking scald, cigarette burns, inconsistent history — safeguarding); diabetic/immunosuppressed. 24–48 h: small partial-thickness burn blistered — cool 20 min running water (within 3 h of injury), cover with cling film/non-adherent dressing, analgesia, review for infection at 48 h, tetanus status. SELF-CARE: superficial erythema (sunburn-like) <1% — cool, moisturise, analgesia.
• SWALLOWED OBJECT — 999/ED immediately: BUTTON BATTERY (any size, even if well — X-ray; oesophageal battery removed within 2 h), 2+ magnets or magnet + metal, sharp objects (needles, open safety pins, fish/chicken bones with pain/drooling), objects >2.5 cm or >6 cm long, choking/drooling/unable to swallow saliva/chest pain (oesophageal impaction — food bolus also), vomiting/abdominal pain after ingestion, known oesophageal disease. SAME DAY: coin in child <5 (X-ray — if in oesophagus needs removal; stomach — can wait), any ingestion with symptoms. 24–48 h/SELF-CARE: small smooth blunt object (coin in older child/adult, bead) in a well, asymptomatic person — normal diet, check stools for 1–2 weeks (no laxatives/induced vomiting), return if abdominal pain, vomiting, fever, blood in stool, or not passed in 2–3 weeks (X-ray).

options.label: IM Adrenaline (999)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Adrenaline 1:1000 IM (anterolateral mid-thigh). Adult: 500mcg (0.5ml). Child 6-12: 300mcg. Child <6: 150mcg. Repeat every 5 mins if no improvement. High-flow O2. NICE NG193.

options.label: Consultant Strategic Approach
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN OVERVIEW:
1. **PTSD Philosophy**: Focus on 're-processing' traumatic memories rather than avoidance. 
2. **OCD Philosophy**: Focus on 'Exposure & Response Prevention' (ERP). Breaking the link between obsession and neutralizing compulsion.
3. **Meds**: SSRIs/SNRIs used primarily to 'quieten' the cognitive noise, facilitating engagement in intensive therapy. NICE NG116, CG31.

options.label: PTSD Evidence-Based Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Diagnosis: Re-experiencing (flashbacks), avoidance, and hyperarousal >1 month post-trauma.
2. 1st-line: **Trauma-focused CBT (TF-CBT)** or **EMDR** (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing).
3. Meds: Venlafaxine or SSRI (Sertraline) only if patient prefers or therapy failed. Do NOT use Benzos. NICE NG116.

options.label: Complex PTSD (C-PTSD)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Features: Core PTSD + disturbances in self-organization (affect dysregulation, negative self-concept, relational diffs).
2. Management: Requires longer-term stabilization phase followed by trauma-focused work. NICE NG116.

options.label: OCD Stepwise Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: **ERP** (Exposure & Response Prevention) +/- SSRI.
2. Meds: Often require higher doses (e.g., Fluoxetine 60-80mg, Sertraline 200mg). Trial for ≥12 weeks.
3. Resistance: Consider adding Clomipramine (TCA) or an atypical antipsychotic adjunct. NICE CG31.

options.label: No red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Advise stay active; paracetamol + NSAID short-term. Consider manual therapy. Do not offer imaging. Review at 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Red flags (cauda equina, fracture, infection)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Cauda equina: emergency referral. Consider fracture if trauma/steroids; infection if fever. MRI if nerve root compression suspected for surgical option. NICE NG59.

options.label: Sciatica / nerve root
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Advise stay active; analgesia. Consider pregabalin/gabapentin for neuropathic pain if significant.
2. Refer if severe or progressive; consider MRI for surgical option if not improving after 6 weeks. NICE NG59.

options.label: Safety net
options.guidance: SAFETY: Reattend if new leg weakness, saddle numbness, urinary retention, or fever with back pain. Cauda equina: emergency. NICE NG59.

options.label: Stable / likely angina
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. GTN prn; beta-blocker or CCB. Secondary prevention: aspirin, statin, ACEi if indicated.
2. Refer: Rapid Access Chest Pain Clinic for CTCA. NICE NG72.

options.label: Acute / possible ACS
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999; aspirin 300 mg if no contraindication.
2. Do not delay for troponin in primary care if typical presentation. NICE NG185.

options.label: Non-cardiac / musculoskeletal
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude cardiac cause (ECG, troponin if indicated). Consider costochondritis, muscle strain, Tietze's; NSAID/analgesia; reassurance.
2. If GORD/reflux: trial PPI. If anxiety: support and exclude organic cause first. NICE NG72, CKS.

options.label: Safety net
options.guidance: SAFETY: Reattend if central/crushing pain, breathlessness, collapse, or pain at rest. If suspected ACS call 999. NICE NG72, NG185.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Emergency (999). Collapse/unconsciousness is time-critical. Call 999 for: unwitnessed collapse; not fully alert (GCS <15); chest pain or severe breathlessness before/during collapse; known cardiac or seizure disorder with prolonged recovery or first fit; head injury with collapse; suspected overdose/poisoning; hypoglycaemia not responding to oral glucose; stroke signs (FAST); anaphylaxis; any doubt. Do not delay. NICE CKS, NG51.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 2. SAME DAY / URGENT? Cannot wait 24–48 h – see synopsis.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day GP, UTC or A&E. Use when: witnessed collapse but recurrent or in concerning context (e.g. during exertion, with palpitations); possible arrhythmia; diabetic with hypoglycaemic collapse needing review; first seizure (unless 999 criteria); collapse in elderly or with comorbidities needing same-day assessment. Direct booking per local policy. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 3. 24–48 H / ROUTINE? Stable but needs assessment.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: GP or nurse appointment within 24–48 h. Fully recovered, no red flags, but needs ECG or follow-up (e.g. first simple vasovagal in young adult; medication review). Safety-net: reattend or 999 if recurrence or worsening. NICE CKS.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Self-care. Single witnessed vasovagal (e.g. pain, emotion, prolonged standing), fully recovered, no red flags. Advice: hydration, avoid triggers, sit/lie if premonitory symptoms. When to reattend: recurrence, chest pain, breathlessness, collapse without clear trigger. Provide written or verbal safety-net. Follow up with GP if no improvement or further episodes. NICE CKS, Urgent care.

options.label: No
options.guidance: Reassess using questions above or arrange same-day/urgent review. NICE CKS.

options.label: Dry eyes / Blepharitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Dry eye: Preservative-free artificial tears (hypromellose, carmellose); lid hygiene; review screen use. Blepharitis: warm compresses, lid massage, lid hygiene. NICE CKS; RCOphth.

options.label: Stye / Chalazion / Subconjunctival haemorrhage
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Stye (hordeolum): warm compresses; chloramphenicol if infected. Chalazion: warm compresses; refer if large or persistent. Subconjunctival haemorrhage: reassure; check BP if recurrent. NICE CKS.

options.label: Conjunctivitis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Viral/allergic: cool compresses, lubricants. Bacterial: chloramphenicol 0.5% 2-hourly 2 days then qds. Safety-net: pain, photophobia, vision loss, contact lens – same-day (RCOphth). NICE CKS Red eye.

options.label: Glaucoma (chronic open-angle)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Ophthalmology-led. Prostaglandin analogue (e.g. latanoprost) first-line. Monitor IOP and visual fields. Urgent referral if acute angle-closure suspected (pain, nausea, hard globe). NICE NG81; RCOphth.

options.label: When to refer (RCOphth)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Same-day: corneal ulcer/keratitis, acute uveitis, acute angle-closure, scleritis, chemical/trauma, sudden vision loss, post-surgery pain. 2WW: referable diabetic retinopathy. Routine: chronic glaucoma, dry eye, chalazion. RCOphth Emergency Eye Care; NICE NG12, NG28, NG81.

options.label: First Seizure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Urgency: Refer to 'First Seizure Clinic' (within 2 weeks). NICE NG217.
2. Investigation: EEG + MRI Brain (Standard protocol including coronal T2/FLAIR sessions). 
3. Safety: High-risk activities (driving, swimming, working at heights) must stop until specialist review.

options.label: Focal Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Lamotrigine or Levetiracetam (Keppra). NICE NG217.

options.label: Generalized Seizures
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Sodium Valproate (Epilim) - **Strict warning: Not for use in women/girls of childbearing potential unless Pregnancy Prevention Programme in place.**
2. Alternative: Levetiracetam or Lamotrigine.

steps.question: 1. GCS < 15, or any dangerous mechanism / high-energy injury?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Emergency (999). Do not delay. NICE CG176.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 2. Current or recent seizure, or suspected open/depressed skull fracture, or basal skull fracture signs?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Emergency (999). NICE CG176.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 3. Age ≥ 65, or coagulopathy, or vomiting ≥ 2 episodes, or amnesia, or loss of consciousness?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day / urgent imaging (CT head) per NICE CG176. A&E or UTC with CT. Safety-net: 999 if worsening.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 4. Minor head injury with no high-risk features?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Self-care + safety-net. Advice on rest, observation, when to reattend (vomiting, drowsiness, worsening headache, visual/speech/balance problems). Provide written safety-net. NICE CG176, CKS.

options.label: No
options.guidance: Reassess or arrange same-day review. NICE CG176.

options.label: First-line: Stratified Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH Guidelines):
1. Combined Approach: Soluble Aspirin (900mg) or Naproxen (500mg) + Triptan (e.g. Sumatriptan 50-100mg) + Prokinetic Anti-emetic (Metoclopramide 10mg).
2. Note: Treat early at onset of headache, not aura. Avoid opioids (risk of Medication Overuse Headache). NICE NG150.

options.label: Triptan Failure
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Switch: Trial different triptan or different formulation (e.g. Sumatriptan Nasal Spray or SC).
2. MOH: Review for Medication Overuse Headache if using triptans ≥ 10 days/month. NICE NG150.

options.label: Initial Choice (Indicated if ≥2 attacks/month)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (BASH/RCP):
1. First-line choices: Propranolol (80-160mg), Amitriptyline (10-50mg nocte), or Topiramate (titrate to 50mg-100mg - warn about teratogenicity/birth control).
2. Second-line: Candesartan (8-16mg) - widely used by neurologists off-label but supported by evidence. NICE NG150.

options.label: Specialist Interventions (Consultant Care)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. CGRP Monoclonals (e.g. Erenumab, Fremanezumab): Indicated if ≥4 migraine days/month and failure of 3 oral preventatives. NICE TA.
2. Botox: Protocolized 31-site injection (PREEMPT) if chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, 8 being migraine). NICE NG150.

options.label: Tension-type
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Paracetamol or NSAID. Address stress, posture. Avoid frequent analgesia (medication-overuse). NICE NG150.

options.label: Red flags / when to refer
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: Thunderclap (SAH), new sudden severe, fever + neck stiffness (meningitis), papilloedema.
2. Refer: New headache ≥50y, progressive, positional, or focal neurology. NICE NG150, NG51.

steps.question: 1. EMERGENCY (999)? Immediate risk to life or others – see synopsis.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Emergency (999). Call 999 for mental health crisis when: immediate risk to life (suicide intent with plan/means, or serious attempt); significant self-harm (e.g. ligature, major bleed); overdose or poisoning; risk to others (homicidal intent, severe agitation with violence); psychosis with danger to self/others; catatonia; severe self-neglect with physical risk; child/vulnerable adult safeguarding emergency. Do not leave at risk; do not delay. NICE NG10, CKS Mental health. Crisis: 111 option 2, Samaritans 116 123.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 2. SAME DAY / URGENT? Cannot wait 24–48 h – crisis assessment needed.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day mental health assessment. Refer to crisis team (or equivalent per local policy); or same-day GP/UTC if crisis team not available and risk manageable short-term. Use when: suicidal ideation without immediate plan/means but needs risk assessment; self-harm needing assessment; deterioration in psychosis or mood; safeguarding concern; need for crisis medication review or admission decision. Do not leave without safety plan and crisis contact (111, crisis number). NICE NG10, CKS Mental health, Urgent care.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 3. 24–48 H / ROUTINE? Stable but needs follow-up.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: GP or mental health follow-up within 24–48 h. Use when: recent crisis now stabilised with safety plan; medication review; non-urgent referral to CMHT or IAPT. Safety-net: advise crisis numbers (111 option 2, Samaritans 116 123); reattend or 999 if risk escalates. NICE CKS Mental health.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Only if not in crisis – low-risk presentation with support in place. Advice: crisis numbers (111 option 2, Samaritans 116 123); when to reattend (worsening mood, suicidal thoughts, self-harm). Provide written safety-net. Follow up with GP if no improvement. For true crisis, same-day assessment is usually required. NICE CKS Mental health.

options.label: No
options.guidance: Reassess using questions above. If in crisis, arrange same-day/urgent mental health assessment. NICE NG10, CKS Mental health.

options.label: Red Flags (Cauda Equina / Malignancy)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Saddle anaesthesia, bladder/bowel dysfunction, bilateral sciatica, night pain, weight loss, history of cancer. Urgent same-day referral/A&E. NICE NG59.

options.label: Stable / Spondylosis
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Keep active. NSAIDs (regular) for flare. Physiotherapy referral. Avoid imaging in non-specific low back pain. Reassure if no neurology. NICE NG59.

options.label: Early Pregnancy Complications (<13w)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (RCOG Greentop):
1. Presentation: Pain and/or bleeding. Referral: EPAU (Early Pregnancy Assessment Unit).
2. Ectopic Risk: If pain/bleeding + tenderness/adnexal mass → Immediate hospital referral.
3. Recurrent Miscarriage (≥3 consecutive): Refer for specialist workup (Antiphospholipid, genetics). RCOG GTG 17.

options.label: Routine Antenatal Care
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Supplements: Folic Acid 400mcg (5mg if high risk/BMI>30) + Vit D 10mcg.
2. Screening: Book by 10w. Offer 12w (dating/NT) and 20w (anomaly) scans.
3. Aspirin: 75-150mg OD from 12w if ≥1 high risk (HTN, CKD, SLE) or ≥2 moderate risks (BMI, Multi-preg, Age>40). NICE NG201.

options.label: Fever + non-blanching rash
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Treat as meningococcal disease until proved otherwise. Immediate parenteral antibiotic (ceftriaxone or benzylpenicillin). Emergency admission. NICE NG51.

options.label: No fever, well child
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
Consider ITP, HSP. FBC, clotting. Refer paediatrics if unwell or platelets <20. NICE CKS.

options.label: Risk Assessment (RCPsych)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Immediate: Assess method, intent, and access to means. 
2. Safety Planning: Identify warning signs, coping strategies (e.g., grounding), and 'Safe People'. Provide 24/7 Crisis numbers (988 / 111 / Local Crisis Team).
3. Referral: Emergency department if lethal act or active intent. Community Mental Health Team (CMHT) for persistent self-harm. NICE NG225.

options.label: Suspected TIA (<24h resolution)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN (Consultant Plan):
1. Antiplatelet: Aspirin 300mg stat (unless bleeding suspected).
2. Triage: Urgent referral to TIA clinic (assessment within 24h).
3. Driving: Mandatory 1-month ban from driving (inform DVLA). RCP/NICE.

options.label: Acute Stroke (Persistent)
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Emergency: 999 for Hyperacute Stroke Unit (HASU).
2. Action: Nil-by-mouth (swallow screen). No Aspirin until CT brain excludes haemorrhage.

options.label: Antiplatelet & Statins
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. 1st-line: Clopidogrel 75mg OD gold standard.
2. Statin: Atorvastatin 80mg (Target LDL < 1.8).
3. AF: Anticoagulate (DOAC) if AF confirmed. RCP Stroke Guidelines.

options.label: Management & referral
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Exclude torsion (urgent surgical referral). USS if mass or uncertainty. Hydrocele: refer if symptomatic or diagnostic uncertainty. Varicocele: refer if symptomatic or size concern.
2. 2WW: testicular mass. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Symptomatic relief
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Identify cause (GI, drugs, vestibular, metabolic, CNS). Cyclizine 50 mg tds or prochlorperazine 5 mg tds; metoclopramide 10 mg tds (avoid if young or parkinsonism).
2. Red flags: Headache, abdominal pain, dehydration – assess and refer as needed. NICE CKS.

options.label: When to refer / red flags
options.guidance:
MANAGEMENT PLAN:
1. Admit: Severe dehydration, suspected bowel obstruction, head injury, raised ICP. 2WW: Unexplained persistent nausea/vomiting with weight loss.
2. Pregnancy: Exclude hyperemesis; treat and refer if severe. NICE NG12, CKS.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Emergency (999). Apply direct pressure; manage ABC. Do not delay. NICE CKS, Urgent care.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 2. Uncontrolled bleeding, arterial spurting, or major vessel injury?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day urgent / 999 depending on control. Direct pressure; consider tourniquet if limb and life-threatening. Urgent care / A&E. NICE CKS.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day / urgent assessment. Wound swab; consider prophylaxis (co-amoxiclav or doxycycline + metronidazole). Rabies risk if abroad. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 4. High-risk wound (deep, tendon/nerve/vessel/joint concern, face/hand, infected, immunosuppressed, or contaminated)?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Same-day or 24–48 h GP/UTC. Assess for infection (NG51 if sepsis suspected); consider imaging or referral. NICE CKS, NICE NG51, Local formulary.

options.label: No
options.guidance: No – proceed to next question below.

steps.question: 5. Clean, minor wound suitable for self-care?

options.label: Yes
options.guidance: DISPOSITION: Self-care. Advice on wound care, tetanus status, when to reattend (spreading redness, fever, pus, worsening pain). Provide written or verbal safety-net. Follow up with GP if no improvement in defined period. NICE CKS, Local formulary.

options.label: No
options.guidance: Reassess using questions above or arrange same-day/24–48 h review. NICE CKS, Urgent care.
